# Test Writing Guide

## Framework

- Bun Test (`bun:test`) — `describe`, `test`, `expect`, `beforeEach`
- Run all tests: `bun test`
- Run one file: `bun test <file>`
- Run `bun test` only from a directory whose `bunfig.toml` loads the host-safety preload guard: the repository root, `tests/` or `tests/integration/`. Bun reads only the `bunfig.toml` in the directory `bun test` starts in (it does not search upward). The repository root and every directory holding a test file have one whose first `[test]` `preload` entry names the guard, which loads before any test file and any other preload (see Host safety under Isolation). Started in a directory with no `bunfig.toml` (outside the repository, or one holding no test file, such as `src/`), the run has no guard. Start every run with its own scratch HOME, outside your home directory, and `SLACK_STATE_DIR` under it, as `tests/README.md` shows: the guard refuses to start (exit 78) when the home the run was launched with could reach the operator's real state (see The launch-home refusal under Host safety)
- A test or hook whose cost is child-process launches must fit Bun's default 5 s timeout (no `bunfig.toml` sets one). A launch costs about 30 ms on a slow host, so a bash harness that loops through `cat`, `awk`, stub scripts or command substitutions can take seconds. A timeout that bounds a possible hang is a different case: it follows the FIFO rule under Credentials Fixtures and Leak Checks
  - Cut launches first: stub with bash functions and builtins, share one run among cases with identical input in a `beforeAll`, run independent runs concurrently with `Bun.spawn` (its `env` still a direct `hostSafeChildEnv` call; see Host safety under Isolation), and give each slow leg its own test
  - Only a case that still needs more after that gets a per-test or hook timeout as a backstop: a named constant sized to the measured cost with margin, with a comment naming the host cost. It sits above any child's own time limit plus any wait for its output after a kill, so that limit ends a stuck child and the test fails on its own assertions
  - `tests/publish-promote-sr61-poll-window.test.ts` and the test-26 describe in `tests/test-timer-overrides.test.ts` are the reference
- When stdout is not a TTY (piped, or run by an agent), Bun prints only failing test titles. To see the passing titles, such as a `test.each` matrix's rows, run it in a TTY or add `--reporter=junit --reporter-outfile=<path>`

`tests/thread-memory.test.ts` retains `SR8_POPULATIONS` (0/10,000/100,000 joins per persona), exact all/oldest-join and no-eviction checks through reopen, compaction and scans. Its per-persona seed hooks use `POPULATION_SEED_TIMEOUT_MS` and its population cases use `POPULATION_CASE_TIMEOUT_MS`, both 30 s: focused 100k cases took 1.3–2.6 s and prior seeds about 3 s per persona, leaving at least 10× headroom for host load.

These named timeouts protect against hangs; [Thread Memory performance runs](#thread-memory-performance-runs) supply the product cost verdicts. Upgrade fixture children use `UPGRADE_CHILD_TIMEOUT_MS` (10 s), with `UPGRADE_WRITE_CASE_TIMEOUT_MS` allowing two sequential children plus 5 s and `UPGRADE_ENTRY_CASE_TIMEOUT_MS` allowing one plus 5 s for termination, output and cleanup.

### Delivery model verification

Current delivery tests cover AD `pending`/`ended`/`missing` transitions and `session_id` changes as relaunch evidence, shared first-waiting callbacks, readiness without a settle timer, and reading older journals while new records omit synthetic launch metadata. Reconnect cases require fresh AD `waiting` at admission, before text and before Enter.

Receipt-discovery regressions in `tests/delivery-engine.test.ts` cover late AD path publication, a changed reference after resume, and a provisional Claude reference healed by the production shared sweep through the isolated delivery client. They also cover sweep memoization, refusal and teardown before the fresh row read. The receipt audit can bind a pathless attempt to a later `delivery-transcript-reference` diagnostic; receipt and notice suites test its persona/instance/session/path binding and redaction.

The delivery model uses AD row transitions and `session_id` for relaunch observations. Replay rejects synthetic launch and settle metadata, covers same-session resumes and changed sessions, and requires the original production FIFO policy to pass before the reversed-order mutant fails. The [model README](../spec/tla/README.md) describes the current scope, evidence checks and reproduction commands. Local proof does not establish scheduler certification or a `/ci` verdict.

Held-notice retries: one in flight at a time; no client at retry time waits again with no line and no Slack call; a throwing persona or client lookup waits the current backoff step with one line per run of throws, which keeps the thrown message redacted; a persona no longer applied drops its notices with one line. Payload errors and a refused `dm` destination open no episode. Isolation: one persona's episode never delays, holds or logs for another. Secrecy: a code that is not a short identifier is logged as `unknown_error`. A destination changed in place during an open episode (`permission_prompts` moved): a failure at a destination the episode has not named logs exactly one more opening line naming it, and never again for that destination (a failure back at one already named logs nothing); a stale failure at the new destination logs nothing and moves nothing; the backoff is not reset; the cleared line names the destination the successful post went to, with the latest named cause, and no line names that destination as failing when it never failed. In open mode, an inaccessible destination channel entered by a held notice or re-derived prompt uses the same `permission_prompts` diagnostic and retry behavior as strict mode. Confirmed posts survive observer/settle/logger faults without reposting, losing their FIFO successors or leaving the retry gate held; pending ready waits create no duplicate attempts or timers. |

The version is written once, as this file's `TOML_PARSER_PIN`. Both bun.lock cases read through `lockPin`, the file's bun.lock pin reader: for a package it gives the root workspace's spec, the root workspace's non-runtime sections naming it, and its `packages` entry's id, ref (the text after `<name>@`), registry and integrity. The agent-director pin, hermetic: `clientPinVerdict(spec)` accepts only the exact released `CI_AD_CLIENT_VERSION` from the central versions helper; it rejects ranges, floating tags, prerelease/build metadata, file/link/git/URL sources, the host floor and older/newer client releases with their specific rule. Package and root-workspace dependencies must use that approved client in runtime dependencies only; their specs must agree, and the lock resolution must be `agent-director@<approved-client>` from the default registry with SHA-512 integrity. Independent SemVer coverage requires the actual client dependency to meet `PHASE1_FLOOR_VERSION`; meeting the floor never substitutes for exact-pin equality. Lock-reader controls retain workspace/resolution mismatch, duplicate dependency placement, prerelease, file-source and missing-entry checks. ### Agent-director call-budget checks

The startup sweep makes one service-filtered `list` and one `get` per applied persona's own `cscb_<key>` row, live or finished, before its latch/cwd verdict. A stray gets one `get` just before its kill when a hold needs its directory. Kept pre-persona rows and strays swept without holds get none. `tests/session-manager.test.ts` checks Light Row inputs, exact read counts/order, missing-data safety, directory/session use and old-life holds. Unconfigured own-ID verdicts and retired-entry clears need only light facts; note-only logs cause no read. The sweep finishes before Slack connects, outside test-32's measured windows; changes still run test-32 and every integration script whose call assertions they affect. `tests/fmk-source-audit.test.ts` rejects raw `ListRow` use or dropped keys in the sweep's narrowed projection and inferred dropped-field reads from list results, with planted indexed/aliased/iterated list violations and a legal get-result control.

Any change to when CSCB calls agent-director must run Test 32 for SR-8 N3,
as required by the [engineering rule](engineering-guide.md#layering-agent-director-owns-tmux).
Use the additional checks below for the affected paths. Script names are
relative to `tests/integration/`; run them through Docker CI as described
under [Integration scripts run only in docker CI](#integration-scripts-run-only-in-docker-ci).

## Isolation

Tests never touch the real home or a real install.

- **Temp directories only.** Every file a test reads or writes (config, credentials, state directory, crontable, logs, working directories, agent-director store) sits under the test's own `mkdtempSync` directory, passed explicitly, and removed in `afterEach`.
- **agent-director's settings file.** A test writes `config.toml` only through `writeAgentDirectorConfig` (`tests/test-helpers/ad-settings.ts`) under a temp HOME, never as a hand-written TOML literal and never under the real `~/.config/agent-director`, and reads it through a reader whose home getter answers that HOME. It takes every settings value (defaults, minimums, key names, the path, refused forms) from `src/ad-settings.ts` or the helper, never typed; the specified numbers appear only in the pin table of `tests/ad-settings.test.ts`.
- **Never the real home.** No test reads or writes `~/.claude`, `~/.claude/channels/slack`, `~/.config/claude-slack-channel-bots`, `~/.config/agent-director` or `~/.npm`, and no path in a fixture resolves to them. Code that falls back to `os.homedir()` is tested through `runInFakeHome` (see Credentials Fixtures and Leak Checks); code that takes a home or `SLACK_STATE_DIR` gets a temp one. `runPostinstall` falls back to the OS home (and so the real `~/.claude/skills`, which a case with `linkSkills: true` or an installed-copy `packageDir` writes) when `homeDir` is unset, so `tests/postinstall.test.ts` calls it only through its `postinstall()` wrapper, which refuses options without `homeDir`, with paths from `makeSandbox()` (home, state dir and MCP path under one `mkdtempSync` root).
- **The retired-key record.** A test writes `retired-keys.json` only through `writeRetiredKeysRecord` (`tests/test-helpers/retired-keys.ts`), in its own `mkdtempSync` state directory passed explicitly, never in the real state directory (`~/.config/claude-slack-channel-bots`); a store under test is loaded over that directory, and a test that reaches `recordStartupError` points its `logDir` (or `SLACK_STATE_DIR`) at the test's own directory.
- **Shared channel state.** Build applied choices through `writeChannelDeliveryRecord` (`tests/test-helpers/channel-delivery.ts`) or `initialSharedState` and `writeSharedState` (`shared-channels.ts`), in the caller’s `mkdtempSync` directory. Both use the sole `config.json.last-applied` envelope. Invalid-state tests derive malformed bytes from a valid serialized envelope; reload tests use their harness’s byte-writing seam. No fixture writes the real state directory.
- **No real server or CLI.** No test calls `main()`, runs `src/server.ts` or `src/cli.ts` as an entry point, or starts a real daemon in-process. The one exception is the usage-text tests in `tests/cli.test.ts` (`unknown subcommand`, and the two `credentials` cases that stop before the script: a usage error and an unknown persona), which run `src/cli.ts` in a child process through the file's `runCli` helper. `runCli` starts Bun by absolute path (`process.execPath`) with its `env` a direct `hostSafeChildEnv` call (see `host-safe-env.ts` below): the temp HOME, no tool, so `PATH` is `EMPTY_CHILD_PATH` and names no directory, its own `TMUX_TMPDIR`, and as extras `SLACK_STATE_DIR` and the fixed `BUN_RUNTIME_TRANSPILER_CACHE_PATH=0`, so Bun writes no transpiler cache under the temp HOME for a tree snapshot to see. Nothing else comes from `process.env`. It has a 15 s time limit and checks that the child spawned and was not killed by it. These cases never reach a subcommand that acts. A new test that spawns the CLI uses `runCli`. The CLI is otherwise tested through `createCli` with injected `CliDeps`; `server.ts` through its importable modules (see Importing server.ts).
- **Inject the `claude_config_dir` check.** The bring-up controller's default `checkConfigDir` resolves an unset `claude_config_dir` against the real OS home's `.claude`, so a dangling real `~/.claude` would hold every persona. Every controller a test builds injects `checkConfigDir`: `checkPersonaConfigDir(persona, { home })` over a scratch home holding a real `.claude` (the `configDirCheckUnder(base)` helpers in `tests/persona-lifecycle.test.ts`, `tests/registry.test.ts`, `tests/health-check.test.ts` and `tests/persona-relaunch-gate.test.ts`; `tests/persona-connections.test.ts`; the reload harness without a real launch), or `checkLaunchConfigDir` where the suite already set the session manager's spawn home (`tests/session-manager.test.ts`, `tests/restart.test.ts`, `tests/persona-bringup.test.ts`, the reload harness with a real launch). `tests/session-manager.test.ts` sets a scratch default spawn home (`_setSpawnHomeDir` over a `default-home` fixture holding a real `.claude`) in `beforeEach`, so no launch resolves against the process home; a test that needs its own replaces it with `useSpawnHome`.
- **CLI log seams.** `openLogAppend`, `closeFd` and `initLogging` are `CliDeps`, so CLI tests inject fakes: no real descriptor is opened and `console` is never taken over. To see which lines reach the log and which the terminal, inject an `initLogging` that swaps `console.error` for a recorder and restore it afterwards. The agent-director calls are built by the exported `createDirectorOps(getClient)`; test it by passing a stub client, not by installing a Client singleton.
- **Fake tokens only.** See the rules under Credentials Fixtures and Leak Checks.

### Host safety

Host `bun test` never executes a real agent-director binary. The client's discovery (`Client.create()`, `resolveSystemBinary()`) finds the host's real install on `PATH` or at the standard install path under `~/.config/agent-director`, and a real client opens its store. Redirecting HOME alone moves neither: `PATH` still names the install, and `src/` code that calls `os.homedir()` still sees the launch-time home. So the preload guard first refuses to start under a launch-time home that could reach the operator's real Claude, Slack or agent-director state, and only then redirects the environment.

**Fake-executable exception (`tests/child-env.test.ts`).** Its bundled-library end-to-end cases run a time-limited Bun child with a direct `hostSafeChildEnv` call, scratch HOME/state/cwd and no PATH tools. Inside that child only, it creates an inert `agent-director` executable, sets PATH to its scratch directory and imports the pinned npm client by absolute path. The fake answers discovery and `list` with canned JSON and records only environment names.

Fake Slack credentials and the daemon marker are injected after discovery: the control proves the verb inherits them, while the scrubbed run removes them and keeps fake `GH_TOKEN`. The test process imports no client value, changes no PATH and widens no preload setting. This is the sole fake-executable exception to the stub-only client and scratch-PATH rules below; no real binary, tmux, agent or store is reached.

- **No unit test executes a real agent-director binary.** Apart from the fake-executable exception above, every unit test gets its client from the stub, and the preload guard (below) makes a test that forgets it fail as not found instead of reaching the host's install.
- **Everything that spawns runs only in the images.** A test that runs a real agent-director binary (the release's, its agent-director-admin, 0.10.0's or any other), starts a tmux server or session, launches a worker (a real `spawn`, reuse or `resume`) or edits an agent-director store with `sqlite3` is a `/ci` scenario (`tests/integration/test-*.sh`, see Integration scripts run only in docker CI), a contained real-agent heavy scenario (`tests/real-agent/`) or a `/ci-live` check (`ci-live/checks/`), never a `bun test` file, and refuses to run outside its image (`/etc/cscb-ci-image`, see `tests/README.md`, Image marker).
- **Real-binary exception: `/ci-live`'s HOST check.** The `/ci-live` runner's host snapshot (`snapshotHost`, `ci-live/lib/host-state.ts`), taken on the host before and after each run, makes two read-only probes there: the host's installed agent-director's `list` of its `service=cscb` rows (`agent-director --store-path <HOME>/.config/agent-director/state.db list --label service=cscb`) and `tmux ls -F '#{session_name}'`. It never runs a binary the images install. Nothing else on the host, in any test, runs a real agent-director binary or touches the host's tmux server or `state.db`; `tests/ci-live-docker.test.ts` and `tests/ci-live-checks.test.ts` pin those two argv as the only host-side ones.
- **The images' agent-director binaries stay in the images.** The release's binary, its agent-director-admin and its `install.sh` are installed and run only inside the `/ci` and `/ci-live` images (`docker/README.md`), as an AD candidate's and reference's are only inside the AD release gate's job image. None of them enters a development tree, is installed globally or in a production CSCB install, or runs on the host; a development tree holds only the npm client at `package.json`'s exact pin.
- **Dependencies are installed with scripts disabled.** Install a development tree's dependencies with `bun install --ignore-scripts`, so CSCB's own `postinstall` never runs against the real HOME (`tests/README.md`, Running the unit suite).
- **Every client is a stub, apart from the fake-executable exception above.** A test that needs an agent-director client gets it from `tests/test-helpers/agent-director-stub.ts`: a `makeStubClient()` installed with `setClientForTests`, or a seam filled with `makeStubCreateClient(...)` (the start gate's `createClient`) or `makeStubResolveSystemBinary(...)`. `makeCloseCountingStubClient(opts?)` gives a `makeStubClient(opts)` stub whose `close()` only counts its calls (`{ client, closes() }`), for a case that checks which client was closed and how often; `makePassingGateDeps(overrides?)` gives the start gate's seams for a run that passes every step (a default `makeStubCreateClient()`, the three API-surface probes passing, an ENOENT state.db stat, UID 1000, a swallowing startup-error recorder and an `exit` that throws), with `overrides` winning over every default. `makeStubClient`'s default `binaryVersion` is `PHASE1_RC_VERSION` (from `tests/test-helpers/agent-director-versions.ts`), which passes CSCB's Phase 1 floor; a test that needs an older or development binary sets `binaryVersion` explicitly, taking the value from that helper. `tests/install-check.test.ts` passes `runInstallCheck` a `makeStubResolveSystemBinary(...)` resolver, and `tests/postinstall.test.ts` passes the probe an injected install check answering canned results; neither mocks `agent-director`.
- **No value import of `Client` or `resolveSystemBinary`.** No test file or test helper holds either as a value from `agent-director`: no named import or re-export (aliased or not), no `export *`, and no read through the module namespace (a property or element read, destructuring, a spread or rest copy, a default or `require` binding, a dynamic `import()`). There is no exception, not even inside `expect(...)`: an identity assertion on `ad.resolveSystemBinary` is a read. Type-only imports (`import type`, an inline `type`) are allowed, and so is spreading the namespace, or a copy of it, into a `mock.module` factory (`{ ...REAL, resolveSystemBinary: stub }`) or comparing a copy with the live namespace entry by entry (see Module Mocks).
- **Every child's `env` is a direct `hostSafeChildEnv` call.** Every child-process call in a test file or test helper (the `child_process` functions, `fork` included, however imported; `Bun.spawn`, `Bun.spawnSync` and `$`) passes an options object literal with exactly one `env`, and that `env` is a direct call of `hostSafeChildEnv` imported from `host-safe-env.ts` (see the helper list under Factory Functions). A `Bun.$` template ends in `.env(hostSafeChildEnv(...))`. A child-process function referenced without being called (put in a deps object, re-exported) is refused: the audit can't follow it.
- **The preload guard.** The `[test]` preload of the repository root's `bunfig.toml` and of the `bunfig.toml` in every directory holding a test file (`tests/bunfig.toml`, `tests/integration/bunfig.toml`) loads `tests/test-helpers/host-safety-preload.ts` once, before any test file, when `bun test` starts in one of those directories. Bun reads only the `bunfig.toml` in the directory the run starts in (no upward search) and resolves a relative preload path against that directory, so each file names the guard relative to its own directory, and every entry starts with `./`, `../` or `/` (a bare `a/b.ts` is looked up as a package). The guard is the first `[test]` `preload` entry: Bun loads the entries in order, so an entry before it would run before the refusal. Entries after it are allowed. A new directory of test files gets its own `bunfig.toml` naming the guard the same way. A run started in a directory with no `bunfig.toml` (outside the repository, or one holding no test file, such as `src/`) has no guard. Its first action is the launch-home refusal (next item); a run it accepts goes on. The guard then computes its variables with `preloadRedirectedEnv(process.env, home, tmuxTmpDir)` from `host-safe-env.ts`, which is pure, and applies them to `process.env`: each of `PRELOAD_ENV_NAMES` is set or deleted, nothing else is touched. Its only writes to disk are the new HOME directory and, when the run inherited no valid one, the `TMUX_TMPDIR` directory, both directly under the OS temp directory (`osTempDir()`, the normalized `os.tmpdir()`, so a `TMPDIR` such as `/tmp//` names the same directory as `/tmp`); a refused run makes neither:
  - `HOME`: a new, empty directory directly under the OS temp directory, named with `PRELOAD_HOME_PREFIX`. Every test file shares it; it is never removed, so each run leaves one.
  - `PATH`: the inherited absolute entries, in order, duplicates dropped, without every directory that holds an `agent-director` entry; `EMPTY_CHILD_PATH` when none is left.
  - `TMUX`, `TMUX_PANE` and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`: unset. `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` names a Claude configuration directory (a run started from a bot's session inherits its persona's), which Claude Code, a hook or any code honouring it would read and write. `TMUX_TMPDIR`: the process's one fenced directory from `childTmuxTmpDir()` (the inherited one when valid, else a new one), the same one `hostSafeChildEnv` hands every child, so a run makes at most one. It is never removed.
  - `SLACK_STATE_DIR`: `<new HOME>/.config/claude-slack-channel-bots` (`PRELOAD_STATE_DIR_PATH`, the server's default state directory since; not created). It is set rather than unset because the state-directory resolvers fall back to `os.homedir()`.
  - `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`: `<new HOME>/.config` (`XDG_CONFIG_DIR`, not created). The server's default state directory, and the crontable in it, with `SLACK_STATE_DIR` unset is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/claude-slack-channel-bots`: an inherited value (the operator's own `~/.config`, say) would put it in the real home, and unset, empty or relative, `resolveXdgConfigHome` falls back to `os.homedir()`.

  It then runs `preloadCheckFailures(process.env)`, the one check shared with `tests/host-safety.test.ts`, and throws, failing the run before any test file loads, when it reports anything. The message names the failed checks by their `PRELOAD_CHECK` labels (a `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` still set, empty included, is `claude-config-dir-set`; an `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` unset or empty is `xdg-config-home-unset`, and one that is relative or not strictly under HOME is `xdg-config-home-not-under-home`) and HOME, never the environment. No file imports the guard. With the guard in place, a test that forgot its stub fails as not found (`ErrSystemInstallNotFound`, the class label `AD_SYSTEM_INSTALL_NOT_FOUND` exported from `src/install-check.ts`) instead of reaching the host's install.
- **The launch-home refusal.** Bun fixes `os.homedir()` and `os.userInfo().homedir` at start-up from the HOME the run was launched with, and the guard cannot move them. So, as its first action, before it makes a directory or changes the environment, the guard checks each launch-time home (`launchTimeHomes()`: both values, duplicates dropped) with `launchHomeRefusal(launchHome, passwdHome(), LIVE_LAUNCH_HOME_PROBE)` from `host-safe-env.ts`. Nothing runs before that check: every module a file loads runs its top-level code before the file's first statement, so the guard loads only `node:` builtins and `./host-safe-env.ts`, and `host-safe-env.ts` only `node:` builtins (no `src/` module, package or other test helper, not even for a type). The decision is pure: its only reads are the probe's (a `LaunchHomeProbe`): `exists` (an `lstat`; a dangling symlink, or an entry that cannot be looked at, counts as present), `canonical` (the path made absolute with every symlink on it followed as far as it exists: the real path of its deepest existing part, a dangling symlink followed to its target, the rest appended, so it names the entry a write to the path would reach) and `tempDir` (`osTempDir()`). Below, a path "resolves" to its `canonical` form. The first rule that applies wins, each with its `LAUNCH_HOME_REFUSAL` label:
  - `launch-home-not-absolute`: the home is empty or a relative path.
  - `launch-home-in-real-home` (passwd home known): the home is the account's passwd home or lies under it, compared by path text first (nothing is probed for a home that matches) and then with both resolved.
  - `launch-home-temp-dir-is-root` (no passwd home): the OS temp directory resolves to the file system root (`/`). Every absolute path lies under the root, so the temp-directory rules would accept any home. Nothing about the home is probed.
  - `launch-home-not-under-temp-dir` (no passwd home): the home does not resolve strictly under the OS temp directory (resolved too); the temp directory itself is refused.
  - `launch-home-holds-slack-state`: anything exists at `<home>/.config/claude-slack-channel-bots` (`PRELOAD_STATE_DIR_PATH`, the server's default state directory), at `<home>/.config/cscb` (`LEGACY_XDG_STATE_DIR_PATH`, its default in 0.14.0 and 0.15.0) or at `<home>/.claude/channels/slack` (`LEGACY_STATE_DIR_PATH`, its default before); both are in `DEFAULT_STATE_DIR_PATHS`.
  - `launch-home-derived-path-in-real-home` (passwd home known): a path in `LAUNCH_HOME_DERIVED_PATHS` under the home resolves to the passwd home (as given or resolved) or a path under it. These are the paths `src/` and the agent-director client derive from `homedir()`: `.claude`, `.claude/channels/slack`, `.claude/projects`, `.claude/skills`, `.claude/slack-mcp.json`, `.config/agent-director`, `.config/agent-director/state.db`, `.config/agent-director/config.toml`, `.config/agent-director/bin/agent-director`, and `.config`, `.config/claude-slack-channel-bots` and `.config/claude-slack-channel-bots/crontab` (the server's default state directory with `SLACK_STATE_DIR` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` unset, and the crontable in it, which the server's start creates and into which it moves the old default's files; bugs). `.claude/channels/slack` (`LEGACY_STATE_DIR_PATH`) stays in the list because the CLI still reads it until the server has moved it.
  - `launch-home-derived-path-not-under-temp-dir` (no passwd home): a path in `LAUNCH_HOME_DERIVED_PATHS` under the home does not resolve strictly under the OS temp directory.
  - `launch-home-holds-agent-director`: the home holds `.config/agent-director` or an entry at the standard install path.

  `passwdHome()` reads `/etc/passwd` with `passwdHomeFrom`: the first line whose uid field equals the user's uid exactly decides, and a later line for the same uid is never used. There is no passwd home when the file cannot be read, when no line has the uid (as for an account served by LDAP), or when that first line is malformed (fewer than seven fields, or an empty or relative home); `launchHomeRefusal` also takes a relative or empty passwd home as none. With no passwd home the real home is unknown, so the guard fails closed: the temp directory must not resolve to the root, the two temp-directory rules take the real-home rules' places, and the home and every derived path must resolve strictly under the OS temp directory. The root is the only ancestor of a home refused as the temp directory: with no passwd home and the temp directory set to another one (`TMPDIR=/home`, say), a home under it, the real one included, passes the temp-directory rules unless a derived path resolves out of that directory, and is then refused only by `launch-home-holds-slack-state` or `launch-home-holds-agent-director`. On a refusal the guard writes one line to stderr, `launchHomeRefusalMessage(reason, launchHome)`: `host-safety preload: refusing to start: <label> (launch-time home "<path>")` and a pointer to `tests/README.md`, never the environment. It then exits with `LAUNCH_HOME_REFUSED_EXIT_CODE` (78, sysexits' `EX_CONFIG`), so a refusal is told apart from a failing test (exit 1). No test file loads and no directory is made. For a home the guard accepts, no path in `LAUNCH_HOME_DERIVED_PATHS` resolves into the real home (with no passwd home, each resolves strictly under the OS temp directory, which is not the root), and nothing exists at its Slack state directory or agent-director install paths. When `src/` derives another path from `homedir()`, add it to `LAUNCH_HOME_DERIVED_PATHS` and to `LINKABLE_DERIVED_PATHS` in `tests/launch-home-guard.test.ts`, which writes the list out so that a path dropped from the helper fails its row.
- **HOME under the preload.** The preload moves only what reads the environment (the client's discovery, the `SLACK_STATE_DIR` resolvers, the crontable's default through `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`). `src/` code that calls `homedir()` directly still answers the launch-time home that the refusal accepted: the start gate's `state.db` path, the state-directory resolvers' fallback with `SLACK_STATE_DIR` unset, the crontable's default with `SLACK_STATE_DIR` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` unset, the Claude config-directory default, the default transcript root and `~` expansion. So every run starts with its own scratch HOME outside the real home (`tests/README.md`; `/publish`'s preflight starts its run the same way), and code that falls back to `os.homedir()` is tested through `runInFakeHome`. Don't patch `os.homedir()` in the preload instead: a patched property misses a named import, and a process-wide `mock.module('node:os')` is the top-level mock that Module Mocks forbids.
- **What a test may change.** A test never widens what the guard set: it never sets HOME, `TMUX` or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` process-wide and never puts back a `PATH` directory the guard removed. It leaves `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` as the guard set it: a test that needs another value, or needs `SLACK_STATE_DIR` unset for the crontable's default, passes `resolveDefaultCronTablePath`, `resolveXdgConfigHome` or the loader (`ResolvePersonaConfigOptions.env`) an explicit environment object and its own temp home instead, never a copy of `process.env`, as `tests/config-cron.test.ts` does. It may narrow `PATH` (a subset of the guard's entries, or a scratch directory of the test's own that holds no `agent-director`) and set `TMUX_TMPDIR` and `SLACK_STATE_DIR`, and restores each to the guard's value in `afterEach`, as `tests/legacy-reply-hook-cleanup.test.ts` (`PATH`, `SLACK_STATE_DIR`) and `tests/host-safety.test.ts` (`PATH`, `TMUX_TMPDIR`) do (see also Credentials Fixtures and Leak Checks). One exception: a host-safety refusal test may point `PATH` at a fixture directory of its own that holds a plain, non-executable `agent-director` file, to prove the refusal, and restores `PATH` in `afterEach`. `tests/host-safety.test.ts`'s "a tool's own PATH directory holds an agent-director file" row is the one such case.
- **Enforcement.** `tests/host-safety.test.ts` audits the tree with the TypeScript parser, so text in strings, comments, templates and regex literals never counts: the value-import rule and the child-environment rule over every file `bun test` runs and every test helper; that no file in the repository imports the preload, and that the repository root and every directory holding a test file have a `bunfig.toml` whose first `[test]` preload entry names it with a path entry that resolves to it from that file's directory (a directory with none fails, naming it; an entry before the guard fails, entries after it are allowed); that the preload's first statement after its imports is the launch-home refusal loop over `launchTimeHomes()`, calling `launchHomeRefusal(<home>, passwdHome(), LIVE_LAUNCH_HOME_PROBE)` and, when it gives a reason, ending in `process.exit(LAUNCH_HOME_REFUSED_EXIT_CODE)`, so nothing in the guard runs before the refusal; that the preload loads only `node:` builtins and `./host-safe-env.ts` (`PRELOAD_LOADS`) and `host-safe-env.ts` only `node:` builtins (`HELPER_LOADS`), checked by `guardLoadFindings`, which flags any other static import (side-effect-only and type-only included, so the rule does not depend on what the transpiler drops), `export … from`, `import x = require(…)`, dynamic `import()` or `require()`, and any load whose specifier is not one string literal, because a loaded module's top-level code would run before the refusal; that only the guard's own files (`REAL_HOME_FILES`: `host-safe-env.ts`, the preload, `tests/host-safety.test.ts` and `tests/launch-home-guard.test.ts`) reference `realHome()` or `passwdHome()`, the helpers that answer the real home's path; over `src/` and `scripts/`, the call sites (`Client.create()` only in the startup gate's module, `resolveSystemBinary()` as a value only in the server, the install check and `/publish`'s check). The value-read matcher these audits share with `tests/fmk-source-audit.test.ts` lives in `tests/test-helpers/ad-value-reads.ts` (`agentDirectorValueReads`, `agentDirectorNamespaceArguments`). It then runs the shared `preloadCheckFailures` on the live environment (every name in `PRELOAD_ENV_NAMES`) and, only when that reports nothing, calls `runStartupGate()` and `runInstallCheck()` un-injected: both must fail as not found. `tests/launch-home-guard.test.ts` covers the launch-home refusal: `passwdHomeFrom` over passwd texts; every rule and their order over a recording fake probe, with the passwd home known and unknown, a temp directory resolving to the root, the `/home` temp directory that lets the would-be real home through, and one row per derived path; the live probe over fixtures beside a fake real home, and against the OS temp directory with no passwd home; the guard in a `bun test` child started from each directory with a `bunfig.toml` (the repository root, `tests/` and `tests/integration/`), refused under a fake home holding either default state directory (`.config/claude-slack-channel-bots` or `.claude/channels/slack`) and accepted under an empty one; that this run's `homedir()`-derived defaults resolve outside the passwd home (with no passwd entry, strictly under the OS temp directory); and preflight's scratch HOME. A refusal test launches its child only with a fake home under its own `mkdtempSync` root, never with the real home.
- **Fixing a finding.** Inject the stub, or pass `env: hostSafeChildEnv(...)` directly in the call. When the preload check fails, run `bun test` from a directory whose `bunfig.toml` loads the guard (the repository root, `tests/` or `tests/integration/`), so the guard loads and sets HOME and `PATH` itself; still start with a scratch HOME (`tests/README.md`). When the bunfig audit names a directory, give it a `bunfig.toml` whose first `[test]` preload entry names the guard relative to it. When the load audit flags the guard or `host-safe-env.ts`, write what the guard needs in `host-safe-env.ts` from `node:` builtins instead of importing it. When the guard refuses to start (exit 78, `host-safety preload: refusing to start: <label>`), relaunch with a new, empty scratch HOME outside the real home, made under a `TMPDIR` outside it too (and not `/`), as `tests/README.md` shows. Never loosen an audit or a refusal rule, add an exemption or widen what the preload set to make room.

### Latest-release and uncertain-input regressions

The current base is `cscb-ci-base:v11`: runtime and exact client `0.18.8`,
release commit `f2c9ce525e3c37e41e4884818354ffe8e793c8fb`, with independent
`0.12.0` host floor. The legacy `0.17.0` fixture verifies its own installer.
`ci-live-docker.test.ts` discovers every base consumer, the candidate included,
and preserves stale v9/v10 negative controls. The [strict latest gate](../docker/README.md#strict-latest-agent-director-check)
FAILs lookup/digest/pin/base drift without fallback; latest unit tests inject
all transport and clock effects. `ci-run-lifecycle.test.ts` composes present,
absent, appearing and built bases; `publish-prepare-changelog.test.ts` proves
SR-2.8 stops before mutation. Composed admission also requires distinct release-digest, present-base and client-only-latest failures to write their exact FAIL codes before packing, building or running any shard.

The `ad-input-*` and `ad-submission-*` suites distinguish recorded AD
uncertainty from ordinary in-flight intent. An unresolved queue
`submission-blocked/ad-input-unconfirmed` or per-persona `uncertain` hold
requires receipt-only custody; invalid/unreadable holds fail closed. Ordinary
unrefused `sent` work with no such evidence recovers after reopen through
receipt/AD reads, guarded recovery Enter and retype/backoff, including a
text-to-Enter crash or a restarted retry episode. Plain text/Enter intents
are removed at startup; known `text-ready` keeps its guarded continuation.

Test actual uncertainty writes before reads/notices and restart after that
first durable write, even if the queue block was interrupted. The accepted
window before any successful uncertainty write falls back to normal
receipt-guarded recovery. Fresh-session or observed-finished same-session
launches release custody into those guards, not into a delivered result;
a CSCB-only restart on the same live launch remains held. Preserve exact
late-receipt and release-persistence controls. Use the existing injected
clients, clocks, real queue/hold files and recovery harness; never infer
readiness from pane text.

### Integration scripts run only in docker CI

The integration scripts and real-agent fixtures run inside the Docker CI harness, importing packed production state/receipt adapters. They never classify native terminal text or retain it in diagnostics.

The `cscb-ci-base:v11` runtime is AD 0.18.8, independently pinned from CSCB's
0.18.8 npm client and unchanged 0.12.0 host minimum. Test 42 checks its raw/displayed-state
contract; Test 43 uses a verified off-PATH 0.17.0 fixture in a separate fresh
HOME/store/socket to check legacy normalization. Both use real AD registered
hooks with the stub worker, packed production consumers and a local Slack
stub. Their contract checks exact raw/normalized list fields, measured HTTP
posts against the production trail and shared production persona-up admission.
Success/failure cleanup scans output and every API record's leak metadata before
releasing driver evidence. This evidence does not establish native Claude
behavior. Keep runtime version/commit/hash evidence distinct from client identity
and from historical captures; see
[the image records](../docker/README.md#what-the-base-holds) and
[the scenario assertions](../tests/README.md#version-specific-displayed-state-coverage-biy3).

- Never run them on a dev box or on any host without container support, and never against the real home. If docker is not available, report the integration run as not done; don't run the scripts directly.
- They refuse outside the image. `/etc/cscb-ci-image` exists only in the `cscb-ci` images and the AD release gate's job image (`scripts/ad-gate/template/Dockerfile`), where `/ad-gate` runs a shipped tag's scripts (`docker/README.md`, The AD release gate). `tests/runner.sh` (before it reads its arguments, writes an in-shard file or runs a script), `scenario.sh` (at source time, so every script that sources it), each `test-*.sh` that does not source it (Tests 1 to 4), `fmk-driver.ts`, `stub-mcp-session.ts`, `switch-over.ts` and `fmk-texts.ts` check for it before their first other step and, without it, refuse and say why; `ad-version-stand-in.sh` checks for it before it reads its settings or runs agent-director, and refuses (exit 70) without it or without its settings file. So does every `scenario.sh` step that installs, moves or swaps an agent-director binary or the shim, every harness agent-director call (`ad`, `ad_capture`, `ad_admin`, `ad_admin_capture`) and every harness `sqlite3` read, edit or copy (`ad_store_edit`, `ad_store_id`, `ad_store_backup`, `ad_store_pending_no_launch`) and every stub-worker helper (`stub_mode`, `stub_dialog_delay`, `stub_release`, `stub_press_enter`, `stub_type_exit`, `write_mcp_config`), the store-row read (`ad_store_row`), the Slack stub and stub-session helpers (`slack_stub_push`, `stub_session_deliveries`, `stub_session_call`; `IMAGE_GUARDED_STUB_HELPERS`, each running the check as its first step) and the agent-director settings writer (`write_ad_settings`), through `require_ci_image`. A script that sources `scenario.sh` runs nothing but `set` options and literal assignments before its source line; one that does not starts with its own marker check. `fmk-driver.ts`, `stub-mcp-session.ts`, `switch-over.ts` and `fmk-texts.ts` statically import only `node:` built-ins and load the package under test (the session client the package's MCP SDK, the printer for an entry that needs it also its agent-director client; `switch-over.ts` also the step reader `tests/test-helpers/runbooks.ts` and `markdown.ts`) only after the check. The Slack stub server has no marker check and statically imports only `node:` built-ins.
- The `SCENARIO_ROOT` rule. Every `scenario.sh` function with a step (`sqlite3`, a copy, move or install, an `install.sh` run, a run of agent-director, or a call of a function with one) calls `require_scenario_home` before its first step, except the functions `tests/host-safety.test.ts` lists with why: `HOME_CHECK_EXEMPT` (primitives, setup and shared-mode helpers) and `HOME_CHECKED_BY_CALLERS` (private helpers run only after an audited helper's check, and from no script). A new helper with a step needs the check, or a commented entry in one of those lists. `slack_stub_push`, `stub_session_deliveries` and `stub_session_call` make no step in this sense, so they need neither, and none of them runs `require_scenario_home`, directly or through a function it calls (pinned in `tests/host-safety.test.ts`), so they work in shared mode too. The check refuses unless `SCENARIO_ROOT` is a directory and HOME is under it, as written and by real path. No harness step touches the invoking user's own `~/.config/agent-director`. An fmk script (a `TEST_NAME` carrying `-fmk-`) gets its own HOME, agent-director install and store, and tmux server under `SCENARIO_ROOT`, with the shim in front of the binary; Tests 5 to 12 and Test 29 keep the container's shared HOME and store, with no shim (`tests/README.md`, Scenario helper). The request-only `configuration_request` instead uses the audited `require_scenario_state` after `require_ci_image`, preserving shared/container HOME; see [Operator review integration fixtures](#operator-review-integration-fixtures) for its containment and file-kind contract.
- Their config and credentials files are written inside the container; the scripts never read a config from the host.
- `bun test` does not run them. `tests/integration/session-leader.test.ts` is the one `bun test` file under `tests/integration/`: it spawns only a throwaway child and touches no CSCB state. The Slack stub server has no host unit test of its own: Test 0's once-invoked `slack_stub_record` leg checks its all-files `files.completeUploadExternal` answer, record redaction and captured-output leak safety inside the image. Test 10 exercises it end to end, and Test 29 its push control, with the stub session's delivery record and tool calls.
- `tests/README.md` has the suite's layout, the run order (canonical order: test-1; then test-2, test-3 and test-4, each when present; then every other script by ascending number, so test-0 follows test-4; in each shard, test-1 first, then the shard's assigned scripts in canonical order; see its Script names, prerequisites and canonical order, and Sharding), the helper's contract and how to add a scenario. A new scenario sources the helper, which gives it its own scratch state dir, port and persona-name tag, bounded polling waits and a cleanup trap, and, for an fmk scenario, its own HOME, agent-director install and store, tmux server and shim. `tests/README.md` (Scenario helper, and Rules for every fmk scenario) describes both shims and required closing assertions: the three server-backed assertions for ordinary fmk scripts, or `assert_codex_d1_safety` for the exact six Codex D1 entrypoints.
- `CSCB_SLACK_API_URL` (the Slack API base URL override, honoured only for an `http://127.0.0.1…` or `http://[::1]…` URL) exists for the scenarios alone. The fmk scenarios (Test 0 and Tests 13 to 28) and Tests 10, 12 and 29 set it to point a live start at the Slack stub. A unit test passes an env object to `resolveSlackApiUrlOverride`, or a `slackApiUrl` to the connection manager or the option builders. The one case that sets it in `process.env`, to prove it is not read from there, restores it in `finally`.
- The test-only timer overrides. A scenario that would otherwise wait out a production timer shortens it with the `test_timer_overrides` block of the CSCB `config.json` it writes (`src/test-timer-overrides.ts`; see the architecture doc, Configuration). The block is never written into a user's configuration, and no user doc names it.
  - Writers are Tests 23, 26, 32, 44, all 16 strict/open membership groups (45/48/51–64), and separate heavy Test 101. The [review checklist](test-review-guide.md#fmk-scenarios) names every complete entrypoint; re-audit direct writes and helper callers when adding one. Test 32 uses `lib/real-scenario.sh`/`fixtures/sr8-evidence.ts` to write the production `queue_compact_interval_ms`; Test 44 and `lib/membership-load.sh` use that config writer for their case's compaction interval. Heavy Test 101 uses `delivery_stuck_after_ms`. Recovery 46/65/66/67 writes no overrides. Never shorten a timer whose actual duration the case asserts.
  - Scenario 20 sets `latch_recheck_interval_ms`. Scenario 24 sets `ad_version_recheck_interval_ms` and `dialog_ready_timeout_ms` in every leg, plus the two retry keys in the refused-stopping, refused-grace and call-timeout legs. Set `unavailable_retry_base_s` and `unavailable_retry_ceiling_s` together, ceiling at least base.
  - Write the block in every start's `config.json`. The server reads it once, from the start-time configuration, so a leg that changes the set removes `config.json.last-applied` and restarts.
  - Require the one `TEST TIMER OVERRIDES ACTIVE` line after every start, equal to the printer's line for that set.
  - Never retype a value: print it through `fixtures/fmk-texts.ts`, which gives the effective value for the set the scenario passes. The entries are `testTimerOverridesBlock`, `buildTestTimerOverridesLine`, `effectiveTestTimer`, `adLaunchBoundMs` (B over a written table and, as one more argument, a floor override) and `unavailableRetryDueS` (a retry's due time, over the retry base and ceiling given together).
  - A leg whose assertion depends on a production timer keeps that timer at its default: test-26's stopping leg, where S's first retry must fall due after the stopping window.

### Busy-send integration and candidate AD

Test-32 delivers one DM through the ordinary receipt/FIFO audit and waits for
AD idle before its own pause. Its saved before-pause AD row must report
`transcript_status: present` on both candidate AD and legacy AD 0.18.8;
other values fail immediately with a before-pause transcript message.

The DOWN baseline records prior acceptances, send/delivery counts and a
diagnostic cursor after pause, alongside the shim's `DOWN_MARK`. Exactly 13
new inputs (10 DMs, two interjects, one cron fire) must be accepted while DOWN,
with zero new sends or deliveries, including attempts on the earlier DM.

The acceptance wait and receipt wait after resume count 14 cumulative inputs,
including the pre-pause DM. Test-32 captures AD's row again after resume and
requires the same non-empty native `session_id` and instance before that
receipt wait.

`tests/real-down-pause.test.ts` uses synthetic AD rows and inert shell
stand-ins to pin the pre-pause turn, transcript rejection, interval baseline,
shifted totals and conversation continuity. These controls do not establish
native runtime compatibility.

The real-scenario receipt audit keeps two distinct evidence paths. Legacy
records retain the packed production parser, exact-text matcher and durable
transcript receipt.

Covered records require an unrefused `submitted` intent
for that part and instance, a durable `agent-director:get-delivery` receipt
whose UUID equals its `delivery_request_id`, and matching intent, receipt and
native transcript session IDs. The intent independently binds the native
file's basename and embedded session ID; the delivered record alone cannot
establish ownership.

A main Claude `user` record with
`origin: {kind: 'task-notification', producer: 'session-task'}` qualifies only
after removing the exact documented AD Claude Wait Turn prefix and suffix.
The audit follows AD commit `8e95f63a`'s capability table and
`unwrapClaudeWake`: raw or escaped reserved closing tags, changed wrappers
and ambiguous batches give no evidence. It splits only AD's numbered
`[agent-director: message N of M]` separators with their documented LF gaps,
then compares each whole part byte for byte after its submission.

Batch slots preserve order and cannot be reused; extra exact take-ins still count
as duplicates. Watchdog progress, failure diagnostics and final usage use
the same classification. Production transcript matching stays unchanged.

Host-safe controls in `tests/transcript-receipts.test.ts` cover the retained
13-message shape, a 13-part batch, missing/wrong receipt or take-in evidence,
wrapping changes, session/instance mismatch, duplicates and path separation.
These synthetic controls do not establish that a retained projection with
withheld text matches the documented wrapper; the candidate rerun must prove
that against its native transcript.

Test-32 chooses its fault leg from a fresh AD `get` row's `busy_send` field.
Uncovered launches keep the swallowed text/Enter faults; covered launches
lose one confirmed Wait Turn reply only after the real call runs.

Require a consumed `send_mode=wait_turn` / `unknown-typed` fault bound by PID
to its actual send and pre-existing durable intent. After kill/reconcile and
resume, audit all 34 original inputs and reminders, then require the same
pair's `get-delivery` lookup, one send, no raw-key recovery and no duplicate
take-ins.

The 20 latency samples follow that proof: admission counts run from 34 to 53
and delivery counts from 35 to 54. The pre-pause DM is outside the last 20
timings used by the latency assertion.

Host controls execute the real fault-leg slice and extracted argument matcher
with inert stand-ins only. Full shim execution and native AD custody/recovery
belong to the container candidate rerun.

Normal covered `wait_turn_raced` hand-over logs through the engine's info
callback as a plain line, without constructing an Error or printing a stack.
Blocked and failed deliveries keep the error callback. The engine unit
controls pin both paths.

`tests/integration/test-68-fmk-busy-send.sh` depends on test-1 and runs in
Docker CI. It drives the packed production queue, engine and covered adapter.
On an uncovered runtime it checks real text/Enter transport and transcript
receipts for absent `busy_send`, projected `not_covered`, and safe
`agent_not_covered` fallback only after a fresh `get`. A truly covered native
launch explicitly skips those legacy legs; projecting an uncovered field
cannot change its transport.

Covered held-to-Final, unknown lookup and default-off reconnect checks use
synthetic custody facts through an explicit fixture adapter. They check
submitted-before-send, lookup-only recovery after queue/engine recreation,
no duplicate/raw send, and no automatic pause/resume before E6. Native stub
receipt counts guard against accidental input from synthetic covered cases.
After removing the custody shim's control file, fixture cleanup runs a real
AD `kill` through `cscb_run`, with a shell retained as AD's recorded parent.
This exercises the AD-to-tmux shim chain even when the runtime skips all
legacy sends. The closing assertions still require that positive evidence,
reject direct bot-server tmux calls, finished-row kills and CSCB deletes,
and recheck at exit. `tests/busy-send-closing.test.ts` executes the extracted
cleanup and closing functions with inert recording stand-ins and synthetic
logs; missing tmux evidence, a failed kill and direct server tmux evidence
must fail closure. The full logging shims and native AD-to-tmux chain are
exercised only by the container test-68 rerun.
These checks do not prove E2 client serialization, Claude busy-send transport,
native holds/turn-start confirmation, an OS crash during send, or E6 reconnect.
Those need the matching candidate/client and real Claude; the stub has no
FileChanged/asyncRewake route.

Use `/ci --ad-candidate-dist /absolute/path/to/dist test-68`, or omit SCRIPT
for all scripts against a candidate overlay. Supply a trusted dist with
regular files `agent-director` (real release/prerelease stamp and nonempty
commit) and matching `client.tgz` (npm `package/` root); optional matching
`agent-director-admin` and `install.sh` replace the base versions. Do not use
`0.0.0-dev`. The [CI skill](../.claude/skills/ci/SKILL.md#testing-a-candidate-agent-director-dist)
holds the full input and invocation contract.

The runner selects `docker/Dockerfile.test.candidate` with a read-only
BuildKit named context; the binary and client are installed only in the
disposable test image. Test 1 unpacks the supplied client privately under
CSCB's `node_modules`; package/lock pins stay unchanged. Image records retain
runtime/client versions and hashes. Candidate checks preserve exact tarball,
native errors, binary identity and client minimum-binary checks; shipped-pin
equality is skipped for this overlay, while CSCB's runtime
floor still applies. Optional omitted tools keep their base versions, with
installer capability tracked separately.

Candidate runs always report SELECTIVE/non-gate, with PASS exit 3, even for
all scripts. They do not replace the ordinary full `/ci` gate, whose current
base pins runtime and client 0.18.8, independently of the unchanged 0.12.0
host floor. Record the actual runtime pair rather than assuming a host
installation selects the gate's runtime. Running test-68 against
a candidate still leaves its covered custody cases synthetic.

The shim and controls are TypeScript: `fixtures/agent-director-busy-send.ts`
and `fixtures/busy-send-controls.ts`; no Python fixture is used.
`fixtures/busy-result.ts` builds and validates complete synthetic Results,
including caller/request/instance/session identity, explicit `launch_token`
and `evidence_kind` (nullable), and `wait`; unknown lookup returns `result: null`.
`fixtures/busy-send-consumer-controls.ts` feeds these responses through the
production queue/engine with covered waiting rows that omit both launch fields.
No shim adds a synthetic row launch token; only the hand-over Result sets it.
The controls require a complete Final to finish durably and the old missing-launch-token Final to fail the actual journal
consumer, rather than weakening its validator. They can also use the packed
package via `CSCB_PKG_DIR`; this remains synthetic evidence.

`bun tests/integration/fixtures/busy-send-client-controls.ts [client-package]`
drives the installed pin or an explicit extracted candidate's real subprocess
decoder against an inert executable, then tests refusal fallback/capacity retry
and conditional-pause details through CSCB. It reads the candidate only and
does not prove native-agent transport or enable conditional pause.

Scenario runtime provenance accepts prerelease/build suffixes only when
the release record has boolean `candidate_overlay: true`. Ordinary records
still require a plain release; string `"true"` grants no exception. The shell
controls in `fixtures/ci-candidate-controls.ts` execute `check_ad_runtime`
with an inert executable and retain exact version/commit/digest checks.

### Asynchronous AD recovery assertions

- Before a harness resumes an ended row, wait with a bounded deadline until the old tmux session ID is gone and its pane pid is dead (a zombie counts as dead). AD refuses a resume as "still stopping" while that old life is exiting, even after its row reads `ended`.
- Use the row's recorded session name/socket to capture the live pane pid and unique tmux `#{session_id}` (`$N`) together before sending the exit sentinel. Poll `list-sessions -F '#{session_id}'` on that socket for the exact old ID; a new life reusing its name must not hold this barrier.
- Bound each tmux metadata query to 3 s within the 10 s exit-wait deadline. Only a successful identity list without the old ID, or exit 1 with one of the three gone-server outcomes of tmux 3.2a's client, confirms absence: `no server running on <socket>` (a stale socket file, which the exited server leaves behind), `error connecting to <socket> (No such file or directory)` (no socket file) and `server exited unexpectedly` (the server closed the connection unanswered while exiting). Other connection/command errors, a status 0 with any stderr (tmux 3.2a's "server version is too old for client" exits 0), timeouts and unexpected statuses fail explicitly.
- A failure of the TypeScript barrier (`fixtures/ended-life.ts`, used by test 4's driver and the shared notice fixture) names its cause, never just "old life never exited": the tmux query and exit status with a fixed label for its stderr (for example `connect-error:permission-denied`, never the raw text), a timeout, a process-probe errno, or at the deadline which of the session and process still held. The shared notice fixture records those labels in its audit metadata under the step `old life exit barrier`. Test 24's shell barrier labels its tmux query failures the same way; its deadline failure stays the generic "old life never exited".
- Test 4 proves the window with the stub's `slow-exit` mode and checks both the unchanged session ID and resumed launch arguments; `fixtures/ended-life.ts` also guards the shared notice fixture's single resume. Tests that deliberately exercise CSCB's stopping refusal and retry retain that window instead.

- Test 13 binds the last resume to the same instance/conversation's move to pending, pending-to-waiting transition and applied SessionStart. Await trail publication without ordering it against a separate harness read; retain waiting, launch-start and no-startup-key checks. Test 19 requires waiting with a session plus the matching durable transition/applied hook in the leg's window; it need not sample the transient pending state and adds no fixed report delay.
- Functional delivery waits renew only on increased exact original-workload receipt progress, with 180 s idle and 1800 s overall watchdogs. Reminders, attempts, duplicates and foreign/stale/nonmatching evidence do not count. Require the complete receipt/FIFO audit for success and keep diagnostics before cleanup. Test 35 uses a post-stop connection cursor in every mode, alongside the existing session identity checks. Preserve the latency native sample counts (Test 32: 20; Test 103: 100) and 2 s/10 s p95 limits; synthetic controls are not native acceptance.
- A `fixtures/real-case-assertions.ts` case assertion that re-reads receipts after a delivery wait runs after `--` in that `real_wait_delivery` call: newer evidence can hold work accepted since, such as a reply reminder, which must be awaited, not filtered or failed. The assertion runs its complete receipt audit first, exits 75 (`RECEIPTS_PENDING_EXIT`) only when that audit fails and 1 for its own verdict. See the [fixture and measurement contract](../tests/README.md#real-claude-gate-and-heavy-legs) for how the wait treats each exit status.
- The reset-spacing, key-proof, unknown-proof, `receipts <count>` and `at-least-one-duplicate` commands follow that contract: test 33 runs the first three after `--`, test 104 `receipts 3` and AI AC106 `at-least-one-duplicate`, while test 39's last receipt check re-polls `real_wait_delivery … no-retype`. AC106's earlier copy check stays in `wait_until 180 … case_assert at-least-one-duplicate`, which retries 75 and 1 until the typed copy reaches the transcript; the `--` form would fail at once on 1 before then. `real_assert_latency` after the last waits of tests 32 and 103, `ai-scenario.sh`'s audits right after `real_wait_idle` (`ai_spoof_readback record`, `ai_readback`, `ai-fresh-session.ts`), and `ac20-diagnostics.sh`'s `ai_readback` after its diagnostic wait (opt-in decision21c diagnostics only) are still one-shot; fixing them is proposed as separate work.
- Tests 32 and 103 request genuine Slack replies through the reply tool so production reply-call facts can resolve eligible prior reminder candidates and establish the measured workload's ready-state preconditions. Each admits every latency DM only after production replay finds no unresolved prior reminder candidates or open work, the complete receipt/FIFO audit passes for the exact prior original count, and fresh AD `waiting`, current connection evidence and journal consistency agree. The 180 s admission watchdog fails closed; never suppress candidates, filter slow samples or retry a failed sample; see the [fixture and measurement contract](../tests/README.md#real-claude-gate-and-heavy-legs).
- Test 32's recovery must also retain the same AD instance and nonempty native `session_id`, with exactly one `--allowedTools` flag immediately followed by the exact production reply rule in the resumed row's saved arguments. A replacement conversation or the preallowed label alone fails this proof. Effective permission still requires pinned-version native replies and drain after resume without a permission decision; saved-argument checks and synthetic controls cannot establish that result.
- Test 33 scopes every key fault to the persona instance and the Slack message ID assigned before intake. The shim binds Enter to that instance's preceding outbound text header, including swallowed text; queued reminders and other messages cannot consume the rule. `key-fault-controls.sh` exercises competing messages/personas, stale headers, body spoofing, exact identity and counted consumption inside the CI container. The Enter recovery proof correlates the consuming shim PID with the exact durable fixed part, its recovery record and the unchanged backoff. `recorded: key-evidence` JSON lines in the script log preserve the shim log, server log, queue journal and pre-compaction receipt history before scenario cleanup; archive the run before the verdict reader removes a passing run's directory.
- A harness poll and CSCB's retry timer are independent observers. For a launch-timeout recovery assertion, identify CSCB's first own `waiting` observation, its matching persona retry and that retry's first owned row read. Require the condition to end within the existing bound after that read, whether the harness sees `waiting` earlier or later; a later read cannot hide a delayed condition end. Test 17's executable shell controls cover both observer orders and the recorded CI timing shapes.
- An AD event's `caller_pid` names the AD CLI child. Match it to the shim's exact invocation PID and require the recorded CSCB parent, instance, operation, time window, event order and expected outcome. Use `ad_cscb_calls … with-pid` when that correlation is needed; its default projection stays six columns. For ordinary reconnect continuation, preserve the originating text and every generic text/Enter or validated no-input Enter refusal through the guarded successful Enter. Generic refusals leave plain intents and retry Enter without retyping; only native ambiguous input requires the separate held/no-further-keys control. Test 18's controls reject a server-PID match and unrelated children, including another child of the same server.
- For timed-out launch recovery, calculate B from AD's `launch_started_at`, then audit actual retry starts, re-arms and the persona's owned AD calls. Bound each timer phase from the preceding re-arm and require a checked kill in the first eligible retry; fail immediately if that retry ends without one. A retry can cross B during an AD call; accepting its deferral requires the production rule's own before-B answer. A nominal schedule or broad final deadline cannot prove these properties. Test 26's executable controls cover a missed retry, launch-start offsets, calls crossing B and bounded jitter.
- From agent-director 0.18.0, `status`, `get` and `list` run the find-missing checks on the rows they select, so a harness read can mark or note a row itself. Gate each such change with `ad_release_at_least 0.18.0` and keep the 0.17.x path as it was. A passive harness observation reads the store (`ad_store_peek`), not the CLI. The `ad.find_missing.tick` record names no caller, so attribute a mark with `ad_mark_caller`: it prints every call that could have made it, and the check must hold for each one (CSCB's, not the harness's). A pending row with no launch start is past its grace, and the next read marks it missing; CSCB meets that at once, without a launch-start-not-recorded latch; the relaunch may meet a leftover-session latch.
- After proving recovery starts in that retry, allow separate bounded checked-kill confirmation, fresh-launch and applied-`SessionStart` phases, plus timer stop where the leg requires it. Keep genuine create errors, no kill before the AD-based B, successful checked-kill evidence, fresh AD terminal evidence and an owned row read before relaunch, and the recovered session's exact hook identity. Production-path tests with modeled AD outcomes do not establish native hook behavior; test 26's Docker scenario owns that proof.

### CI track and cleanup controls

Use the composed `ci-run-lifecycle.test.ts` cases to check ordinary work
while login waits, early protected login release, combined failures/missing
coverage, reason retention, mount integrity, build-lock cancellation and
late output secret scans without a released-login reread. Its Docker and
credential dependencies are fake; it does not establish native acceptance.

Run [contained runner controls](../tests/README.md#contained-runner-controls)
only in a marked disposable image. They exercise the actual shell loop and
process cleanup, including a late final survivor after every script END
passes. Require no `done`, retained lock ownership until retirement and a
non-PASS host outcome for uncertain final cleanup. Preserve default
fail-fast and unsafe-cleanup precedence, transitive dependency skips,
independent continuation and every failure/reason in merged evidence.

### Safe Docker inspection

Agents MUST use the private inspection wrapper for Docker diagnostics, as required by root `AGENTS.md`. Supply credentials only through the environment; never print them or dump environment values. Use one of:

```sh
bun scripts/safe-docker-inspect.ts docker inspect NAME
bun scripts/safe-docker-inspect.ts docker container inspect NAME
bun scripts/safe-docker-inspect.ts docker image inspect NAME
```

The wrapper emits complete sanitized JSON with all recursive `Env` fields removed and copied credential/routing values masked. Only `--format '{{.Id}}'` and `--format '{{json .Id}}'` (or `-f` equivalents) are supported; these project locally after sanitization. Other formats, global Docker options and unsupported commands are refused before spawning Docker. Never bypass it with raw inspection through a tool, pipe or log, even with `--format`; on failure, stop inspection rather than fall back.

The CLI captures both streams privately with a 4 MiB combined input budget and a 30 s deadline, and bounds sanitized output too; failures emit neither stdout nor stderr. The API accepts a byte budget up to 16 MiB, a deadline up to 30 s and an abort signal, returning wrapper `code`, inspection `text`, `actualExitCode` (null when unobserved), sanitized `stderr`, `timedOut` and `outputTruncated`; every failure has empty `text`.

Incomplete or uncertifiable capture, including a byte cap, deadline, abort, read failure or cancellation, withholds child stderr behind a fixed nonempty reason while retaining available exit metadata; no secret prefix may escape. Snapshot monitors must retain the redacted command, wrapper and actual exit codes, and sanitized stderr or the withholding reason for every inspection attempt.

Wrapper exit codes are 1 (child/capture failure), 64 (refused request/options), 65 (invalid or unsafe data), 75 (byte limit), 124 (deadline) and 130 (cancellation). This protects wrapper callers, not unrelated shell commands, and leaves existing CI's narrow inspection contracts intact.

#### Operator review integration fixtures

`fixtures/fmk-texts.ts` provides these installed-package contracts:

| Entry and arguments | Assertion/output |
|---|---|
| `operatorReviewRequest <config-path> <record-path> <id> <request-or-revise-or-refresh-or-cancel> [name/channel/delivery...]` | Production request bytes bound to current generation and target identities. |
| `operatorReviewPending <config-path> <record-path> <pending-path> <id>` | The exact recorded request generation has the current durable review. |
| `sharedReviewConsumed <config-path> <record-path> <review-path>` | The saved review has a durable consumed outcome; absent, previewed, attempted, superseded, rejected or foreign evidence fails. |
| `sharedApplicationPreserved <config-path> <before-record> <after-record>` | Validated applied/source/lifetime facts survive intent-only operations. `sharedAuthorityPreserved` also preserves pending intent. Both retain reset fields and membership identity/type/external-sharing facts while permitting freshness metadata to advance. |
| `stoppedDowngradeBaseline <config-path> <record-path>` | Applied `resume_enabled:false` configuration only with no outstanding intent, used by `tests/reload-fixtures.test.ts`. Test 40 uses preserved 0.18.0 references instead. |

Controls cover shared/fmk success plus missing-image, outside/traversal/symlink/file-kind refusals. The helper atomically publishes generated bytes and waits for its exact current review. `configuration_application_preserved` and `hold_not_applied` compare validated authority facts. Scripts 8/9/29 request or revise before the separate rename. Test 9 counts every non-preview runtime line for unchanged personas, with startup/connection/teardown negative controls; separately observed input/request may legitimately produce multiple previews without application. Test 10 saves the exact credential-rotation review and requires its consumed outcome alongside the existing credential handshake/socket/session checks.

Test 40 is a stopped prior-release fixture: snapshot config/authority/request/pending/apply separately, validate raw applied resume=false configuration with that release's loader before replacement, run only that fixture, stop again, archive its files and restore exact original bytes. Live process, nonempty queues, outstanding intent, resume=true and loader refusal fail closed. Shell controls seed present and absent request/pending/apply files, assert withholding/restoration/old-run archival and ordering, and leak-check intermediate previews before replacement/confirmation; they prove no native/live upgrade acceptance or runtime schema conversion.

The ci-live lifecycle consumers use `validReviewSuffix` and `checkPreviewLog`: exact lifecycle prefixes plus mandatory operator/channel-review grammar, and every log line compared to the full pending body. Keep altered, missing, duplicate and reordered negative controls. Pure operator/preview tests establish projection semantics independently; static consumer checks are not live evidence.
