A static/unit check or `--plan` result proves neither paid acceptance nor measured durations; record actual gate/heavy verdicts, duplicate/token reports and durations only after those runs.


### The /ci-live runner

The `/ci-live` runner (`ci-live/`, see `docker/README.md`) has its own dependency, `playwright-core`, installed only in `ci-live/node_modules`. Its unit tests live in `tests/` like every other suite.

- Import only from `ci-live/lib/`, `ci-live/provision/`, `ci-live/checks/` and `ci-live/dry-run/`. Never import `ci-live/run.ts`, `ci-live/main.ts`, `ci-live/maintenance.ts`, `ci-live/runtime/` or `ci-live/browser/` (`driver.ts` and the flows): they load `playwright-core`, directly or through `main.ts` or `ci-live/runtime/workspace.ts`, so `bun test` and `bun run typecheck` would fail on a clone where the runner's dependency is not installed. Put logic a test must reach in `ci-live/lib/` or `ci-live/provision/`, as the memory watchdog (`lib/memory-watchdog.ts`), the copy of the container's own logs (`lib/container-logs.ts`), the stray-app rules (`provision/app-listing.ts`) and the prompt guard (`checks/prompt-guard.ts`, driven through `PromptGuardDeps` with a fake trail and the shared fake clock) are.
- Put no `*.test.ts` or `*.spec.ts` file under `ci-live/`: `bun test` would pick it up.
- A runner file loads nothing from outside `ci-live/` except `src/`'s two import-free text modules, `src/reload-preview-clauses.ts` (the reload preview's retired clauses) and `src/startup-summary-ending.ts` (the start summary's ending builder), plus `scripts/non-reclaimable-memory.ts` (the shared non-reclaimable memory calculation), and no package but `node:*` builtins and `playwright-core`. The runner runs on the host and `ci-live/tsconfig.json` typechecks every file it reaches: any other `src/` module would load the Slack SDKs, the agent-director client or `bun:sqlite`. None of these three modules may import anything. The checks build the texts these modules cover from them, never a literal copy; other `src/` texts the checks expect stay copies, each pinned against `src/` in `tests/ci-live-checks.test.ts`. `tests/ci-live-docker.test.ts` enforces the load rule by a source audit.
- Drive I/O through the runner's seams (`SecureFs` for the secret store, `ScanFs` for the secrecy scan, `LockDeps` for the run lock's file access and PID liveness test and a collecting warning sink for its stale-lock `WARNING`, the spawn function for docker and the host probes, the injected fetch and clock; `ContainerLogsSink` for the copy of the container's logs (an in-memory sink, or `containerLogsSink` over a `mkdtempSync` results dir) with a fake `ContainerExec` for the container and the shared fake clock as the collector's `clock` (`CollectorClock`), which a caller's wait runs on; for the memory watchdog, its `WatchdogSources` and `WatchdogClock`, the file reader `readHostCgroup` takes and the `/proc` reader, `ProcReader`). A test never reads `~/.config/cscb-test/` or the host's cgroup files, takes the real run lock, starts a container or reaches Slack.
- The code no test may import (`ci-live/run.ts`, `ci-live/main.ts`, `ci-live/maintenance.ts`, `ci-live/runtime/`, `ci-live/browser/`) is pinned by the source audit in `tests/ci-live-docker.test.ts`: its environment reads, spawn sites, host commands (the HOST check's two read-only probes the only host-side agent-director and tmux argv), the staged agent-director binary (selected only through `selectAgentDirectorBinary`, copied into a fresh temp dir removed in a `finally`, never in a spawn or docker argv), the tmux and agent-director commands inside its `bash -c` scripts (collected by `shellScriptCommands`, with a script it cannot read on a closed list of one), docker subcommands (the exact `docker stats` and `docker stop` argv included), leftover removal, the run lock's acquires and their warning sinks, signal handling (`main.ts`'s `stopRun` and `maintenance.ts`'s stop), the memory watchdog's wiring, the cleanup order, the copy of the container's own logs awaited before every removal or stop of the container (so a failed check can still be traced once the container is gone) and sealed before the closing scan, `appsCommand`'s order, the prompt guard's wiring, the browser's bounds in `browser/driver.ts` (`ensureSignedIn`'s idle and the one-at-a-time flows included) and each account's sign-in-code wiring (its own address for the mailbox, `ensureSignedIn`'s password and emailed-code branches, the second address's `addressForms` registered with the redactor, `openSessions`' fixed skip reason). A change there that adds a host command, a `bash -c` tmux or agent-director command, a spawn site, a lock acquire, an environment read or a removal or stop of the container, or reorders a pinned sequence, fails the audit; widen or update the audit for that one item in the same change, and never loosen a pattern to get it green.
- Correlate delivery evidence through `ci-live/checks/delivery-evidence.ts`: `deliveryLines` matches complete persona/source/channel/timestamp fields and `waitDeliveryLines` waits for the receipt diagnostic that can follow a Slack reply. Assert the expected sender where the check requires it. Never select a delivered item by body text in a server log; transcript-only `tagstext` remains available for edited messages.
- Use `ci-live/checks/agent-control.ts` for Check 12's terminal stop/lift and Check 18's permission-prompt input. It sends an optional Escape through agent-director, polls `status` for `waiting` within `REPLY_TIMEOUT_MS`, then attempts one `send-keys --text` submission; agent-director appends Enter. Keep its permission/dialog guards: no pending or pane-hash override, screen-based readiness check or automatic resend after refused or uncertain input. Check 7 injects its fault with agent-director `kill` and requires `kill_sent === true`; that confirms the fault was sent, while the existing reconnect, log and Slack-reply assertions still prove recovery.
- Test agent control through `fakeContainer`, `makeCtx` and `virtualClock` in `tests/ci-live-checks.test.ts`: literal text quoting, Escape before status polling, waiting after pending/working states, refused or malformed status, bounded waiting and no text resend. Retain the end-to-end delivery and permission assertions when changing the control mechanism.
- `queueEvidenceScript` projects metadata inside the container: full acceptances, compacted delivered keys, original sequences, sent attempts, receipts, confirmed items and outstanding counts. It confirms a full item only when every fixed part has a receipt, and recognizes a compacted Slack key by channel, timestamp and delivered time. Only the projection leaves the container. Check 24 retains the original timestamp immediately and records its accepted sequence, proves one outstanding item with no premature send/receipt/reaction/restart and the exact fixed waiting notice, then blocks later checks until that same item has a transcript tag, matching delivered diagnostic and no outstanding parts after recovery. A new successful post cannot satisfy teardown.
- Drive those checks with `fakeContainer`, `makeCtx`, scripted human sessions and `virtualClock`; use `assertNoLeak` plus body sentinels. Exercise wrong persona/channel/timestamp, early receipt, incorrect notice body, duplicates and failed original-item recovery. Keep the helper free of production adapter imports on the host.
- The runner's tokens are fakes built at runtime, as everywhere under `tests/` (see Credentials Fixtures and Leak Checks); `tests/secrecy-audit.test.ts` rejects a token literal.

#### Remaining agent-director dependencies

The migration is partial. The following existing paths remain unresolved; do not extend their lower-layer access or weaken their assertions to complete the migration. The [two cardinal rules](engineering-guide.md#the-two-cardinal-rules) govern tests and fixtures too.

- **Native idle compaction (B10):** `tests/integration/fixtures/native-idle-compaction.ts` still interprets native binary fragments. agent-director must own compatibility detection and expose structured support/disabled/unknown reasons and current-launch observations for native compaction before this fixture can migrate. Preserve the real compaction boundary, launch/session provenance, timing bounds and queued-delivery assertions; a version string or generic idle state cannot establish them.
- **Process continuity (Check 13):** its existing pane-PID comparisons require an agent-director observation that verifies the same live launch/process before and after both in-place reloads, with PID-reuse protection and an explicit unknown/unavailable outcome. An unchanged row ID, session ID or launch timestamp alone does not prove that process survived. Preserve the one-row, server-PID, routing, receipt and remembered-word assertions as well.
- **Diagnostic pane capture (B11/B12):** `ci-live/lib/container-logs.ts` still captures panes through tmux. agent-director's [v0.14.0 caller contract](https://github.com/gabemahoney/agent-director/blob/v0.14.0/docs/caller-contract.md) permits `read-pane` only while `pending`, at most once a second; replacing arbitrary working/permission-state captures with that verb would still violate the contract. Request an agent-director-owned diagnostic surface with supported states, ownership checks, bounds and explicit refusal/unknown results. Treat its output only as diagnostics, never as readiness or delivery evidence.

### Slack intake proof in containers

Run `tests/integration/test-31-fmk-ack-burst.sh` only through `/ci`. It submits
1,000 distinct events concurrently to one silent stub persona, correlates
every WebSocket send with its actual ACK by envelope ID, generated socket
UUID and label, and requires every monotonic pre-send-to-ACK interval to be
at most 3,000 ms. Its pass state intentionally keeps all 1,000 items
outstanding, with no typing, receipts, receipt reactions or model calls.
Before asserting the deadline, it prints all 1,000 numeric elapsed intervals
in push order, their maximum and p95, and over-limit and negative counts,
so a deadline failure retains the complete timing evidence.
This is separate from test-44's durable-store p99 on actual storage and the
real-agent framework's transcript latency. Record actual script duration
from `/ci`, not from the host's static checks.

Test 29 compares the exact `message-received` Counter over all stopped
writers' log rotations with the complete accepted queue set, preserving
pre-compaction evidence across restart. Cover paired-event dedupe, both
shared recipients, direct DM and every refused input/nonrecipient. Keep its
 metadata and transcript export. See the Slack stub and acknowledgement
burst sections in `tests/README.md` for timing fields and proof boundaries.

All four entrypoints source `scenario.sh` directly before

| Test | Phases and coverage |

| 46 | 1–5: queue/directory faults, process kills, live membership, review replay and lost bot-attempt answers. |

The helper bootstraps 65–67 with genuine accepted/receipted P/Q inputs and

### Thread Memory performance runs

The production routing adapter coalesces separate join saves for up to 10 ms
or 32 requests per persona. `thread-memory.test.ts` uses the injected
`joinSaveClock` and held durable-I/O fsyncs to check shared success/failure,
record order, both bounds, intervening writer operations and lifecycle
cancellation. The server wiring test executes the actual adapter and checks
that it opts in. These savings do not change any performance limit.

Optional diagnostics require exactly `CSCB_TEST_DIAGNOSTICS=1`; absent,
empty, `0` and all other values leave them off. The host runner forwards a
defined switch unchanged through the child environment and bare
`--env CSCB_TEST_DIAGNOSTICS`; absence adds no option or default. `/ci`
never enables it automatically. Leave it unset for gate measurements.

Only Test 44's measured burst cases, Test 45's strict first-hang measured
start/burst/ordered writes, and Test 32's strict/open measured thread phases
can profile. Later-hang, open membership 48, all new membership groups and
recovery groups remain unprofiled. Disabled runs create no profile, load no
profile preload and do no optional profile waits; Test 44's optional server
timing rows and CPU/latency observers are also off. Required measurement
records, performance evidence and numerical verdicts remain on.

Enabled profiles stay in scenario scratch, with bounded best-effort cleanup
and content-free summaries; they cannot change test status or observation
boundaries. Test 32 samples at 100 ms for at most 300 s to cap profile memory,
with one continuous wave around its 20 samples. See the
[diagnostic scope table](../tests/README.md#optional-test-diagnostics).

Run `tests/integration/test-44-fmk-thread-burst.sh` (bursts, Post Holds and the
large shared list), all strict/open membership groups (45/48/51–64; full
filenames in [Layout](../tests/README.md#layout)), and the
thread phase of
`tests/integration/test-32-fmk-real-order.sh` (real-agent DM p95 and strict/open thread-selected latency with 100,000 joined threads and two personas, delayed/hung names and concurrent shared-state writes) only through
`/ci`. Use the packed server, acknowledgements captured from the actual
socket, and stores on the container's real scratch storage; unit or simulated
runs do not supply this evidence. For an authorized complete two-lane run,
follow the [two-lane integration procedure](../tests/README.md#two-lane-integration-procedure):
take scheduler network access into account. While scheduler jobs run with the
network off, Test 13 and Test 47 run locally because they install packages
from the npm registry; every other no-model/non-burst workload, including
recovery 46/65/66/67, goes in one scheduler selection. Each local workload,
including native-model and burst workloads, runs in its own disposable-container
`/ci` invocation, one at a time. Every other workload keeps its current lane. Resolve
prerequisite closure and retain SELECTIVE verdicts and reader exit 3;
the caller judges combined coverage separately.

The bounds measure CSCB, so the tests' own burst driver (`sr8-evidence.ts`
`burst`, `fault-burst` and `fault-recover`) runs off the measured server's
CPU quota. Test 44 and every strict/open membership group run in
[burst-driver shards](../docker/README.md#burst-driver-shards): the server
keeps 2 CPUs of `cpu.max` quota, as in every shard, shared as before with the
Slack stub, the scripts and the runner. `tests/integration/fixtures/burst-driver.sh`
hands each driver run to a launcher born in its own group beside the server's,
at 0.9 CPU, and the cgroup each run ran in is recorded. The container has
4 CPUs (`CPUS_PER_SHARD` + `DRIVER_CPUS`), so 1.1 CPU is headroom above both groups.
The runner's naming-family classifier includes every suffixed membership
entrypoint. Admission reserves the two extra CPUs per driver-bearing shard;
multiple driver scripts in a shard add them only once. These shards retain
`--init`, private cgroup namespaces and writable cgroups. Recovery groups
remain ordinary no-model, non-burst workloads.

The launcher takes only one of the three driver commands, its arguments, a
record path, and the `SCENARIO_ROOT` and three `SR8_*` profiling fields. It
runs the image's root-owned Bun itself, from `/`, with its own `PATH` and
`HOME`, so a caller's `PATH`, Bun options, preload, `bunfig.toml` or `.env`
file never reaches the driver. The server's UID owns no cgroup file, so
nothing it runs can change group or limit.

While the measured server still runs, `driver-cpu` reads that record and the
server's cgroup. As the server's UID, from the server's group, it opens every
guarded cgroup file on both paths write-only, and writes nothing. It passes
only when:

- the server's quota is 2 CPUs and the driver's is finite;
- every cgroup holding both allows both;
- every present guarded file refused the open.

A driver in the server's group or quota, a guarded file that opened (even a
write-only one), a probe error other than a refusal, or an unreadable
placement is missing. It checks placement, configured quotas and permissions,
not throttling. A throttled ancestor (the container's quota) never shows in
the server group's own `cpu.stat`: its tasks wait runnable, which only its
`cpu.pressure` shows. With 0.1 CPU of headroom (a 3-CPU container), b.9p6's
SR-8 runs saw such gaps of up to 313 ms, and a Post Hold released 110 ms late
fits that class. The 1.1 CPU of headroom keeps the container's quota clear of
the 2.9 CPUs the groups can use. The entrypoint refuses, and `driver-cpu`
reports `missing` for, a container with less than 1 CPU of headroom
(`SR8_CONTAINER_HEADROOM_CPUS`). A passing control still does not rule out
contention outside the container (the host's own quota or other load).

Take populations and burst counts from `tests/test-helpers/thread-populations.ts`:
0, 10,000 and 100,000 Joined Threads per persona across 100 eligible
`thread_hybrid` channels, in both `strict` and `open` Channel Modes, with one
recipient and two recipients sharing the channel. Test 44 runs all 12
combinations in `sr8Combinations()` order: population, mode, recipients.
These are verification populations, not product limits: check counts, every
seeded identity (including the oldest Joined Threads), and every new burst
root after a clean restart; forget nothing to meet a limit.

Seed through production Thread Memory **before the server's first start**.
The `seed` command in `tests/integration/fixtures/sr8-evidence.ts` first writes
the matching `config.json.last-applied` record when absent, using production
`initialSharedChannelState` and `serializeSharedChannelState`; it writes no
journal or seal schema itself. Require exactly one changed-while-stopped
report per seeded persona on the first start, stop cleanly, then measure the
next start reopening those populations with no such report or Joins lost
report.

At population 0, omit both seeding and the first start; the measured
start still requires no report.

Per combination, submit 1,000 first-time root-mention joins, then 1,000
unmentioned replies in those threads, plus 100 dropped unmentioned top-level
messages. Build events with `tests/integration/lib/scenario.sh` before the
burst, and count each recipient's actual envelopes by ID.

Submit the held
probes first, wait for their ACKs and durable Post Hold stores, then submit
ordinary traffic while their own-post outcomes remain unresolved. Require an
ordinary acceptance strictly between hold admission and resolution on the
server clock, with every overlapping item's ACK meeting N1 on the stub clock.

At 100,000, shorten maintenance through `queue_compact_interval_ms` and prove,
for each recipient, a queue compaction by two different existing queue journal
file identities observed between the first push and final ACK (creation or a
replacement first seen afterward is insufficient), and a Thread Memory
compaction by its `thread-compaction` entries in `test-measurements.jsonl`.
An entry counts only when it lies wholly inside the span of the burst's own
acceptance stores on the server clock, a span inside push-to-final-ACK, so
startup and other out-of-burst compactions never count; skips count as
complete, but each recipient needs at least one rewrite. Retain
pre-compaction queue observations, including the fixture's validated
held-admission archive, for later readers.

Test 44 also keeps a new channel post unresolved for at least 120 seconds in
each mode, through a full 100,000-join, two-recipient burst: replies in another
user's new thread must acquire no Post Hold, while bot-parent and
unknown-parent replies exercise timed holds. That case keeps the production
maintenance interval, longer than its whole window, so no compaction is
required and both reads must see one Thread Memory journal. The test's large
shared-list case requires at least 1,000 channels per persona, configuration
and ordinary preview content each above 64 KiB, growth and reopen without
loss, and a proved write failure preserving the previous state and prepared
input.

Eight independent membership groups per mode retain all 14 strict and all
14 open cases through `tests/integration/lib/membership-load.sh`. Tests 45/48
run first/later hang only; strict 51–57 and open 58–64 respectively run
first/later transient, rate, scope, denied and late, then lookup and
undurable. Every case freshly seeds and reopens 100,000 joins for both the
faulted persona P and unaffected Q. Every entrypoint requires only test-1,
with no sibling prerequisite or serial wrapper; original bursts, verdicts
and bounds are unchanged.
Their `fault-plan`, `fault-burst` and `fault-check` path declares
P's dependent work before submission, proves fault overlap with Q's burst,
and preserves every original, refusal and replay.

Dependent originals remain
unacknowledged and unstored while withheld; recovery uses new envelopes,
stores accepted work exactly once and judges recovery N1 from each new push.
Q keeps the full burst and limits, P's independent traffic keeps N1, and
intentional drops remain acknowledged and unstored.

Require the case-specific evidence too: first/later membership deadlines and
incomplete scans, retry spacing and `Retry-After`, idle repair within its
published bound, unchanged membership state after an abandoned first- or
later-page late answer (excluding only `source: own-post` joins for threads
absent from the before read taken after the complete mark; facts, attempt order
and all retained joins compare byte for byte in order), zero ACKs for an
undurable live membership event with a failed write probe, fired hung and late
`users.info`/`conversations.info` lookups, and
overlapping durable ordered writes. Fresh senders and channels must reach the lookup rather than
a lifetime cache; missing fault or overlap evidence cannot pass. Membership
request deadlines use stub arrival and server diagnostic timestamps on the
container wall clock; wall-clock steps that leave a valid interval are not
independently detected.

Test 32 runs its whole thread phase once in `strict` and once in `open` mode,
each with fresh state and evidence and two personas seeded at 100,000 through
the sequence above; one supplies at least 20 sequential thread-selected
real-agent samples and the other supplies concurrent writes. Admit samples
through the existing `real-scenario.sh` gates: fresh own-row agent-director
`waiting`, current connection/relay/marker/lifecycle evidence, drained prior
work and reply candidates, and controlled N2 setup without competing input.
Transcript receipts prove delivery only; never filter out or retry a sample,
and judge every verdict on its own mode's evidence.

`real_assert_thread_latency` in `tests/integration/lib/real-scenario.sh` uses
the `thread-latency` command in `tests/integration/fixtures/transcript-receipts.ts`
to audit receipts and print the N2 samples and p95 verdict.

In each mode, include one 500 ms delayed lookup that resolves the name and one
hung lookup, using senders not yet resolved in that server lifetime; require
the stub's fired record for each. The hung sample waits for fallback and is
slow by design: nearest-rank p95 of 20 is the 19th sorted value, tolerating
that one slow sample while retaining it. Keep the delayed sample within the
typing limit.

Start each sample's membership event and shared-state write only after its
reply's ACK, which follows its durable admission, and record each operation's
own start and end on the host's epoch clock. `thread-intervals` in
`transcript-receipts.ts` takes a sample's admission from its accepted
`received_at` and its delivery from its last durable delivered part;
`concurrent-overlap` in `sr8-evidence.ts` credits an operation only when it
starts at or after admission and before delivery, and requires at least one
credited membership event and one credited write. Membership events and open
writes receive start-only credit: this proves the operation was issued while
the sample was in flight, not that the server handled it then. A strict-mode write (the writer persona's own live leave or rejoin of its write channel, ACKed only once durable) also needs its end before that sample's delivery, because its durable application lies inside that push-to-ACK span.

Use the one nearest-rank implementation, `percentile` exported by
`tests/integration/fixtures/transcript-receipts.ts`: sort ascending and select
rank `ceil(p × n)` for percentile fraction `p` and sample count `n`, without
interpolation. The fixture owns `SR8_ACK_LIMIT_MS`, `SR8_STORE_LIMIT_MS` and
the 100 ms `SR8_DISPATCH_ALLOWANCE_MS`; obtain production timer/budget values
through `tests/integration/fixtures/fmk-texts.ts`, never copied script limits.

| Measure | Statistic and limit |
|---|---|
| Receive-to-ACK (N1) | Maximum over every accepted event, held probes included, and every dropped unmentioned message: at most 3,000 ms. |
| Durable acceptance | p99 below 50 ms over all burst acceptance stores, accepted and held items included; exclude post-ACK fixation appends from the count and percentile. Every membership group also checks each persona separately. |
| Real-agent latency (N2) | After storage, typing p95 at most 2 seconds and receipt-confirmed delivery p95 at most 10 seconds. |
| Held-reply resolution | Strict limit: `THREAD_REPLY_HOLD_MS` from CSCB's receipt of the Event plus that hold's own durable resolution append. Pass when excess over this limit is at most 100 ms; fail above it. Every `post-hold` line prints signed `excess_ms` and `allowance_ms`, including failed or missing results. |
| Agent-director calls (N3) | At most `DELIVERY_MAX_AD_CALLS_PER_S` × 10 (40) per persona in every sliding half-open 10-second window of the measured phase, and none in the observed empty-queue interval (`empty_calls` must be 0). The fixture conservatively counts every CSCB call in its per-instance evidence, excluding harness calls. On the current agent-director 0.18.8, `list` doesn't show unproven requests, so one turn-end read is required to catch b.92q's race. Test 32 opens the empty-queue window one poll interval plus a 1000 ms margin after the final turn-end transition, conservatively waiting from its observation of that transition; the margin covers list/get latency and dispatch. Separately, `n3-turn-end` asserts at most 1 counted `get` per persona from AD's final `state_changed_at` to that idle boundary; those reads still count toward the sliding rate limit. Follow-up: when CSCB moves to an agent-director whose `list` exposes unproven requests, drop the turn-end read and return to the original window. |
| Hung name fallback (N4) | Strict limit: `NAME_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT_MS` (2 seconds). Pass when excess is at most the same 100 ms allowance; fail above it. Every `n4` line prints `fallback_ms`, `excess_ms` and `allowance_ms`. |
| Startup load | Record the measured start's external start-to-ready time with the seeded Joined Thread count; no pass bound. `population` is per persona; `joined` is the total across recipients. |

N4 requires all four checks: fallback timing within its limit and allowance,
delivery with the fallback name, the hung sample's ACK within N1, and its
continued inclusion in the N2 sample set. Measure `fallback_ms` on the
server's monotonic clock from that sample's durable accepted store to the
start of its fixation append, matching persona key and sequence number.
The lookup starts after the first endpoint and uses fallback before the
second, so this interval includes dispatch and preparation; delivery follows
the full timeout and lookup-to-delivery is not the N4 measure.

The 100 ms
allowance applies only to Post Hold resolution, N4 and a membership hang's
request duration (D − A) over `MEMBERSHIP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`, whose
`membership-fault` hang lines also print signed `excess_ms` and
`allowance_ms`. It never applies to N1, store p99, the membership attempt
deadline, retry spacing, `Retry-After` or idle repair.

Read ACK intervals from the stub's monotonic push and ACK observations.
Store, Post Hold and name-fallback timings and compaction observations come from the test-only
`test-measurements.jsonl` in the state directory: each record carries the
server's `at_mono_ms`, and stores carry their duration. The scenario enables
it with `test_measurements: true` in `config.json`; clean shutdown awaits its
drain before the final read.

Every Test 44 case and membership-load case enables `test_measurements: true`
through the shared SR-8 config generator. That base switch alone enables hold
attribution, synchronous-work markers and a 10 ms unref'd server probe recording
dispatch gaps over 20 ms. Each `event-loop-stall` row carries last-tick/start, expected and actual
fire times, elapsed/gap ms, process user/system CPU deltas (µs), the server's own
cgroup-v2 `cpu.stat` counters and deltas since the preceding tick, and heap-used/
heap-total bytes at both ends. A missing/malformed reading is `null`, never a
zero-throttle claim. High process CPU hints at busy work; low CPU plus raised
throttle counters supports quota starvation. Heap changes only hint at GC;
unmarked busy work, mixed causes and host scheduling may need further profiling.

Each stall also carries `resource_delta` (Bun `process.resourceUsage()` counters:
minor/major page faults, voluntary/involuntary context switches, filesystem block
input/output operations), sampled at every probe tick. `resource_before_mono_ms`
identifies its pre-gap reading. Unavailable readings/counters and counter resets
are `null`, never zero. Process resource counters include the runtime's threads;
filesystem operation counts are not bytes.

The costly bundle adds cgroup `cpu.pressure`, `memory.pressure`, `io.pressure`
`some`/`full` totals and deltas (µs), endpoint `memory_current`/`memory_max` (bytes,
or `max`), selected `memory_stat` and deltas (`anon`, `file`, `shmem`,
`pgmajfault`, `workingset_refault*`), and host aggregate `host_steal_ticks` plus
`host_steal_delta_ticks` from `/proc/stat` (kernel clock ticks, not milliseconds).
Memory byte gauges may have negative deltas; fault/refault counters may not.
`system_sampling=stall-end` means the bundle is read once at startup and then
only at stall endpoints: local every-tick sampling cost about 144 µs, versus
15.7 µs for a normal tick with endpoint-only system reads. `system_before_mono_ms`
and `system_after_mono_ms` expose that wider interval. A positive PSI/refault/
steal delta therefore does not prove it occurred in this one gap; resource and
`cpu.stat` deltas still use the preceding probe tick. These are observer-cost
measurements with injected timer re-arm, not contained SR-8 performance evidence.

`recorded: sr8 attribution ... verdict=info` lines preserve this evidence even
when a lane keeps only `recorded:` output. `type=post-hold` prints persona key/seq,
server process ID, receipt, due, every callback with its armed delay, evaluation time and signed
lateness, plus stalls and synchronous work overlapping `[due, evaluate]` on the
server clock (including work by other personas). Process IDs keep restarted
server lifetimes separate when a retained file includes several starts. `type=stall` prints each gap's
CPU/throttle/heap data and overlapping work; the largest 200 gaps are printed,
with `type=stall-summary` giving the full count, maximum and sum. Per-window
arrays cap at 50 and retain their uncapped counts. Work markers cover runs over
20 ms in Thread Memory judge, digest, image concatenation and save selection,
queue compaction selection/stringify/rebuild, and measurement serialization.
Fine markers cover Thread Memory activation replay (intents, joins, judge,
settlement), read/parse/index recovery, compaction collection/sort/merge/cache,
image indexing/encoding/concatenation, write/publish/digest, save encoding and
publication, journal synchronous generator steps/writes, shared-seal/authority durable
writes, atomic durable replacements/unlinks and console-log writes. Whole
`thread-compact-sync`/`queue-compact-sync` stretches stay open across resolved
promises and close only at existing macrotask yields or native asynchronous
journal I/O; they resume at continuation. Nested phase/whole-operation spans
and spans of different personas can overlap and must not be summed as exclusive
CPU time. No new scheduling boundary is introduced by these markers.
All attribution observers, reads and probe timers are absent when the base
`test_measurements` switch is off.

On a verdict or script failure, the shared SR-8 failure hook runs after server
stop and recorder drain, before scratch cleanup. It copies up to 64 regular
measurement files (including scenario snapshots) to
`/test-results/<script>.sh.sr8-measurements-N.jsonl`, the shard-results mount;
on the host these are beside the script logs in
`/run/openclaw/horde/cscb-ci-<run>/shard-N/` (or that run's configured temp root).
`type=kept-file` prints the container path and original source;
`type=failure-row` prints at most 400 rows per file within ±2 s of each failing
Post Hold deadline-to-evaluation window, prioritizing timing/stall/work rows.
`type=failure-summary` gives window, available-row and printed counts. Full
files retain every byte. Retention is informational and preserves the script's
failure; result ownership allows only these numbered regular files for assigned
burst scripts. Test 44's optional CPU profile and detailed `observe` output still
require `CSCB_TEST_DIAGNOSTICS=1`. Its per-event ack/append/save rows remain
opt-in under `test_measurement_timings: true`, enabled only for diagnostic burst
cases. Default and non-burst test-44 cases do not gain per-event ack/append/save
rows. Membership-load cases already enable that separate per-event switch.

Membership-load cases print
`recorded: sr8 diag` lines before the post-restart verdicts. `diagnostic=ack-summary`
gives each persona's stub push-to-ACK and server receive-to-ACK maxima;
`diagnostic=ack-slow` correlates its five slowest stub samples by envelope ID,
with both intervals, process-local timestamps, ACK-call duration, and
receive-to-store/store-to-ACK splits where the durable target is uniquely matched.
The server interval ends at the ACK call; its return timestamp includes the call.
Compare durations across processes, never their monotonic timestamps. `gap_ms`
also includes delivery/dispatch before routing and ACK transport/observation;
it does not by itself prove stub scheduling delay. Replayed timestamps may give
`server=ambiguous`; absent observations print `none` or `ack-unavailable`.
`diagnostic=append-cost` adds six lines per persona: `window=burst` and
`window=roots`, each split into `journal=queue-acceptance`, `queue-other` and
`thread-memory`. Each complete window runs from its first server receipt to
its last ACK return; every original event in that window needs a unique successful
server ACK. Lines give append counts, records per append (min/p50/max), append,
fsync-wait and non-fsync sums/p50/p99/max, file/directory fsync totals, wall time,
and `append_wall_ratio` (summed append duration divided by that wall time).
Queue acceptance appends match the same persona's following acceptance-store
rows in recorder order; partial group matches print `unclassified_queue_appends`.
Only whole append intervals inside the window enter sums; straddling intervals
print as `boundary_appends`, without prorating their fsync cost. Incomplete ACK
windows print `window_complete=no` and no cost sums; invalid append timings
print `append-unavailable` while preserving ACK diagnostics. Zero samples have
no percentile or ratio. Fsync wait includes callback dispatch, and the residual
includes other waits and scheduling as well as synchronous append work; it is
not a CPU measurement. Compaction rewrites have no append timing row and are
excluded. Post-ACK appends completing after the window are excluded as well.
These lines supply no verdict or allowance. Timing observers add clock reads,
record construction, buffering and periodic file writes to the measured process,
so diagnostic runs include that instrumentation cost.

A restart resolution without `held_ms` supplies
no timing sample.

Measure startup immediately before launching the measured start and after
its readiness wait succeeds, on one external clock in the same container;
exclude the first seed/seal start. The measurement file contains no load
record. With the test-only settings absent, the server writes no measurement
file and keeps hourly maintenance.

Read results against the `recorded: sr8 conditions` line: Bun version, CPUs,
cgroup memory limit, filesystem type, the state directory's mount and server
peak RSS. Test 44 captures its largest two-recipient open-mode burst, every
membership group captures each case, and Test 32 captures each mode's thread
phase while its measured server still exists. Membership groups also add the server's
cgroup's `cpu.max`, its 2 CPUs, and that cgroup's throttling deltas since the
case's start (`unknown` when unreadable). Test 44 and every membership group follow each
driver run with `driver-cpu`, which records where the driver and the server
ran, how many guarded cgroup files a write-only open by the server's UID
reached and how many it could not probe. The
fixture's output forms are:

```text
recorded: sr8 conditions bun=<version> cpus=<count> memory_limit=<limit> fs_type=<type> state_dir_mount=<mount> peak_rss_kib=<KiB>[ cpu_max=<quota|max>/<period> nr_periods_delta=<n> nr_throttled_delta=<n> throttled_usec_delta=<usec>]
recorded: sr8 driver-cpu scenario=<scenario> mode=<strict|open> population=<joins-per-persona> recipients=<1|2> samples=<driver runs> server_cgroup=<path> server_cpu_max=<quota|max>/<period> server_cpus=<n> server_usage_ms=<ms> driver_cgroup=<path> driver_cpu_max=<quota|max>/<period> driver_cpus=<n> driver_usage_ms=<ms> shared_cpus=<n|none> guarded_files=<n> writable_files=<n> unprobed_files=<n> limit=2 verdict=<pass|missing>
recorded: sr8 <measure> scenario=<scenario> mode=<strict|open> population=<joins-per-persona> recipients=<1|2> samples=<count> <statistics> limit=<limit> verdict=<pass|fail|missing|recorded>
recorded: sr8 summary scenario=<scenario> measures=<count> pass=<count> fail=<count> missing=<count>
recorded: sr8 membership-fault-row case=<case> source=<fault|fault-settled|api|scan|stub> <fields>
```

A `membership-fault` case that does not pass first prints its
`membership-fault-row` lines, before its verdict lines. They are correlation
rows, not measures, and carry no `verdict=`: each staged fault, its
settlement and API answer (joined by fault ordinal), and each scan
diagnostic, as numbers and code words only (`rows=unavailable` when the
stub records or scan diagnostics are absent).

Each verdict command prints every result line and its summary before
returning failure for any `fail` or `missing`; a script can therefore stop
before later cases. Keep the full emitted output, including strict limits,
`excess_ms` and `allowance_ms`, in the CI run record. This guide records the
method, not measured results.

Missing evidence is never a pass. The `sr8-evidence.ts` header holds the full
list and command-specific requirements; its common missing cases are:

- An absent or malformed measurement file, or fewer or mismatched acceptance
  stores than accepted burst items; fixed appends count toward neither the
  acceptance count nor p99.
- A push without its unique ACK, or missing push, timing, accepted-item or
  join snapshots. The declared withholding path instead requires explicit
  zero-ACK observations and complete recovery accounting.
- Fewer real-agent N2 samples than required.
- Either required compaction not proved inside the burst at 100,000.
- A held reply without its resolution or its own key/sequence-number
  `resolution-store` append.
- An absent hung N2 sample or accepted/fixed record for its key/sequence number.
- An absent fired fault for either the hung or delayed lookup sample.
- Absent external startup timestamps or N3 idle-window observations.
- A burst driver run inside the server's CPU quota, a guarded cgroup file the
  server's UID can open write-only, a probe error other than a refusal, or an
  unread driver or server placement
  (`driver-cpu`).

## Fixture Patterns

### Factory Functions

Every test file defines factory functions that create fixtures with sensible defaults and optional overrides:

```text
makePersonaConfig(overrides?, baseDir?) — a resolved PersonaConfig with one default persona
makeMultiPersonaConfig(specs, baseDir, overrides?) — a resolved PersonaConfig with one persona per spec
makeTransport() — minimal transport stub
makeServer() — minimal MCP server stub
```

Always use factory functions instead of hardcoding fixture values in individual tests. When a new field is added to a type, update the factory function — all tests automatically pick up the default.

Reload-controller tests build their configuration directory, personas and runs with `makeReloadHarness` (see Reload Tests), not by hand.

Persona-loader tests, and tests of persona-keyed code such as `spawnForPersona`, `startupSessionManager` and `launchSession` in `src/session-manager.ts`, use the shared persona-config helper, `tests/test-helpers/persona-config.ts`. Use it for ordinary resolved and file-form configs; committed upgrade fixtures live under `tests/fixtures/upgrade-0.11.1/` and `tests/fixtures/shared-channel-upgrade/`, while rejected shapes appear only as raw input to rejection cases. The CLI's `loadConfig` dependency returns a resolved `PersonaConfig`, so CLI tests build it with these helpers too. The persona-config helper provides:

```text
makePersona(overrides?, baseDir?) — one PersonaInput entry in file form; default paths sit under baseDir
makePersonaConfigInput(overrides?, baseDir?) — a PersonaConfigInput file-form config with one default persona
makePersonaConfig(overrides?, baseDir?) — a resolved PersonaConfig, as loadPersonaConfig returns it, except mcp_config_path (see below)
makeMultiPersonaConfig(specs, baseDir, overrides?) — a resolved PersonaConfig with one persona per PersonaSpec, in order
makeStandInPersonaConfig(personas, baseDir, overrides?) — makeMultiPersonaConfig for stand-in personas keyed and named by one channel ID each
writeConfigFile(dir, input) — writes input as JSON to <dir>/config.json and returns the path
```

The config builders take `channel_mode: 'strict' | 'open'` through server-wide overrides; persona `channels`, `permission_prompts` and `dm` keep the same shape in both modes. `makePersonaConfigInput` and `makePersonaConfig` take config-level overrides and build one default persona; use `makeMultiPersonaConfig(specs, baseDir, overrides?)` for persona-level fields. Each `PersonaSpec` is `Partial<Omit<Persona, 'index'>>`, with direct `channels`, `permission_prompts` and other supported persona overrides; resolved builders must agree with the production loader.

`makeMultiPersonaConfig` requires the test’s temporary `baseDir`, rejects duplicate names or keys and keeps input order. Each persona defaults to its own `all` channel, that channel as its Notice Destination and DMs off; with no channels, the default destination is `dm`, so supply an enabled DM and contact when the loader will validate it. `makeStandInPersonaConfig(personas, baseDir, overrides?)` builds the same shape with channel-ID keys/names for suites that require them. Builders perform no validation; validate file-form input through the production loader when that is what the case exercises.

For the other helpers, `baseDir` defaults to the OS temp directory; pass the test's own `mkdtempSync` directory when paths must exist or be unique to the test. `writeConfigFile` writes only into the caller-supplied temp directory and has no default location. Pass `loadPersonaConfig` a temp home as well, so `~` never expands to the real home. Remove both the temp directory and the temp home in `afterEach`.

Build agent-director rows in tests with the canned-row helpers in `tests/test-helpers/agent-director-stub.ts` (`cannedListRow`, `cannedGetResult`, `cannedGetResultPlural`), never by hand. Every row they build is persona-labelled:

- **Default form** — `cannedListRow({ instance_id })`: the row stands for the persona whose key is the instance ID without its `cscb_` prefix. Labels are exactly `service=cscb` and `persona=<key>` (no `config_dir`, no `channel`), tmux `slack_bot_<key>`, and `cwd` is `defaultCannedRowCwd()`, the working directory of the default persona fixture (`makePersona()`, `<tmpdir>/personas/test_bot/work`; nothing creates it). The stub client's default `get` row uses this form. Use it for permission-poller and click-handler rows, and pair it with a `getPersona` stub that knows that key.
- **Persona form** — `cannedListRow(overrides, persona, home)`, likewise `cannedGetResult` and `cannedGetResultPlural`.

A `channel` label appears only in explicit negative rows that test the rejection of pre-persona rows (the poller skipping a row with no `persona` label, the start sweep killing a live one and keeping it): override `labels` to carry only the old `channel` label.

For the persona form, pass a resolved persona (e.g. from `makePersonaConfig`). The row then carries what a spawn of that persona writes: `cwd` = its working directory, `cscb_<key>`, `slack_bot_<key>`, and the `service`, `persona` and `config_dir` labels. The collision ladder and the start sweep replace a row whose `cwd` or `config_dir` label doesn't match ( the ladder with no row deleted, a finished row by a reuse spawn of the same id and a live row through the live-row sequence first), so a fixture meant to reach a resume, reconnect or wait path must use this form. `home` is required and the persona form throws without it; there is no OS-home fallback. The `config_dir` label must be computed under the same home the session manager's `_setSpawnHomeDir` seam uses, or it won't match the one the code computes, so pass that home. To test a guard, override `cwd` or `labels` explicitly. `spawnForPersona` joins a launch already in flight for the same key, so a suite that can leave a launch unsettled calls `_resetInFlightLaunches()` in `afterEach`.

To test that only one launch per persona is in flight, wrap the stub with `holdSpawns(stub, shouldHold?)` from the same file. Each `spawn` whose instance ID passes `shouldHold` (all by default) stays open until the test settles it; other spawns go to the stub's original `spawn`. The handle exposes `calls` (every spawn received), `held()` (instance IDs still open), `entered(id)` (resolves once a spawn for `id` is issued), `release(id)` and `fail(id, err)` (settle the oldest held spawn for `id`), and `releaseAll()` for teardown.

To keep a live-row sequence's `find-missing` run outstanding while a case drives other work (the start pass, an apply, a stop, a lost message), wrap the stub with `holdFindMissing(stub)` from the same file (`FindMissingHold`). Every `find-missing` call stays open until the test settles it, oldest first: the handle exposes `calls` (every call received since the hold, in order; held calls are not in the stub's own call log), `heldCount()`, `entered(count?)` (resolves once that many calls, 1 by default, have been received), `release(result)` (resolve the oldest with a placement built with `cannedFindMissing()`), `fail(err)` (reject the oldest) and `releaseAll()` (resolve every held call with the empty result) for cleanup.

To assert which agent-director calls a case made (for example, none for a persona that is not up), use the shared stub call-log helper in the same file rather than a hand-rolled recorder, so every suite reads the stub's calls the same way.

To give a stub `list` the filter of agent-director 0.16 and 0.17.0, answer it with `listByDisplayedState(rows, params)` from the same file: a row matches a `state` filter by the state it shows, so a row showing `needs_intelligence` or `idle_screen` never matches its raw state, and `label` entries must all match. Use it wherever a stub `list` filters rows that show a displayed state, never a hand-written filter.

To stand in for `resolveSystemBinary()` (the start gate's system-install lookup, the runtime version re-check's resolve, `/publish`'s check), use `makeStubResolveSystemBinary(opts?)` from the same file; no test runs a binary to learn a version. It returns an `(opts?) => Promise<{ path, version }>` function. With no options every call resolves with `PHASE1_RC_VERSION`, which passes CSCB's Phase 1 floor, at `/usr/local/bin/agent-director`; `path` changes that path, `version` the version of every call, and `throws` rejects every call with that error. `outcomes` answers the calls in order, one entry per call, and once the list runs out its last entry answers every later call: `{ version, path? }` resolves with that version (at `path`, else the builder's `path`), `{ throws }` rejects with that error, and `{ never: true }` returns a promise that never settles, for a time-limit case. `outcomes` given with `throws` or `version`, or empty, throws when the stub is built. `calls` records each call's argument, a call that never settles included.

**agent-director errors.** Build an agent-director error in a test with the stub's builder wherever one exists; every builder builds from its class binding, the three Phase-1-only ones included. For an error the stub has no builder for, or a description or verb no builder takes, a test may use `new` on the client's own class imported from `src/agent-director-errors.ts` (for `ErrTmuxUnresponsive`, `ErrTmuxKillFailed` and `ErrTmuxSessionConflict`, its binding there; never a named import, re-export or destructuring of one from `agent-director`). The classifier decides by class, so a base `AgentDirectorError` named like a class is not that class: use one only as a look-alike, expecting UNCLASSIFIED. A test of a site's error handling builds the error with the stub builders and imports the class it expects from `src/ad-error-class.ts` (`AD_ERROR_CLASS_*`), never a literal label. Assert a call-capture array with `toHaveLength`: Bun's `toEqual([])` also passes on `[undefined]`.

Each builder uses the installed client's own class, except:

- `errGeneric(verb, errName, message?)`, which builds the base `AgentDirectorError` for any `errName`; a name CSCB gives no handling is UNCLASSIFIED, a refusal at every launch site, so a case that wants a launch failure uses `errTmuxSessionCreate`, never an invented name or `errGeneric` with a class's name;
- `errAmbiguousRequest()` and `errPermissionRequestNotFound()`, which build the base `AgentDirectorError` with the error's `errName` although the client exports a class for each, because the code under test recognises both by `errName`.

The builders of the three Phase-1-only errors (`errTmuxUnresponsive*`, `errTmuxKillFailed`, `errTmuxSessionConflict`) use `new` on `ErrTmuxUnresponsive`, `ErrTmuxKillFailed` and `ErrTmuxSessionConflict` as `src/agent-director-errors.ts` re-exports them (the pinned client's own classes), each value carrying its verb, its name as `errName` (the `ERR_TMUX_*_NAME` constant) and its description.

The description words CSCB matches come from `src/ad-description-phrases.ts`, and the builders take them from there. A test that checks for one imports the constant from that module, never a literal. The builders' default names are the default persona fixture's: `STUB_TMUX_SESSION_NAME`, `STUB_INSTANCE_ID`, and `STUB_TMUX_SOCKET_PATH` for the socket.

- **`ErrTmuxUnresponsive` (class binding)**: `errTmuxUnresponsive(verb?, description?)` (verb `resume`; `status` only reads the store and never returns it; by default a tmux call that did not answer and did nothing). The variants CSCB tells apart: `errTmuxUnresponsiveLaunchTimeout(verb?, instanceId?)` (verb `spawn`, or `resume`; carries `LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_PHRASE`), `errTmuxUnresponsiveStillStopping(verb?, sessionName?)` and `errTmuxUnresponsiveStillStarting(verb?, sessionName?)` (verb `resume`, session `STUB_TMUX_SESSION_NAME`; the description names the quoted session name, as agent-director's does, and carries `STILL_STOPPING_PHRASE` or `STILL_STARTING_PHRASE`), `errTmuxUnresponsiveAfterDuplicateSession(verb?)` (verb `resume`; tmux answered "duplicate session" and the session holding the name could not be read, so nothing was started), and `errTmuxUnresponsiveNewRowEnded(verb?, sessionName?)` (verb `spawn`, session `STUB_TMUX_SESSION_NAME`; HO rev 26, a plain spawn's `tmux new-session` answered "duplicate session" and its re-lookup of the holder did not answer, so agent-director ended the new row; the description names the quoted session and carries `NEW_ROW_ENDED_PHRASE` and the retry `NEW_ROW_ENDED_RETRY`, the stub's own export, "retry with reuse_finished once the session name is free", since `src/` keys nothing on it and holds no constant for it; it carries none of `LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_PHRASE`, `STILL_STOPPING_PHRASE` or `STILL_STARTING_PHRASE`, so it is no launch timeout).
- **`ErrTmuxKillFailed` (class binding)**: `errTmuxKillFailed(sessionName?, description?, pids?, options?)`, verb `kill`. The descriptions follow agent-director 0.12.0's wording (`pkg/api/kill_errors.go`): each is the full text the client delivers, starting `tmux: agent process still running: instance <id>: tmux session "<name>": ` (the id from the file-local `killFailedInstanceId`: `cscb_<key>` for a persona's session `slack_bot_<key>`, else `STUB_INSTANCE_ID`), and ends "retry kill later; never delete this row" (`RETRY_KILL_LATER_PHRASE`, `NEVER_DELETE_ROW_PHRASE`), and a kill sent is "a kill was sent to the agent's pane and to its labelled session" (the stub models only that opening). `description` is a `KillFailedDescription`: `'outlived-exit-wait'` (the default; a kill was sent, and "the agent process (pid N)" was still running after the kill exit wait of 5 s), `'pane-process-survived'` (a kill was sent, and the survivor clause was or were still running after it), `'unverifiable-session-present'` (a kill was sent, but the agent process cannot be checked and its labelled session is still there) or `'no-session-no-kill'` (no session or pane of this launch was found while its agent process still runs "(pid N)", so no kill was sent, with the "Operator actions" pointer). N is `STUB_WORKER_PID` (4194350, above Linux's largest pid and distinct from every pid of `STUB_SURVIVOR_PIDS`). Only `'pane-process-survived'` carries the survivor clause: for one of `pids`, `SURVIVOR_CLAUSE_ONE_PHRASE` then "(pid S)"; for several, `SURVIVOR_CLAUSE_MANY_PHRASE` then "(pids S1, S2)", joined with ", " (default `STUB_SURVIVOR_PIDS`, one fake pid above Linux's largest), the form `SURVIVOR_PID_PATTERN` matches and `survivorPids` lists in order; the other three ignore `pids` and name no survivor. `options` is `KillFailedOptions`: `workerAlsoRunning: true`, with `'pane-process-survived'` only, puts "the agent process (pid N)" and " and " before the survivor clause, with "were still running", the form agent-director writes when the worker and survivors both outlived the wait. The builder checks its own text with `survivorPids` and throws if the survivor pids it reads are not exactly those given (none for the other three, with or without the option for the survivor description), if `'pane-process-survived'` is given no pid, or if `workerAlsoRunning` is given with another description. `KILL_FAILED_DESCRIPTIONS` lists all four for `test.each`.
- **`ErrTmuxSessionConflict` (class binding)**: `errTmuxSessionConflict(verb, conflictCase, sessionName?, options?)`. `conflictCase` is a `ConflictCase`, one per case of agent-director contract `no-valid-id`, `different-id`, `another-store`, `own-id`, `leftover`, `scan-leftover` (the pre-spawn scan's refusal: "left over from an earlier life", the session's tmux id `STUB_TMUX_SESSION_ID`, "nothing was written and no row was created"), `duplicate-session-leftover` (a plain spawn at "duplicate session": "its label names this instance id", "left over from an earlier life", "the new row was ended"), `not-this-launch`, `pane-not-found` (also "this row's own id"), `conflicting-labels`, `never-reported-in` (also "this row's own id" and "no kill was sent"), and `unrecognised`, which carries none of the case words. `not-this-launch` from `kill` also carries "this row's own id" and "no kill was sent". `CONFLICT_CASES` lists all twelve. Every description carries the `agent-director list --tmux-session-name <quoted name>` line. `different-id` and `another-store` ("another agent-director store") say the session is another row's (another store's) agent and must not be ended, and point to no "Operator actions"; every other description points a human to "Operator actions". `options` is a `ConflictOptions` selecting the variants the positional form cannot: `plainSpawn` on `different-id` or `another-store` (a plain spawn at "duplicate session": also "its label does not name this instance id" and "the new row was ended"), `notAdopted` on `pane-not-found` (a lost create reply: also "the agent's pane was not adopted"), `scan` on `conflicting-labels` (the pre-spawn scan found an agent-director label value set at the server, global or global-window scope: also "nothing was written and no row was created"); an option set on any other case throws. No description names a command that ends a session; "no kill was sent" is the one mention of a kill. The case words and extras come from `src/ad-description-phrases.ts`. A test that iterates the latch's conflict cases uses `CONFLICT_CASE_ROWS` from `conflict-cases.ts` (under Other shared fixture builders), which covers every entry of `CONFLICT_CASES`.
- **0.10.0 classes**: `errTmuxNotAvailable(socketPath?, verb?)` (verb `spawn`; with `socketPath` that socket is not accessible to this user, without it tmux could not be run); `errTmuxNotAvailableDifferentServer(socketPath?, verb?)` (verb `resume`, socket `STUB_TMUX_SOCKET_PATH`; other single-row verbs that call tmux, such as `read-pane`, also return it, `status` never; carries `DIFFERENT_TMUX_SERVER_PHRASE`); `errTmuxNotAvailableNewRowEnded(verb?, sessionName?)` (verb `spawn`; the ENVIRONMENT form of `errTmuxUnresponsiveNewRowEnded`: tmux could not be run for the re-lookup, with the same words, `NEW_ROW_ENDED_PHRASE` and `NEW_ROW_ENDED_RETRY`, HO rev 26); `errTmuxCaptureFailed(sessionName?, verb?)` (verb `read-pane`; the session is gone); `errSpawnNotPausable(verb?)` (verb `pause`); `errSystemInstallDisappeared(verb?, binaryPath?)` (verb `status`, path `STUB_RESOLVE_DEFAULT_PATH`). Beside `errSpawnNotInteractive(verb?)`, `errSpawnNotInteractiveLeftover(sessionName?, verb?)` (the session is a leftover of an earlier launch) and `errSpawnNotInteractiveNoLaunchStart(verb?)` (a `pending()` row with no launch start), both verb `send-keys`. `errSendKeysWhileRelayed()` builds the client's `ErrSendKeysWhileRelayed` (verb `send-keys`: agent-director refuses keys to a row that sits on a relayed permission prompt, and nothing was sent), which classes UNCLASSIFIED; use it rather than `errGeneric` with that name. `errInvalidFlags(verb?)` builds the client's `ErrInvalidFlags` (verb `decide`; pass `spawn` or `resume` for a launch verb's refusal). `errCwdNotFound(verb?, cwd?)` and `errCwdNotADirectory(verb?, cwd?)` (verb `spawn`, `cwd` `/x`) build the client's directory errors, and `errTmuxSessionCreateStaysPending(verb?)` (verb `spawn`) an `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` whose description ends with agent-director's sentence that the row could not be restored and stays pending (`RESTORE_SENTENCE_STAYS_PENDING`), built through `withRestoreSentence`. `RESTORE_SENTENCES` holds HO rev 28's four restore sentences that can end a failed `resume`'s or reuse's description (restored to its prior state; changed after the move and left as it is; removed after the move, so nothing restored; could not be restored and stays pending), and `withRestoreSentence(err, sentence)` gives `err` again, same class, verb and name, its description ending with `sentence`, so it classifies as `err` does. CSCB matches no part of any of them (the retry's read of the row decides), and a case's row stays as the case scripts it, never derived from the sentence.
- **No class in any client**: an unknown name arrives as `ErrUnknownErrorName`, built as the client builds it: `unknownName` is the name and `envelope` is the binary's `{ err_name, err_description }`. The client's own `verb` and `errDescription` stay as it sets them, so read the binary's description from `envelope.err_description`. `errUnknownErrorName(unknownName?, description?)` builds any name (default `ErrFromALaterBinary`); `errInternal(description?)` an `ErrInternal`; `errSchemaMismatch(description?)` an `ErrSchemaMismatch` (by default the store could not be opened), while the other two store-open names, `ErrSchemaMigrationRequired` and `ErrStoreOpen`, are built with `errUnknownErrorName` and the `ERR_*_NAME` constants from `src/agent-director-errors.ts`; `errUnusableName(fault?)` the unusable-recorded-name `ErrInternal`, carrying `UNUSABLE_RECORDED_NAME_PHRASE`, where `fault` is an `UnusableNameFault` (`'empty'`, the default, `'control-character'` or `'stored-differently'`, all in `UNUSABLE_NAME_FAULTS`; `tests/ad-error-class.test.ts` and `tests/conflict-latch.test.ts` iterate `UNUSABLE_NAME_FAULTS` directly, and the session-manager, server, restart and health-check cases take their UNUSABLE NAME answers from `UNUSABLE_NAME_CASE_ROWS` in `conflict-cases.ts`, which crosses it with every site kind); `errConfigMalformed(key?, value?, minimum?, unit?)` an `ErrConfigMalformed` in agent-director's refusal form, `config <path>: refused [tmux] values: [tmux] <key> = <value>, below its safe minimum <minimum> <unit>. A missing key, or 0, gives the default.` (default `starting_session_seconds` = `30` below `60` `s`; `unit` is `s` or `ms`).
- **Every UNAVAILABLE form**: `UNAVAILABLE_FORMS` is the one table of UNAVAILABLE forms, each an `UnavailableForm` tuple `[label, make(verb), causeKind]`: `ErrTmuxUnresponsive` and its three variants (`ErrTmuxUnresponsive, still stopping`, `ErrTmuxUnresponsive, still starting`, `ErrTmuxUnresponsive, launch timeout`), `ErrCallTimeout`, `ErrUnknownErrorName`, `a wrapped UnknownError` (CSCB's `UnknownError` wrapper), `ErrTmuxKillFailed` (cause `kill-failed`; only a kill answers it) and `a plain Error`, every other form with cause `unavailable`. A file takes its subset with `unavailableForms(...picks)`, in the order given: a label picks its row as is, a `[label, as]` pair relabels it, and a label the table lacks throws. Never write a file-local copy of the table.

**Dead-session causes, escalate-dead verdicts and dead evidence.** Tests import the causes (`DEAD_SESSION_CAUSE_*`), the prompt-row/reconnect verdicts (`ESCALATE_DEAD_ROW_ABSENT_AT_PANE_READ` included), the evidence texts (`ESCALATE_DEAD_EVIDENCE`) and the evidence helpers (`isDeadEvidence`, `carriedDeadEvidenceOf`, `CARRIED_DEAD_EVIDENCE_NONE`, `DEAD_EVIDENCE_NONE`, `describeDeadEvidence`) from `src/session-manager.ts`, and iterate the exported lists `DEAD_SESSION_CAUSES` and `ESCALATE_DEAD_VERDICTS` rather than a copy of their values, so a new cause or verdict is covered by every case that walks them. The expected answer of each is `DEAD_EVIDENCE_OF` (`tests/test-helpers/dead-evidence.ts`), the one table of which cause or verdict is dead evidence: keyed by `DeadEvidenceSource`, so a new value fails the typecheck until it has an answer there, and written out by hand, never asked of the code under test. `tests/session-manager.test.ts`'s describe alone checks `isDeadEvidence` against it; other suites (`tests/restart.test.ts`) read it for what a cause or verdict leads to and never re-assert `isDeadEvidence`. Expected lines come from their builders (`deadSessionRouteLine`, `deadEvidenceVoidedLine` with `deadEvidenceVoidingRead` or a `DEAD_EVIDENCE_VOIDED_BY_*` text, `waitRowFinishedLine`, `waitRowAbsentLine`, `promptRowSweepFinishedLine`, `joinedLaunchDropsDeadEvidenceLine`, `relaunchWithoutKillLine` with its reason, `killVoidsVerdictLine`), each pinned once as a literal. A cause's GONE-ness (`DEAD_EVIDENCE_OF`) never changes with the path; whether it leads to a kill or a sequence also depends on the path's last read, since dead evidence covers one life: a read of the row as `ended`, `missing` or gone voids every piece the path holds, and a reconnect's `row-not-interactive` voids a carried verdict. So a session-manager case states, in its hand-written row, whether the path still holds live evidence at the not-resumable step (`liveEvidence`) and which pieces it voided, in line order (`voided`); a restart case crosses each verdict with each `dead` re-probe, and expects no kill after a first probe or re-probe that read a row: installation disappearance reads unknown and never kills or relaunches. Regression cases cover first probes, re-probes and legacy dead-shaped readings, preserving outage and recovery counters until fresh authoritative AD evidence arrives. A restart-path escalate-dead answer is built as the adapter builds it, `{ outcome: 'escalate-dead', deadEvidence: carriedDeadEvidenceOf(verdict) }` (`ReconnectEscalateDead`). Build every carried value through `carriedDeadEvidenceOf` (or `CARRIED_DEAD_EVIDENCE_NONE`): `CarriedDeadEvidence` carries a type-only brand, so an object literal fails the typecheck. The one exception is the `handBuilt` helper in `tests/session-manager.test.ts`, which casts past the brand to pin the builders' run-time shape and to hand the code a deliberately inconsistent value (an `evidence` flag its source does not prove); never copy it into another file.

**Phase 1 results.** The Phase 1 result fields `kill_sent`, `launch_started_at`, `liveness_note` and `pre_trust` are typed by the client's own result types; `src/ad-phase1-types.ts` names only the `liveness_note` values CSCB tells apart (`LivenessNote`) and the `pre_trust` type (`PreTrust`, the client's own). A binary older than Phase 1 omits `kill_sent` and `pre_trust`, which the client declares required, so the stub's `kill`, spawn and `resume` answers are typed `StubKillResult`, `StubSpawnResult` and `StubResumeResult`: the client's type with that one field optional (`MayLackPhase1Fields`). A Phase 1 field given as `undefined`, or left out, is absent from the built result, as from a binary older than Phase 1, with one exception: a `pending` row's launch start (below).

- `cannedKillResult(killSent?)`: `{ kill_sent }`, or `{}` without an argument. The stub's default `kill` result is `{}`.
- `cannedStatusResult(overrides?)`: `{ state: 'waiting' }` by default, which is also the stub client's default `status` answer (`cannedStatusResult()`). Its one Phase 1 override is `launch_started_at`: agent-director's `status` result has no `liveness_note`.
- `cannedGetResult` and `cannedListRow` take `launch_started_at` and `liveness_note` as overrides. A `pending()` row from any of the three canned builders (`cannedStatusResult()`, `cannedGetResult`, `cannedListRow`, and so the stub client's default answers) shows the sample launch start `SAMPLE_LAUNCH_START_DEFAULT` (`SAMPLE_LAUNCH_STARTS.fractional`) unless the overrides have a `launch_started_at` key, since a configured persona's own `pending()` row with no launch start latches the persona. "No launch start" is an explicit request: `launch_started_at: SAMPLE_LAUNCH_START_NONE` (`undefined`: the key is left out of the row) or `launch_started_at: null` (the key shown as `null`). A row in any other state has no launch start, and no row has a note, unless given one; an explicit override wins in every state. Launch starts: `SAMPLE_LAUNCH_START_FRACTIONAL`, `SAMPLE_LAUNCH_START_WHOLE` and `SAMPLE_LAUNCH_START_NONE` (`undefined`), all three by form in `SAMPLE_LAUNCH_STARTS` for `test.each`; take launch starts from these constants and never type a timestamp. Notes: `provenanceNote` (`provenance_conflict`, the only note that latches a persona, with the CONFLICT case "conflicting labels"; the stub's own spelling of the wire value, not `src/`'s constant, so a misspelt constant fails a test), `nonLatchingNotes` (every other note agent-director names: `tmux_server_changed`, `process_not_seen_session_present`, `process_not_seen_tmux_unchecked`, `probe_eacces`, `tmux_session_name_empty`, `tmux_session_name_control_char`, `tmux_session_name_rewritten`, typed as the client's free text) and `unknownNote` (a note CSCB does not know, `provenance_conflict_cleared`, so a prefix match of the latching note fails). Take note values from here, never type them; the note-rule cases in `tests/session-manager.test.ts` and `tests/conflict-latch.test.ts` iterate `nonLatchingNotes` and `unknownNote`: every entry at the pure decision, the collision `get` and the post-run `get`s, and a sample of them (one or two listed notes, `unknownNote` and no note) at the other sites, which share the one note rule.
- `cannedSpawnResult(instanceId?, preTrust?)` and `cannedResumeResult(instanceId?, preTrust?)`: `preTrust` sets `pre_trust` (`ok`, `skipped` or `failed`); leave it out for a result from a binary older than Phase 1, which carries no `pre_trust` key.
- `PRE_TRUST_VALUES`: the three `pre_trust` values (`readonly PreTrust[]`), for `test.each` with the two builders above; an absent field is their `preTrust` left out. It is built from a private record keyed and valued by every `PreTrust` member, so a member missing from it, an extra key or a misspelt one fails `bun run typecheck`. Tests take `pre_trust` values from this list and never type them.
- A recorded `spawn` may be a reuse spawn: `spawnCalls` and `holdSpawns`' `calls` are typed with the client's `SpawnParams`, so a test reads `reuse_finished` with no cast; the stub answers a reuse like any spawn, from the same queue and knobs.
- `cannedFindMissing({ rows })`: `rows` maps each row ID to where a sweep reports it, `'ids'`, `'unverified_ids'` or `'neither'` (`FindMissingRowPlacement`; `'neither'` on a row read `pending` models a row the run did not judge); both ID lists are sorted and `count` and `unverified` are their lengths. `cannedFindMissing(overrides?)` builds the result field by field (empty by default).

**Stub client knobs.** A `<verb>Queue` on `makeStubClient` holds `cannedOk(value)` and `cannedErr(error)` entries; N entries answer the next N calls in order. Once the queue is empty the verb falls through to `<verb>Error`, then `<verb>Result`, then its default. `killQueue` and `findMissingQueue` work this way (defaults `{}` and `cannedFindMissing()`).

For Light Rows, pass `'light'` after the instance-id overrides, or as the fourth argument of persona-form `cannedListRow`; it emits only retained list fields. Supply Full Rows through `get`. An unscripted `get` can reuse a matching full `listResult` fixture, while Light Rows require an explicit Full Row answer. `scriptSweepFullRows` and `sweepOver` in `tests/test-helpers/old-life.ts` make full fixtures available for the first selected read of each applied own row or live stray needing a hold, then preserve the caller's later read script. A kept stray consumes no fixture read.

- `readPaneQueue` wins over `readPaneError` and `readPaneResults` while it holds an entry. Once empty, the call falls through to `readPaneError`, then `readPaneResults` (whose last entry sticks), then `{ pane: '' }`; the queue's own last entry does not stick. The stub reads these knobs off its options object at each call, so a harness may pass `readPaneError` and `readPaneResults` as getters over its own options to change the answer between attempts (the reconnect adapter's `makeHarness` in `tests/server.test.ts`).
- `statusFn(params)` and `getFn(params)` compute each `status` or `get` answer from the call's params and take precedence over every other knob of their verb. Returning an `Error` rejects; the call is still recorded in `statusCalls` or `getCalls`. `getFn` and `statusFn` may each return `undefined`, which hands that call to the verb's other knobs (`getQueue`, `getError`, `getResult`, then the default; the same for `status`), as if it were unset, so a knob that answers for one instance leaves the others alone.
- `findMissingFn(params)`, `readPaneFn(params)`, `sendKeysFn(params)` and `killFn(params)` are per-call knobs like `spawnFn`: each answers a `StubCallAnswer`, may be async, and wins over its verb's queue, error and result; `undefined` falls through to the verb's other knobs, queue first, and an `Error` rejects. Every call is recorded in its capture list (`findMissingCalls`, `readPaneCalls`, `sendKeysCalls`, `killCalls`) before the knob answers; `find-missing` is also in `callLog`, as before. A `findMissing` that `holdFindMissing` held never reaches `findMissingFn`. Use them to script a judged, unjudged or marked-missing run, a pane with or without a dialog, or a `send-keys` error, per call.
- `spawnFn(params)` and `resumeFn(params)` are the per-call launch knobs: each answers a `StubCallAnswer` (a result, an `Error`, `undefined`, or a promise of one) and wins over its verb's queue, error and result. The call is recorded first (`spawnCalls`; `callLog` then `resumeCalls`), then the knob is awaited, so it may be async and move a fake clock inside the call, which is how a case sets a launch call's window; an `Error` rejects, a result resolves, and `undefined` falls through to the verb's other knobs. A reuse spawn reaches `spawnFn` too (`reuse_finished: true` in its params). Take a launch timeout's description words from `src/ad-description-phrases.ts` through the builders (`errCallTimeout(verb)`, `errTmuxUnresponsiveLaunchTimeout(verb, instanceId?)`), never a literal.
- `makeStubCreateClient({ calls })` records the options each client is built with in `calls`, typed `ClientOptions[]`, one entry per call in order (a rejected call included), so a test reads `calls[0].callTimeoutMs`. A field the caller did not pass is absent.
- `makeCloseCountingStubClient(opts?)` returns `{ client, closes }`: a `makeStubClient(opts)` stub whose `close()` is replaced by a counter, and `closes()` the number of calls so far.
- `makePassingGateDeps(overrides?)` returns `Partial<StartupGateDeps>` for a start gate run that passes every step: `createClient` from `makeStubCreateClient()`, `probeGetPermission`, `probeErrorCatalog` and `probeDecideArgv` passing, a `statSync` that throws ENOENT (the same-user check passes silently), `geteuid` 1000, a `recordStartupError` that swallows, and an `exit` that throws, since a passing run never reaches it. `overrides` wins over every default (a test that checks the exit code passes its own `exit`).

Other shared fixture builders in `tests/test-helpers/`:

- `ad-settings.ts`: agent-director's settings file for tests. `writeAgentDirectorConfig(home, input)` writes `.config/agent-director/config.toml` (the path `src/ad-settings.ts` exports as `AD_SETTINGS_RELATIVE_PATH`) under `home`, creating the directory, and returns the path; it throws, writing nothing, when `home` is the real home (`isRealHome()`) or is not a directory under the OS temp directory (the temp directory itself included). `input` (`AdConfigInput`) is either `AdConfigTables` (`tmux`: any of the nine keys; `pauseTimeout`: `[pause] timeout_seconds`; `extraTmuxKeys`: unknown or misspelt `[tmux]` keys; `extra`: other top-level entries, which can replace `tmux` or `pause` with a plain value) or `AdConfigNotToml` (`{ notToml: true, embed? }`: fixed text smol-toml refuses, with `embed` on its offending first line so a leak case can put a fake token there; the one raw-text write). Every other file goes through smol-toml's `stringify` with `numbersAsFloat: true`, and a value (`AdConfigValue`) is a `bigint` for a TOML integer, a plain number for a float or a string. Without that option the serializer writes an integral number such as `60` as the integer `60`, so a float case could never be produced; with it every number is written as a float (`60` as `60.0`), and integers are written as `BigInt`, the type the reader's values have. `REFUSED_AD_CONFIG_FORMS` (rows of `RefusedAdConfigForm`: `name`, `input`, and the `key` the refusal concerns, undefined for text that is not TOML) is list of refused forms for `test.each`: text that is not TOML, a string, a float, a float with a zero fraction, a negative value, `stopping_window_seconds` and `starting_session_seconds` one below their minimums, `pending_grace_seconds` one below the minimum a raised `create_timeout_ms` gives, and that raised `create_timeout_ms` with `pending_grace_seconds` missing and 0. `RAISED_CREATE_TIMEOUT_MS` (the default grace period in milliseconds) and `RAISED_GRACE_MINIMUM_SECONDS` (the grace minimum it gives with the default pipe-close wait) are exported for the grace cases. `DEFAULT_AD_SETTINGS` and `AD_SETTING_MINIMUMS` are re-exported from `src/ad-settings.ts`, never copied, and every threshold in the forms is derived from them and `pendingGraceMinimumSeconds`, so a change to a default or a minimum moves every form. It holds no module-scope state and starts no process.
- `ad-value-reads.ts`: the TypeScript-parser matcher of reads of `agent-director` values, shared by `tests/host-safety.test.ts` (call-site audit) and `tests/fmk-source-audit.test.ts` (the Phase-1-only class reads). `agentDirectorValueReads(sf, names)` finds every read of the named exports from `agent-director` in a file: a named import or re-export, a namespace property or element read (through a cast or a copy included), a destructuring, a default-import, `import x = require`, dynamic-import or `require()` read, and a read it cannot name; `agentDirectorNamespaceArguments(sf)` finds the namespace, a dynamic import or a copy passed to a call. Also shared by both audits: `agentDirectorNamespaces(sf)`, the names a file binds to the agent-director namespace (a namespace or default import, `import x = require`, a dynamic `import()` or `require()` held in a variable, and copies of any of them; type-only imports bind none), which both matchers collect their namespaces with; `finding(sf, node, what)`, the `<1-based line>: <what>` finding format; and `AD_NS`, the `import * as ad from 'agent-director'` line the synthetic sources start with. The node helpers beside them (`forEachNode`, `unwrap`, `moduleLoadOf`, `propertyNameText`) serve both audits. It starts no process and reads no file.
- `ad-version-entries.ts`: `expectRuntimeEntryPointsToDebugSkill(message)`, the one check of a runtime version re-check's startup-errors entry of either class: it names `RUNTIME_RECHECK_PHRASE` and points to the debug skill (`DEBUG_SKILL_RUNTIME_STOP_POINTER`, `DEBUG_SKILL_PATH`), names neither the switch-over runbook nor any line of the install skill's block, and carries no instruction to upgrade or install agent-director (`UPGRADE_FORMS`, whitespace collapsed by `flat`). `tests/ad-version-gate.test.ts` (the re-check's record) and `tests/startup-errors.test.ts` (the entry the real recorder writes) both use it; don't keep a file-local copy.
- `agent-director-versions.ts`: the agent-director versions tests check against CSCB's Phase 1 floor, independent CI runtime and compatibility fixture identities, and the minimum Claude Code version. A test imports every agent-director version it checks from here or from `src/`, never as a literal.
