Floor-derived cases follow `PHASE1_FLOOR_VERSION` (`src/ad-version-gate.ts`); `CI_AD_RUNTIME_VERSION`/`CI_AD_RUNTIME_COMMIT` name the current gate release, and `LEGACY_DISPLAYED_STATE_AD_VERSION`/`LEGACY_DISPLAYED_STATE_AD_COMMIT` name the separate legacy fixture. `PHASE1_RC_VERSION` is the version the Phase 1 release candidate reports: the floor with `-rc.1` appended, built from the constant; the released client rejects it as below its own 0.12.0 minimum. `OLD_AD_VERSION` is the release below the current floor, which the released client and the floor refuse. `DEV_PLACEHOLDER_VERSION` is the client's own `DEV_SENTINEL_VERSION`, re-exported (never typed); the floor refuses it. `DEV_UNPARSEABLE_VERSION` is a non-SemVer defensive injected value that the own floor refuses; native resolution rejects it as unreachable first. `CLIENT_MIN_VERSION` is the installed client's `min_binary_version`, read once at load from its `dist/version-floor.json` through the package's subpath export `FLOOR_SUBPATH` (exported: `agent-director/dist/version-floor.json`, the file `src/install-check.ts` reads); the module throws a clear error at load when the file cannot be resolved or read or holds no string `min_binary_version`. `BELOW_CLIENT_MIN_VERSION` is the plain release one step below the client minimum's core (one patch below, else the previous minor's or major's `999` release), which the client refuses as too old; the module throws at load unless `compareAdVersions` puts it below the minimum. `MIN_CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION` is the minimum Claude Code version agent-director states for its exec-form hooks and the version the fleet runs (the released 0.12.0 notes' "Required agents"). This helper is its one definition: there is no `src/` constant (no `src/` module reads a Claude Code version), and a test never writes a Claude Code version; it imports this constant (`tests/ci-live-docker.test.ts` checks `docker/Dockerfile.live`'s `ARG CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION` pin against it, with its one-patch-below negative control derived from it; a check of the runbook or the docs imports it the same way). `tests/ad-version-gate.test.ts` checks that it is strict SemVer and that no other `tests/` TypeScript file, and no `src/` TypeScript file, writes its value in code. It starts no process, holds no value import of `Client` or `resolveSystemBinary()`, and imports only `src/ad-version-gate.ts` and the client's sentinel, so the agent-director stub imports it without a cycle.
- `archive-db.ts`: `buildTempArchiveDb(rows, defaultChannel)` builds a real message-archive SQLite file through the production `openArchiveDatabase` in its own `mkdtempSync` directory (rows at chosen timestamps, optional per-row channel, WAL checkpointed so a read-only open sees them) and returns `{ dbPath, cleanup }`; `messagesSince(startedAt, channelId, count)` gives `count` rows strictly after a spawn's `started_at`, the one place that boundary rule lives. Used by `tests/jsonl-persistence-check.test.ts`, `tests/session-manager.test.ts` and `tests/persona-routing.test.ts`; call `cleanup()` in teardown.
- `channel-delivery.ts`: `declarationOf(persona)` locally projects `name`, `credentials_file` and `working_directory` from `Pick<Persona, 'name' | 'credentials_file' | 'working_directory'>` to production `PersonaDeclaration`; seeds and records use that same declaration type.

  Both seed helpers accept `Readonly<Record<string, ChannelDeliveryPersonaSeed>>`: persona keys map to a declaration and channel IDs mapped to `{ delivery, set_at? }`. `channelDeliveryRecordOf` and a successful read return `ChannelDeliveryRecord`, a persona-keyed `Map` of declarations and channel `Map` values containing only `delivery`.

  `writeChannelDeliveryRecord(stateDir, entries)` builds the sole envelope through `initialSharedState`/`writeSharedState` and returns its path; its scratch guard refuses the real home, the OS temp directory itself and paths outside it. `readChannelDeliveryRecord(stateDir)` returns declaration/channel maps or `null` when absent and throws on an invalid envelope, while `channelDeliveryRecordOf(entries)` builds the matching in-memory projection; `set_at`/`SAMPLE_SET_AT` are accepted fixture vocabulary, never persisted timestamps.
- `ci-live.ts`: the shared fakes for the `/ci-live` runner suites (`tests/ci-live-*.test.ts`). `memSecureFs()` is an in-memory `SecureFs`, the secret store's seam: files and directories with their modes, plus a log of every call, so a suite can assert the order of a private write (temp file, chmod, rename) and that a path was never read. `virtualClock()` is the runner's `Clock` over the shared fake clock: `sleep(ms)` advances virtual time by `ms`, so a bounded wait runs to its deadline with no real delay. It imports the runner only from the directories The /ci-live runner allows.
- `ci-run.ts`: the builders and fakes of the sharded `/ci` runner's suites (`tests/ci-run-*.test.ts` and `tests/ci-verdict.test.ts`), which drive `scripts/ci-run.ts` and `scripts/ci-verdict.ts` in process through their injected dependencies. One banner per owner, in this order: 1. the spawn recorder; 2. the process table, signals and `/proc`; 3. the lock probe; 4. the fake container interface, which follows Docker's image rules; 5. the worktree builder; 6. the run-directory builder; 7. the reader additions ; 8. the lock directory and password file ; 9. cgroups, `/ci-live` and readings ; 10. sample sequences . A test hand-writes no status file, reservation, results file, result-file line or verdict: a valid one is built here through the runner's own writers, an invalid one from a valid one by a stated change. The helper types no runner constant or message, starts no child process and uses no `mock.module()`; time moves only on `createFakeClock()`. A lane adds only under its own banner.
- `clear-latch-terms.ts`: `CLEAR_LATCH_TERMS` and `clearLatchTermsIn`, the one list of the `clear-latch` spellings nothing offered to a bot may carry: the command and the route, imported from `src/clear-latch.ts` (`CLEAR_LATCH_COMMAND`, `CLEAR_LATCH_ROUTE`), and the underscore and camel-case forms derived from the command, so no spelling is typed in tests; `clearLatchTermsIn(text)` answers the terms found, case-insensitively, in list order. Used by registry.test.ts, shipped-docs.test.ts and notice-texts.test.ts (see Not-Offered Checks).
- `cli-teardown.ts`: fixtures shared by the CLI teardown's two suites (`tests/cli-teardown.test.ts`, the pure pieces, and `tests/cli.test.ts`, the commands). `UNKNOWN_STATE` is a row state CSCB does not know, which the precheck and the teardown take as live; `teardownKillFailedDescription(error)` is the raw description of an `ErrTmuxKillFailed` as the teardown's kill-failure alert decision quotes it, read through the checked kill under `TEARDOWN_KILL_OPTIONS` (it throws when the error gives no such outcome); `cliAlertLine(command, persona, content)` is the kill-failure alert line a CLI teardown gives a persona, built from `src/kill-failure-alert.ts`'s builders with `killFailureCliTeardownEntryContext(command)` and the CLI closing sentence. Pure: no client, process, timer or file.
- `dead-evidence.ts`: `DEAD_EVIDENCE_OF`, the one table of which dead-session cause and escalate-dead verdict is dead evidence: true exactly for the GONE-based ones, keyed by `DeadEvidenceSource` so a new cause or verdict fails the typecheck until it has an answer, and written by hand rather than asked of `src/`. `tests/session-manager.test.ts` checks `isDeadEvidence` against it; `tests/restart.test.ts` reads it for what a verdict leads to. A cause's GONE-ness here is unchanged by the path; whether it leads to a kill or a sequence also depends on the path's last read (dead evidence covers one life: a finished or absent read voids it, and a reconnect's `row-not-interactive` voids a carried verdict), which each case states in its own row. Never keep a copy of it in a test file.
- `durable-io.ts`: the durable-step seams over real files. Journal writers wait for the disk through callback `fs.fsync`/`fs.rename`, so a seam that patches only `fsyncSync`/`renameSync` never sees a journal step; inject, record or hold journal steps through this module.
  - `durableIo({ base?, before? })` wraps `base` (default `node:fs`) and intercepts every fsync and rename in both forms; every other call goes to `base` unchanged. `steps` records each one in call order with its `op`, `form` (`callback` or `sync`) and `path` (the descriptor's path as opened through the seam, or the rename source).
  - `before(step)` runs before each step's syscall. Throw to fail the step without its syscall, or return a promise to hold a callback step until it settles (a rejection fails it). A blocking step cannot be held: returning a promise for one throws. An injected callback failure is reported asynchronously, as a real one is.
  - `busy()`, `next()`, `held()` and `idle()` count started, unheld callback steps; `createFakeClock().settleOn(io)` waits on them (see Fake Clock). The reload and Thread Memory harnesses settle their clocks on their queue and Thread Memory seams, the delivery-notice harness on its queue seam, and the persona-routing harness its opt-in Thread Memory clock on its queue seam (`h.queueIo`) and its opt-in hold clock (`h.resolvers.clock`) on both seams.
  - Nesting: a seam's `fs`, or an object spread from it, carries a mark. A `durableIo` over a marked base passes its callback steps through uncounted and reports the base's in-flight and held steps as its own, so a step the inner seam holds never counts as in flight. A base that spreads a seam but replaces its `fsync` or `rename` must drop the mark, or neither seam counts that step.
  - `failFileSyncs(when, message, base?)` fails file syncs (never directory syncs), in either form, while `when()` holds. `heldStep()` is a gate a `before` hook returns: its `promise` settles on `release()` or `fail(error)`. `holdFirstSync(match, { armed?, base? })` holds the first callback fsync whose path `match` accepts while `state.armed` (armed by default) and returns `{ io, gate, state, reached }`; `reached()` resolves once the step is held. Use it rather than a hand-rolled hold.
- `fifo.ts`: real FIFOs. Node and Bun have no mkfifo API; a test makes a FIFO only through this module, never by starting `mkfifo` itself. `mkfifoAvailable()` is probed once per process: `false` with no child started when `mkfifo` is not on `PATH`, otherwise whether `mkfifo --version` exits 0. Guard a real-FIFO case with `test.skipIf(!mkfifoAvailable())`, the reason in the test name. `makeFifo(path)` creates a FIFO at `path` and throws, naming the path, the exit status or signal and `mkfifo`'s stderr, when `mkfifo` fails; it neither removes an entry already there nor creates the parent directory. Each `mkfifo` child is bounded (`MKFIFO_TIMEOUT_MS`) and its `env` is a direct `hostSafeChildEnv` call naming only `mkfifo`, over a fresh temp HOME removed as soon as the child exits. A `HostSafetyError` (for example `mkfifo`'s `PATH` directory holding an `agent-director`) is thrown, never read as "unavailable". `mkfifoAvailable()` runs while tests are collected (inside `test.skipIf`), so the error makes the whole test file fail to load rather than its FIFO cases skip; from `makeFifo` inside a test it fails that test. The reload harness's `mkfifoAvailable` and `h.makeFifo` delegate to it; `tests/fifo-helper.test.ts` pins it.
- `fungible-decision.ts`: pure `FungibleDecisionRow`/`ChannelDeliveryRow` fixtures for `delivery-decision-fungible.test.ts`; `eligibleMembership` is also consumed by delivery-decision, lifecycle, inbound-recovery and the routing/recovery helpers. `eligibleMembership` supplies explicit positive observations; `decisionArgsOf` and `channelDeliveryArgsOf` compose shared choices, membership and affected `readableFor`. `FUNGIBLE_DECISION_GROUPS` retains predecessor groups plus `currentAuthority`, run forward/reverse with immutable maps. Missing evidence is an explicit unresolved control; no file, timer or module mock.
- `host-safe-env.ts`: `hostSafeChildEnv(home, { tools, pathDirs, extras })`, the environment of every child process a unit test starts. Pass it as the child call's `env` option directly (not built earlier into a variable, spread, merged or wrapped); add variables through `extras`. It returns exactly `HOME` (`home` as given), `PATH`, `TMUX_TMPDIR` and the extras, nothing else from `process.env`, so no token reaches the child.
  - `PATH` is the absolute, test-owned `pathDirs` first, in order (stub or shim bins), then the directory each named tool resolves to on the current `PATH`, duplicates dropped. `tools` defaults to `DEFAULT_CHILD_TOOLS` (`bun`, `bash`, `sh`). With no tool and no `pathDirs` it is `EMPTY_CHILD_PATH` (`/dev/null`), which no lookup can search; pass `tools: []` for a child started by absolute path (`process.execPath`) that runs nothing by name.
  - The tmux fence: `TMUX_TMPDIR` is one directory under the OS temp directory whose name starts with `CHILD_TMUX_TMPDIR_PREFIX`, fixed on the first call and returned by every later call in the process, and no extra can set `TMUX` or `TMUX_PANE`, so a tmux the child starts never reaches the host's tmux server. The first call reuses the process's own `TMUX_TMPDIR` when a parent's `hostSafeChildEnv` set it (`inheritedChildTmuxTmpDir`: an existing directory, not a symlink, owned by this user, directly under the OS temp directory, named with the prefix and more); otherwise it makes one with `mkdtempSync`. So a `bun` child that loads the helper again (a harness run in a child) hands its own children the parent's directory.
  - The directory is never removed: tmux falls back to `/tmp`, the host's default socket directory, when `TMUX_TMPDIR` is missing, so it must outlive every child. Each `bun test` run leaves at most one, plus one for each child whose OS temp directory differs from its parent's: the helper does not pass `TMPDIR` on, and only a directory directly under the child's own OS temp directory is reused. A test that starts such a child and wants the parent's directory reused passes `TMPDIR` as an extra.
  - It throws a `HostSafetyError` whose `reason` is one of `HOST_SAFETY_REFUSAL`, and whose message names the path or name at fault without printing the environment, when: `home` is relative, is the real home or holds an agent-director install (`.config/agent-director`, or anything at the standard install path); a tool name is empty or holds `/` or the `PATH` delimiter, or the tool is not on `PATH`; a `pathDirs` entry is relative or holds the delimiter; any directory on the built `PATH` holds an entry named `agent-director` (a file, directory, symlink or dangling symlink); or an extra sets a reserved name (`RESERVED_CHILD_ENV_NAMES`: `HOME`, `PATH`, `TMUX_TMPDIR`, `TMUX`, `TMUX_PANE`) or is not a string. Fix the fixture, or take the offending directory off the test run's `PATH`; don't catch the error to skip a case.
  - The real home is the account's passwd home or the home the run started with, symlinks resolved. Test for it with the exported `isRealHome()`, never `os.homedir()` or `os.userInfo().homedir`: Bun fixes both at start-up from the launch-time `HOME`. `realHome()` and `passwdHome()`, which answer the real home's path, are referenced only in the guard's own files (`REAL_HOME_FILES` in `tests/host-safety.test.ts`: this helper, the preload, `tests/host-safety.test.ts` and `tests/launch-home-guard.test.ts`), so no other test can build a path under the real home. The module also exports the agent-director predicates (`dirHoldsAgentDirector`, `homeHoldsAgentDirectorInstall`), the discovery names, and the `PATH` lookups (`absolutePathEntries`, the absolute entries of a `PATH` value; `resolveToolDir`, the directory of a tool's first executable on it), so nothing else spells them. `osTempDir()` is the OS temp directory made absolute and normalized (`resolve(tmpdir())`), so `TMPDIR=/tmp//` or `/tmp/.` names the same directory as `/tmp`; every "directly under the OS temp directory" comparison uses it, never the raw `tmpdir()`. `runCli`, `runInFakeHome` and `fifo.ts` use it; `tests/host-safety.test.ts` pins it.
  - The preload guard's logic lives here too, so the guard and `tests/host-safety.test.ts` share one implementation. `preloadRedirectedEnv(inherited, home, tmuxTmpDir)` returns the guard's variables (`PRELOAD_ENV_NAMES`) computed from an inherited environment, and changes nothing: not `inherited`, not `process.env`, not the file system. `preloadCheckFailures(env)` lists why `env` is not an environment the guard produced, as `PRELOAD_CHECK` labels, or returns `[]`; it only `lstat`s and starts no process. The launch-home refusal lives here as well, shared with `tests/launch-home-guard.test.ts`: `launchTimeHomes()` lists the homes Bun fixed at start-up; `launchHomeRefusal(launchHome, passwdHome, probe)` returns a `LAUNCH_HOME_REFUSAL` label or `undefined` and asks the file system nothing except through `probe` (a `LaunchHomeProbe`: `exists`, `canonical` and `tempDir`; the guard passes `LIVE_LAUNCH_HOME_PROBE`, a test may pass a recording fake); `LAUNCH_HOME_DERIVED_PATHS` lists the `homedir()`-derived paths it follows (among them `XDG_CONFIG_DIR`, `.config`, where the guard points `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` under the new HOME, and `CSCB_XDG_CONFIG_PATH`, `.config/claude-slack-channel-bots`, the crontable's default directory); `launchHomeRefusalMessage(reason, launchHome)` is the guard's one stderr line; `LAUNCH_HOME_REFUSED_EXIT_CODE` is its exit code; `passwdHome()` is the account's passwd home: `passwdHomeFrom` over `/etc/passwd` (read once per process) and the process's uid, or `undefined` when the file cannot be read or the process has no uid. `passwdHomeFrom(passwdText, uid)` is pure: the first line whose uid field equals `String(uid)` exactly decides, giving its home field when the line has at least seven fields and the home is absolute, and `undefined` otherwise; a malformed first match is never passed over for a later line, so the guard fails closed. It is `undefined` too when no line matches or `uid` is not a non-negative safe integer.
  - The preload imports this helper, so whatever the helper loads runs before the refusal: it imports only `node:` builtins (pinned by the load audit in `tests/host-safety.test.ts`). Never import a `src/` module, a package or another test helper here, not even for a type.
- `host-safety-preload.ts`: the `bun test` preload guard (see Host safety under Isolation). `bunfig.toml`, `tests/bunfig.toml` and `tests/integration/bunfig.toml` load it as their first `[test]` preload entry; it exports nothing and no test or helper imports it, and it loads only `node:` builtins and `./host-safe-env.ts`. It first refuses to start, with exit code 78 and one stderr line, under a launch-time home `launchHomeRefusal` refuses. It then makes the HOME directory (`PRELOAD_HOME_PREFIX` under `osTempDir()`), takes the `TMUX_TMPDIR` directory from `childTmuxTmpDir()`, applies `preloadRedirectedEnv` to `process.env` and throws when `preloadCheckFailures` reports anything; all of these come from `host-safe-env.ts`.
- `install-check-fixtures.ts`: fixtures for the install check, its callers and the tests that check versions against the client minimum. Version constants: `SATISFYING_VERSION` (the client-admitted development sentinel below CSCB's numeric floor: the check passes it with the note) and `STALE_VERSION` (below the client minimum: too old), both checked against the installed client's minimum and the floor when the module loads, which throws if either is out of place; `SENTINEL_VERSION` and the re-exported `DEV_SENTINEL_VERSION` (never type the sentinel); `CANNED_BINARY_PATH`, the path every canned result reports by default (equal to the stub resolver's `STUB_RESOLVE_DEFAULT_PATH`, pinned by `tests/agent-director-stub-resolve.test.ts` rather than imported, since the stub helper pulls in the session manager and persona modules); `UNREACHABLE_REASONS`, every `ErrSystemInstallUnreachable` reason agent-director defines in a fixed order, built from a `Record<UnreachableReason, true>` so the compiler holds the set complete. Version-floor JSON builders (`makeVersionFloorJson`, `makeMalformedFloorJson`, `makeMissingFieldFloorJson`). Canned `runInstallCheck` results in its shapes and texts: `cannedSuccessResult(opts)` defaults to `CANNED_BINARY_PATH`, `CLIENT_MIN_VERSION` and `CLIENT_MIN_VERSION` (from `agent-director-versions.ts`) with no note; any success field overrides, a `binaryVersion` below the floor carries `buildInstallCheckPhase1Note(binaryVersion)`, `phase1Note: true` or `false` forces the note on or off, and an explicit `note` wins. `cannedFailureResult(label, opts)` takes an exported label value and builds that label's default detail and message (too old: `STALE_VERSION` against `CLIENT_MIN_VERSION` at `CANNED_BINARY_PATH`, the message from `buildSystemInstallTooOldMessage`); `opts.detail` and `opts.message` replace them, the message otherwise built from the effective detail. The not-found, unreachable and floor-unreadable messages are copies of `src/install-check.ts`'s text, pinned by `tests/install-check.test.ts`, which compares real results whole with the canned ones; where a message names the publishing-host block, the switch-over runbook section or the client-package remedy, the copy builds that part from `src/install-check.ts`'s exports (`PUBLISHING_HOST_BLOCK_POINTER`, `RUNBOOK_SECTION_POINTER`, `CLIENT_PACKAGE_REMEDY`), never a literal. From `src/install-check.ts` it value-imports those three text constants and otherwise imports types only.
- `line-parts.ts`: a line builder's own text around the parts a case cannot rebuild (every asserted line comes from its exported builder, never typed). Hand the builder `LINE_HOLE` (a NUL) for each open part (a thrown value's description with its stack frames, a label the module does not export, a value the case leaves open): `lineParts(build)` answers the builder's text split at each hole, in order (one more part than holes), for matching a line by its head, tail or the words between; `builtAround(build)` answers a pattern of the builder's text before and after its one hole, anything in it. Use these instead of splitting a builder's output at a marker by hand.
- `old-life.ts`: the fixtures and line helpers the old-life hold and wait cases share, over the recovery harness, so none is kept per file: the pre-persona row a hold is begun on (`PRE_PERSONA_ID`, `PRE_PERSONA_LABELS`, `PRE_PERSONA_SESSION`); start-sweep rows and the sweep (`listed(h, key, overrides?)`, a persona's own row as the `list` gives it; `absentRow(h, key, overrides?)`, an absent persona's row in the first persona's directory; `sweepOver(h, rows, config?, isShuttingDown?)`, the sweep as `main()` runs it, answering its result, the stub calls in order and what the first kill met); holds begun by hand (`beginApplyHold(h, key, dirOf?)`, apply step 1's hold on a persona's own row, at `dirOf`'s working directory, the key's own by default, so a case can hold `cscb_<P>` at another persona's directory as a destructive modify that moved P away; `holdOldAt(h, instanceId, oldKey, dirOf)`, an id held at a persona's directory as a start-sweep kill that did not succeed begins it); the old-life gate (`oldLifeGateLine` and `gateLine`, its launch line through `oldLifeHoldLaunchLine`; `gateLinesIn(h)`, the gate lines among the harness's errors; `heldBack(key)`, `spawnForPersona`'s answer for a held persona); the wait's end line (`waitEndLine(instanceId, oldKey, end, armed)` through `oldLifeWaitEndLine`, and `waitEndLinePrefix`, the head every end line of one old row shares); and `settledRetryLinePrefix` (the head of a persona's end-retry settled line). Every label, line and answer comes from `src/`, cut from the builders' own output where a prefix is needed; it keeps no module-scope state. A new old-life case imports these rather than defining its own copy.
- `own-post.ts`: `makeRecordingOwnPostObserver(steps)` returns an `observer` typed from production's `OwnPostObserver`, one ordered `calls` log of every `start` and `end` (`OwnPostCall`), and `enqueue` for later steps. Each `OwnPostStep` chooses an operation with no `ready` (the default), a test-settled `ready` from `holdOwnPostReady()` (`ready`, `resolve`, `reject`), no operation (`start: 'undefined'`), or a throwing `start` or `end` (`throwStart`, `throwEnd`). The log holds raw input content; leak-check the surface's outputs.

  `makeOwnPostHarness(stateDir, options?)` builds one real owner and observer as `src/server.ts` does, over real Thread Memory, queue `lookupSlackKey`, membership and stored-choice readers, with no stubbed reader. Both `owner` and `read` expose captured `pendingOwnPosts`, `unknownOwnPosts`, `operation`, `awaitingUploads`, `memoryOnlyJoins` and `resolvedThreads`; `read.subscribe` forwards owner events. These reads, `memory.unresolvedIntents`, `view(key, channel, root)` and `records(key = 'alpha')` snapshot their results in `captured().returned`, preserving leak evidence after settlement, outcome release or persona forgetting.

  `threads`, `io`, `clock` and `flush` drive memory faults and settlement; `events` and `captured()` collect owner, membership, shared-write, Thread Memory and output-file evidence. Options accept caller-owned started `members` and `queue`, `choices` with their matching `members`, `membership` inputs for a new membership harness, `memory` storage options, an `operationId` factory and `isDryRun`. `prepareMembership(members)` synchronously configures Slack fixtures before helper-owned membership authenticates; `start: false` leaves memory and helper-owned membership initialization to `start()`, which scripts the configured channels, starts membership and scans it.

  Shared-state publication automatically notifies the owner and kicks optional lookups by default. Set `publishSharedState: false` when a case must explicitly call `settleDeferred` or `onSharedStatePublished`; this leaves Thread Memory's own authority subscription intact. With `lookups: true`, the helper also builds the lookup runner as `src/server.ts` does (none in a dry run), over the same owner, Thread Memory, stamp reader, membership connection manager and fake clock. Its own subscription kicks it on `unknown` and `awaiting-thread` events, and `start()` reads and kicks each persona; `lookups` exposes `runner`, `events`, `ownMessage(key, event, identity?)` and `stop()`, with `lookupEvents` in `captured()`.

  `reopen()` closes the current harness and rebuilds it over persisted membership/memory with startup enabled and memory filesystem faults cleared. Call idempotent `close()` before removing scratch: nested cleanup checks leaks before and after shutdown and closes only helper-owned membership/queue. The `tests/own-post.test.ts` adapter supplies two `thread_hybrid` channels, pre-authentication shared identity through `prepareMembership`, scan/eligibility and choice/durability controls, deterministic operation IDs and explicit publication; composition, startup, replay and cleanup use the shared harness. Other consumers include `tests/registry.test.ts`, `tests/persona-destination.test.ts`, `tests/persona-destination-hold.test.ts`, `tests/permission-poller.test.ts`, `tests/persona-notifier.test.ts`, `tests/own-post-lookup.test.ts`, `tests/own-post-recovery.test.ts` (`holdOwnPostReady`) and `tests/server-startup-wiring.test.ts`.
- `pending-row-model.ts`: model authoritative AD pending/live/finished states, launch start, scripted verb outcomes, find-missing judgments and checked launch/kill transitions on the shared fake clock. Drive state changes through AD readings, not terminal content or automatic dialog answers. Keep latch refusal, row provenance and ordinary pending retry coverage.
- `delivery-queue.ts`: `makeQueue(stateDir, options?)`, `seedQueue`, `readQueue`, `queuePath`, `slackInput`, `injectedInput`, `sentRecord`, `deliveredRecord` and `acceptedRecord(seq, input, received_at)`, a Slack input's accepted record as the queue writes it. Pass the caller’s scratch directory and fake clock; seed torn-last-line cases as raw string bytes, which `tornRecord(record, through)` builds from a valid record: its serialized line cut after its `through` field and that field's comma (never valid JSON; it throws when `through` names no field before the record's last, or the cut is not a prefix of the line).

  Reuse these fixtures across queue, routing, interject, cron and reload tests.

  For concurrent acceptance/preparation, assert exact accepted/prepared results, immutable caller views and completion order across queue sizes; stop preparation during cleanup. Check values, serialized bytes, caller mutation isolation, getter effects and publication order through the real owners.

  [Thread Memory performance runs](#thread-memory-performance-runs) measure end-to-end cost: test-44 covers ACK/store latency at 0/10,000/100,000 joins and compaction at 100,000; all membership groups (45/48/51–64) cover membership, faults and recovery at 100,000; test-32 covers latency, concurrent writes and the 2 GiB shard memory cap. These workloads measure the combined paths, without assigning per-copy budgets or unit heap verdicts; a passing unit run supplies no fresh integration evidence.

  `memoryHold(arrived_at, overrides?)` and `postHold(arrived_at, overrides?)` build typed holds; `unknownRootPostHold(arrived_at)` sets `root_unknown`, `HOLD_FIELDS` selects the builder and `heldSlackInput(hold, overrides?)` builds the held Slack acceptance.

  `releasedRecord(seq?, at?)`, `withdrawnRecord(seq?, at?)` and `parkedRecord(seq?, at?)` build resolution records, with withdrawal serialized as `hold-withdrawn`; `fixedRecord`, `refusedRecord` and `noticedRecord` supply the other journal facts.

  Queue, routing and hold suites share these builders. `makeQueue` forwards production options without adding a first-opening callback.
  - `sentRecord(seq = 1, attempt = 1, send_kind = 'text', overrides?)` builds a known `text`, `enter` or `retype` send. `SentRecordOverrides` can replace part, time, session ID, transcript path and EOF size (the receipt byte-window facts) without replacing its kind, sequence, attempt or send kind; omitted fields retain the helper defaults (part one, `at = 1000`, fixture session/path and zero EOF size).

    Supply the caller’s actual scratch transcript and clock/window facts when testing receipts.

    The typed alternative `sentRecord(seq, attempt, { unknown_outcome: true, quarantine, at? })` carries only unknown-outcome evidence, `quarantine: { path, line }` and time (default `at = 1000`), with no fabricated part, send kind, session or transcript facts.
  - `deliveredRecord(seq = 1, at = 1000, { part?, receipt? } = {})` defaults to part one and the fixture path/UUID receipt. A supplied receipt replaces that default entirely: pass its path with UUID, offset (including zero), or both.

    Offset-only credit must acquire no default UUID. Receipt, engine and queue consumers retain independent expected results and deliberate malformed inputs; derive valid inputs from these builders.
- `recovery-harness.ts`: production retry, launch, AD row, pending-rule, latch and live-row-sequence composition over one stub and fake clock. Drive launch/retry/latch/shutdown through the shared harness, advance the injected clock, and await in-flight work. Its routing uses a real shared authority and explicit positive membership; the down-recovery driver preaccepts the original event through the actual queue before replay. The four suites consuming the changed `expectLostMessageReports` path use a named focused selection for this change, not a full-suite claim for every importer. The harness has no startup autoanswer loop. Own-launch fixtures use an authoritative AD launch start inside the call window; pending recovery keeps grace/bound and standard backoff.

- `reload-terms.ts`: `RELOAD_TERMS` and `reloadTermsIn`, the one reload-term list (see Unadvertised Reload Checks).
- `launch-calls.ts`: `observeLaunchCalls(stub, onCall)` wraps the stub's `spawn` and `resume`, reports each verb before delegating, and preserves the stub's result. It performs no directory I/O. Used by session-manager and restart tests.
- `retired-keys.ts`: the retired-key record for tests, built only through `src/retired-keys.ts` (`retiredKeysPath`, `serializeRetiredKeys`, `parseRetiredKeys`). `writeRetiredKeysRecord(stateDir, entries)` writes the record holding `entries` (by key: `cause`, and optionally `retiredAt` and `mark`, `true` for `SAMPLE_NEW_LIFE_BEGUN_AT`, a timestamp, or `false`, `null` or unset for none) and returns its path; it refuses, writing nothing, the real home and any directory not under the OS temp directory (the temp directory itself included). `readRetiredKeysRecord(stateDir)` returns the record as the module's parser reads it, or `null` when there is no file; it throws naming the file and the parser's problem when the parser refuses the file, and rethrows any other read failure. `retiredKeysRecordOf(entries)` is the same entries as the in-memory record, for comparing with a store's snapshot. `SAMPLE_RETIRED_AT` and `SAMPLE_NEW_LIFE_BEGUN_AT` are the default times, and `RFC3339_UTC` matches the form the server writes a time in, for a `retired_at` or a mark the server wrote. Tests never hand-write the record: no JSON literal of it and no file name typed as a string; a malformed record is the serialiser's output altered.
- `runbooks.ts`: the runbooks' titles and block headings (docs/migration.md), the form of their step headings, and the one reader of a runbook's steps (ruling Q13); tests take every one of them from here. `ROLLBACK_RUNBOOK_SECTION_TITLE` is the rollback section's title and `REFUSAL_BLOCK_HEADING` the switch-over runbook's refusal-block heading, both defined here because no `src/` code reads them. Two runbook names live in `src/ad-version-gate.ts`, and tests import them from there: the switch-over section's own title, `PHASE1_RUNBOOK_SECTION_TITLE`, which every refusal and note reads, and the publishing-host block heading, `PUBLISHING_HOST_BLOCK_HEADING`, which the install check's not-found message and not-found and below-client-minimum diagnostics name (the startup gate's not-found message names `RUNBOOK_SECTION_POINTER` instead). `stepHeadingPrefix(n)` builds the start of step n's heading title and `stepNumberOf(title)` reads the step number back (`undefined` for a title that is not a step's), so no reader re-types the form. The step reader: `runbookSteps(section, { count?, level?, name? })` reads a runbook section's body (its heading line excluded, as `findSection` and `requiredSection` return it) and returns one `RunbookStep` per step, in order: its `number`, its heading `title` as written, its heading's 0-based `line` in the section and its `text` as written (up to the next heading of its level or higher). Steps are found by number through `stepNumberOf`, never by title, at `level` (default: the section's shallowest heading level); `count` defaults to the highest step number found. A missing, duplicated, out-of-order, beyond-the-count or step-0 heading throws naming the step, after `<name>: ` when given; a section with no step fails as step 1 missing. Its users: `shipped-docs.test.ts` (every switch-over and rollback carrier, through `readRunbookCarrier`, and the switch-over step ranges), `fmk-switch-over-runbook.test.ts` (the runbook steps Test 13 must follow) and, in the image, `tests/integration/fixtures/switch-over.ts` (the step titles Test 13 enters). The Markdown contract it carries: each runbook is a `###` section under `## Migration`, its blocks and steps are headings one level below it, and each step heading's title starts with `stepHeadingPrefix(n)`. Pure. Its load path is image-safe: it imports only `markdown.ts`, which imports nothing, and nothing from `src/`, `agent-director` or any package, so it loads in the `/ci` image's `/tests`, which has no `src/` or `node_modules`; `shipped-docs.test.ts` guards that load path (see its row).

An exit-code entry is a header line `# <code> SR-x.y …` with its continuation lines, and its code column is a number or `--` for a step with no exit code of its own (`publish-prepare.sh`'s). `headerExitCodes(header)` answers the numbered codes in order, `--` entries left out; `headerEntries(header, sr)` answers every entry for one SR id, matched as a whole word (`` finds no ``), each a `HeaderEntry` (`code`, `null` for `--`, and `text` as written); `joinCommentLines(text)` joins an entry's lines into one for a phrase check. both read the source with one small lexer that follows string literals, templates nested inside `${…}` to any depth, and regex literals, taking a `/` for a regex from the token before it (a punctuator or a keyword such as `return`), so a quote or backtick inside a regex or a nested template, or a `//` inside any literal, never throws it out of step; call and `main()` locators such as `callsOf`, `callArguments`, `splitTopLevel`, `objectProperties`, `mainBody` and `importSource`, whose bracket scanners skip string and template literals, nested templates included, but not regex literals or type arguments; the start's anchor `startResolution` (see server.ts wiring and call order under Stubbing External Dependencies); `objectProperties(text, spread?)` resolves a bare `...name` spread through the optional resolver, nested spreads included, merges its properties in and throws `duplicate property` on an override, and without a resolver any spread still throws `not a plain property`), and the runtime import walk: `srcModules()` reads every `src/*.ts` module's comment-stripped code by file name, `importedSpecifiers(code)` lists the specifiers a module imports or re-exports (static or dynamic), `runtimeSpecifiers(code)` drops the whole-statement type-only ones, and `runtimeLoads(modules, entry)` follows `entry`'s runtime imports transitively, answering each module reached with the import chain that reaches it and each package or builtin loaded on the way (`RuntimeLoads`); it throws on a relative import that names no `src/` module, so an import the walk cannot follow fails the audit rather than being skipped. It lists `dir`'s own mtime, then every entry depth first with names sorted, each with its kind, its size (or, for a symlink, its `readlink` target) and its mtime. Its launch-timeout legs use persona-scoped `launch-reply-timeout` faults: run the real AD launch, then lose only its successful response after pane identity is persisted. Pass collisions and other errors through without consuming the rule; preserve the 23-second report delay, G=60, retry timing and combined polling deadline. Assert that the hold and launch-timeout recovery make no automatic `read-pane` or `send-keys` calls.

Runbook and shipped-doc audits keep the guide synchronized; frozen 0.11.0 release copies remain unchanged.

### Delivery engine and model fixtures

Use the production engine/gate policy with injected AD rows, typed refusals, durable queue and fake clock. First send, retry, reconnect text and Enter require fresh AD `waiting` and the existing non-screen guards. Assert that a change between text and Enter blocks the latter, preserves queued work and retains retry/backoff. Test independent persona clients and lifecycle cancellation.

For ordinary in-flight sends without recorded AD uncertainty, including reopened unrefused sends, assert receipt and fresh AD reads before durable `send_kind: enter` recovery after backoff, then the receipt window and a full retype only if an exact receipt remains absent. Cover a restart between text and Enter and a restart during a retry episode. A queue `ad-input-unconfirmed` block or per-persona `uncertain` hold instead requires receipt-only custody without automatic Enter/retype, including after a failed AD read or an interrupted queue-block append after the hold was saved.

Test observed new-launch release into the normal guards, and exact late-receipt settlement separately from release; see [Uncertain input and retained delivery](../skills/debug-slack-channel-bots/SKILL.md#uncertain-input-and-retained-delivery). Receipts confirm only CSCB's full own text; native queue, turn, task and compaction records supply no state. No screen fixtures, native glyph classifiers or leftover-text cleanup tests belong in CSCB.

Drive a working-to-waiting cycle with exact receipts across 20 FIFO items and 20 multipart parts; require prompt progress after each durable `delivered` append. Cover failed delivered-append retry and launch replacement so `receiptWorking` cannot leak to another part or launch or clear before durability.

For test 33's restart reset, assert durable Enter/retype/Enter/retype records, matching part/session/launch and first-waiting evidence, actual persona key calls, and the swallowed text fault's process ID. Check the 10-second first stage and both 30-second stages separately, including the guarded text-to-Enter delay of at least 500 ms. A single less-than-60-second text-gap assertion cannot represent these two recovery stages.

For recovery Enter returning AD `GONE`, reopen a durable queue with ordinary in-flight `sent` work and no AD uncertainty evidence, then drive the production engine and checked live-row sequence together. Keep distinct cases with actual uncertainty evidence held on the same live launch, plus exact late-receipt and observed-new-launch release controls.

Cover restart delay zero, an ordinary restart already pending, stale `waiting`, a refused checked kill, local holds and cancellation; require lease release before the detached handoff, no keys during the sequence, conversation-preserving resume and exact-receipt FIFO drain. These adapter regressions extend no TLC claim.

For retained `GONE`, exercise both normal ticks and reconnect retries: require a fresh AD read despite the row cache, reject an unannounced session or launch-timestamp replacement, retain work on refused reads, and recheck guards changed during the read. Hold a read in flight to prove reconnect cannot start a second read or handoff; then release it and require eventual checked recovery. Use `KILL_RETRY_TRIES` for exhausted-kill coverage.

For fresh `ErrSpawnNotFound` after retained `GONE`, drive the real retry controller with permanently absent `get`/`status` rows and restart delay zero; require exact-receipt FIFO drain without a stale kill. Cover a replacement appearing before the controller acts, rejected transfer, guard/launch changes during the absence read and status refusal preserving normal backoff. Exercise the actual server callback: only `RAN` and `ARMED` transfer ownership; `RUNNING` and `CLOSED` retain evidence. Hold an overlapping pending-only retry on an older `waiting` read, then require eventual recovery through tick and reconnect. Accepted transfers must not repeatedly bypass the controller’s backoff.

Conformance renders AD observations and exact receipt facts through production policy. The [model README](../spec/tla/README.md#verification-scope) distinguishes 84 delivery rows (12 positive exhaustive, 42 exhaustive controls and 30 simulations) and eight auxiliary checks. The portable corpus has 285 traces and 42,643 states, 40 negative controls and 116 frozen model/config/helper inputs, including the finite 19-state/18-edge pullback and 5-state/4-edge reconnect prefixes. Its executed action/fault coverage and the prefixes’ limited proof scope are listed there. The [coverage inventory](../tests/fixtures/delivery-traces/coverage.json) binds the current fixtures, input hashes and independent proofs; local `certification: false` establishes no scheduler certificate. Keep no-loss/FIFO/durable queue and at-least-once controls. See [reproduction commands](../spec/tla/README.md#reproducing-verification) for offline validation and separate checker workflows.

Real-agent action waits use AD state. Retain independent exact transcript input/output assertions, but omit pane text from diagnostics. Test outcome-only probes by AD success/error class; native display compatibility belongs to agent-director.

For replacement waits, require AD to report a new native session before asserting replacement; an old live row and historical connection log cannot finish that wait. For pending-window fixtures, use an explicit bounded report delay and AD transition records rather than assuming a one-second sampler sees every state. Release a persistent lost-create fault only after its exact timeout and pending-get proof, so the next launch can succeed under the normal AD-checked sequence.

Audit ordinary reconnect text through its guarded successful Enter, retaining generic text/Enter and validated no-input Enter refusals after the unwedge mark; generic refusals retain only plain intent and require Enter-only retries without retyping. Native ambiguous text or Enter stays held without that automatic continuation; require no further keys even when the fresh AD read fails and after durable reload. Select both call and outcome streams through that same success, with matching AD outcomes and unchanged launch/session identity. Exercise the actual scenario selector with refusal-boundary controls. The Codex gate must stop all observation owners and verify AD retirement before spawning in the shared workdir.

### Credentials Fixtures and Leak Checks

Any test that touches Slack tokens or a persona credentials file uses the shared helper `tests/test-helpers/credentials.ts`. It builds fake tokens that all carry one marker, `LEAK_SENTINEL`, and checks captured output for that marker or any token-like value. A leak then fails a test instead of reaching a log.

| Export | Use it for |
|--------|------------|
| `LEAK_SENTINEL` | The marker every fake token embeds. It uses identifier characters only, so an error that quotes an identifier quotes the whole sentinel. Refer to the constant; never copy its value into a test. |
| `BOT_TOKEN_PREFIX`, `APP_TOKEN_PREFIX` | The Slack token prefixes, for building fakes and for asserting on rule text. A bare prefix is not a token. |
| `fakeToken(prefix, suffix?)` | One fake token built at runtime: the prefix, the digit `1`, the sentinel, then `-` and the suffix when one is given. The digit after the dash gives it a real token's shape, not just `TOKEN_LIKE`'s. Use distinct suffixes to tell two fakes apart; pass a wrong prefix or none for bad-prefix cases. |
| `sentinelInMessage(label, prefix?, marker?)` | The sentinel as a test error's *message* carries it: `fakeToken(prefix, label)`, a space, then `sentinelTicketUrl(STUB_WSS_ORIGIN, marker)`. `prefix` defaults to `BOT_TOKEN_PREFIX` (`APP_TOKEN_PREFIX` for a Socket Mode leg), `label` tells two fakes apart (`''` for none), and `marker` is the ticket (a Slack stub passes its `leakMarker`). Wrap it as the message needs, e.g. `` `failed (${sentinelInMessage('x')})` ``. |
| `REDACTED_SENTINEL_TAIL` | What `sentinelInMessage(…)` reads as after `redactSlackLogText` (`<redacted-token> <redacted-url>`), built from the redactor's own placeholders. Assert the logged `message="…"` holds it in the same wrapping as the thrown message. |
| `sentinelTicketUrl(origin?, marker?)`, `STUB_WSS_ORIGIN` | A Socket Mode WebSocket URL `<origin>/link/?ticket=<marker>`, the shape a real connect error quotes; `origin` defaults to `STUB_WSS_ORIGIN` (the Slack stub's `wss://` origin) and `marker` to `LEAK_SENTINEL`. For a URL on its own; a message uses `sentinelInMessage`. |
| `withoutName(captured, name, key)` | A copy of `captured` with a persona name and its key replaced by `<name>` / `<key>` (the longer first), with the same traversal as `assertNoLeak`: `assertNoLeak(withoutName(captured, name, key))`. Only for runs whose output legitimately holds a token-shaped name (built with `fakeToken`, so it carries the sentinel); anything else token-like, a credential value included, still fails. |
| `makeCredentials(overrides?)` | A credentials object. By default it is valid (exactly `bot_token` and `app_token`, distinct fakes); an override set to `undefined` removes that key, and any other override adds or replaces one. |
| `writeCredentialsFile(dir, name?, overrides?)` | Writes a credentials file with mode 0600 inside `dir` and returns its path. An object override merges over the valid defaults; a string override is the whole file content, for non-JSON or non-object cases. `dir` is required and `name` must stay inside it. |
| `writtenFile(path)` | Marks a file or directory the code under test wrote, so `assertNoLeak` checks its content. This is the only way to check a file: a plain string is always checked as text, never read as a path. |
| `TOKEN_LIKE`, `isTokenLike(text)` | The one definition of token-like that `assertNoLeak` applies: `xox` plus a lower-case letter, or `xapp`, then a dash and a letter or digit, with a boundary before the prefix (the start of the text or anything but an ASCII letter or digit). A bare prefix in rule text, a word such as "Xoxo bot" or a prefix glued to a word (`inboxapp-bot`) doesn't match. It needs no digit after the dash (a prefix followed by a letter is flagged too), so `assertNoLeak` errs on the strict side; `tests/persona-identity.test.ts` pins its rows. Not global: build a global copy from `TOKEN_LIKE.source` to find every occurrence. The secrecy audit uses the same matcher. |
| `assertNoLeak(captured, label?)` | Fails if the sentinel (any case) or a token-like value appears anywhere in `captured`. Strings, errors (message, stack, properties, `cause`, aggregated errors), arrays, objects, maps, sets, buffers and `writtenFile` marks are all checked, recursively. |

Rules:

- **Fakes only.** Tests use only tokens from `fakeToken`, `makeCredentials` or `writeCredentialsFile`, so every token embeds `LEAK_SENTINEL`. No test file contains a token literal, not even a fake one; build it at runtime from the prefix constants.
- **Check everything captured.** Every test that handles credentials runs `assertNoLeak` over its captured log lines, errors and results, including rejected calls and failure paths. Pass them together as one object so a failure names the leaking item (for example `captured.lines[2]`). Wrap any file the code wrote in `writtenFile`. A test of a log line lists (a latch, re-check round, retry timer, `tmux-unresponsive`, `ad-config-malformed`, kill-try, live-row sequence, old-life, retired-key, settings or version re-check line) runs `assertNoLeak` over the lines it captured too, even when it handles no credentials, with the line's text taken from its `src/` builder; where the line quotes agent-director, its error's description carries `sentinelInMessage(…)`.
- **Override the token environment.** Nothing in `src/` reads `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` or `SLACK_APP_TOKEN`, so tests normally leave them alone. A suite that sets either (for example to show that `start` or the connection manager ignores them) sets both to fakes for its whole run and restores the previous values afterwards, so an ambient real token can never reach a failure message.
- **Log errors by description.** Code under test logs a thrown value on a Slack or agent-director path through `describeThrownValue` (see the engineering guide's Error Handling), which keeps the message only as `message="…"` after `redactSlackLogText`. Log lines keep the redacted message, so a test error's message carries `LEAK_SENTINEL` only through `sentinelInMessage` (inside a `fakeToken()` and a `?ticket=` URL, the shapes redaction removes); its other properties (headers, `data`, `original`, bodies, extra fields CSCB must never read) carry it bare. The case asserts the line holds its type, safe `code` or `errName` and the redacted message (`REDACTED_SENTINEL_TAIL` in the message's wrapping), then runs `assertNoLeak` over everything logged. A line that skips redaction, or a redactor that loses either pattern, then fails `assertNoLeak`; a bare sentinel in a message would survive redaction, so it proves nothing about the describer.
- **Token-shaped persona names.** A persona name may be shaped like a Slack token ( no format rule), and a test builds one with `fakeToken()`, so it carries the sentinel. A run whose output must hold that name is checked with `assertNoLeak(withoutName(captured, name, key))`, never left out of the check: the name and key are masked and everything else, credential values included, is still checked.
- **Why the failure is safe.** `assertNoLeak` reports which item leaked and whether it held the sentinel or a token-like value, never the leaked text. Rule text such as "must start with" a bare prefix passes.

Isolation applies to credentials files, crontables, cron logs and working-directory fixtures exactly as it does to config files:

- Create them only under the test's own `mkdtempSync` directory, pass every path explicitly, and remove the directory in `afterEach`. `writeCredentialsFile` has no default location and refuses a name that escapes `dir`.
- Never read or write `~/.claude/channels/slack`, `~/.config/claude-slack-channel-bots` or `~/.config/agent-director`, and never point a credentials path at the real home.
- To test code that falls back to `os.homedir()`, use `runInFakeHome` from `tests/test-helpers/fake-home-subprocess.ts`. Setting `process.env.HOME` in a test doesn't work: Bun fixes `os.homedir()` from the launch-time HOME, so the helper launches a fresh child with the caller's scratch home.

  Choose mutually exclusive module inputs `{ modulePath: absolutePath, call, input }` or script inputs `{ scriptPath: absolutePath, args?: readonly string[] }`. Module calls may await and have imported `mod` and parsed JSON `input` in scope; script mode executes the actual entry with `import.meta.main` intact and `process.argv.slice(2)` equal to `args` (empty by default).

  Both modes require `home` and accept `stateDir?`, `env?`, `timeoutMs?` and `tools?`. Use an existing writable caller-owned scratch home for script mode's temporary preload; omit `stateDir` to leave `SLACK_STATE_DIR` unset and exercise the default under that home. Pass explicit extras such as `TMPDIR` or `SCENARIO_ROOT` through `env`, state through `stateDir`, and module data through `input`.

  The single spawn starts Bun by absolute `process.execPath` and takes its environment directly from `hostSafeChildEnv`: fake HOME, checked tool PATH, fenced `TMUX_TMPDIR` and explicit extras. Tools default to `FAKE_HOME_CHILD_TOOLS` (`bun`, `sh`); `tools: []` gives an empty tool PATH while Bun still starts by absolute path. No ambient credentials or other parent environment values are copied.

  Results are `{ status, stdout, payloadStdout, stderr, observedHomedir }`; assert `observedHomedir === home` before trusting status, output or files. The same child prints `HOMEDIR::<path>` before the module call or script entry runs; raw `stdout` retains the line, while `payloadStdout` removes only its first occurrence. Compare payload-only output, including an entry's empty refusal output, through `payloadStdout`.

  The helper refuses the account's real home and the launch-time home before preload creation or spawning; `hostSafeChildEnv` rejects homes/tool directories holding agent-director. Timeout, signal and spawn errors throw; `timeoutMs` defaults to `FAKE_HOME_SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT_MS` (30 s), and ordinary nonzero exits return their status for assertions. Script preloads are removed in `finally`; callers remove their own scratch trees in test cleanup, as `tests/shared-channel-upgrade-fixtures.test.ts` and `tests/legacy-reply-hook-cleanup.test.ts` demonstrate.
- Code that can call `recordStartupError` writes `startup-errors.log` under `SLACK_STATE_DIR`, which the preload guard points under its shared temp HOME (unset, it would default to a path under the launch-time home). Point `SLACK_STATE_DIR` at the test's own temp directory for the whole file in `beforeEach` and restore the environment (the preload's value) in `afterEach`, as `tests/legacy-reply-hook-cleanup.test.ts` does. A test that reads the log points it at its own directory.
- When a test compares real paths (for example a symlinked credentials file shared with another persona), resolve the temp directory with `realpathSync` first; the OS temp directory may itself be a symlink.

Permission cases (an unreadable credentials file, an unreadable or unsearchable working directory) inject a failing operation through the check's file-system seam, so they pass under root in docker CI. The credentials seam is `openFile`, `fstatFile`, `readFileFd`, `closeFile` and `realpath`; the working-directory seam is `stat`, `access` and `realpath`, and the combined `PersonaBringUpFs` carries both. For an unreadable credentials file, make `openFile` or `readFileFd` throw an errno-style error (`EACCES`, `EPERM`, `EIO`). To test a credentials path that is not a regular file (a FIFO or a device), make `fstatFile` report `isFile()` false, assert `readFileFd` is never called and `closeFile` is called for the opened descriptor. Because the real open is non-blocking, a real FIFO, directory or `/dev/zero` is also safe to use as a control. The config reader (`readPersonaConfigBytes`, used for `config.json` and the last-applied record) has the same seam, `PersonaConfigFs`, and the same rule, reached through `configFs` on the reload controller and `readAppliedPersonaConfig`. A durable write whose directory open or fsync fails after the rename (`DurableWriteUnsyncedError`), or a durable delete whose directory open or fsync fails after the unlink (`DurableUnlinkUnsyncedError`), is driven through the `DurableWriteFs` seam. The reload detection tick's credentials reads take the same `CredentialsFs` seam, through `opts.credentialsFs` on a reload harness run. A variant that uses real permission bits is marked `test.skipIf(isRoot)`, with the reason in the test name. Restore any mode a test changed before `afterEach` removes the directory.

A test that could hang on a blocking open or read (a real FIFO with no writer) runs the risky call in a child `bun` process (`spawnSync` with a `timeout`, typically 10 s, and its `env` a direct `hostSafeChildEnv` call) and asserts the child was not killed (`child.signal` is null), with a per-test timeout above that bound. A test timeout can't interrupt a blocking synchronous call, so in-process a regression would hang the whole suite instead of failing one test. Make the FIFO with `makeFifo` from `tests/test-helpers/fifo.ts` (the reload harness's `h.makeFifo` delegates to it), never by spawning `mkfifo` yourself, and skip the case where `mkfifo` is missing (`test.skipIf(!mkfifoAvailable())`, the reason in the test name). The reload harness (`tests/test-helpers/reload-harness.ts`, its `mkfifoAvailable` and `h.makeFifo`) is the reference.

#### Secrecy Audit

`tests/secrecy-audit.test.ts` enforces these rules across the suite, and the describe-don't-echo logging rule across `src/` (closing audit, ). It reads files under `tests/` and `src/` only, comment-stripped, and anchors on content, never line numbers.

Its child-environment audit uses the TypeScript AST over every TypeScript file under `src/`: process starts and CLI adapters must carry an environment built by `childEnv`, and both executable entries must call `scrubProcessEnv` before dispatch. Planted unfiltered calls, option spreads and missing/late/comment-only/literal-only scrubs prove the rules reject violations. The CLI adapter checks follow the filtered argument from the dependency call through the production spawn or credentials runner.

- **Which suites it covers.** A suite touches a secret-bearing surface when it imports a function/value (including aliases, value namespaces and dynamic imports) from a `SOURCE_SURFACES` module; type-only imports and SCREAMING_CASE constants do not count. The source patterns are `src/channel-membership.ts`, `src/channel-membership-scan.ts`, `src/channel-membership-readiness.ts`, `src/channel-membership-evidence.ts`, `src/codex-config-keys.ts`, `src/config.ts`, `src/shared-channels.ts`, `src/shared-state-reports.ts`, `src/shared-recovery.ts`, `src/test-mcp-drop.ts`, `src/test-measurements.ts`, `src/persona-credentials.ts`, `src/persona-bringup.ts`, `src/persona-bringup-controller.ts`, `src/persona-slack-*.ts`, `src/persona-connections.ts`, `src/persona-connection-errors.ts`, `src/persona-web-api-watch.ts`, `src/persona-diagnostics.ts`, `src/persona-start.ts`, `src/persona-lifecycle.ts`, `src/slack-log-redaction.ts`, `src/reaction-log-fields.ts`, `src/reload*.ts`, `src/registry.ts`, `src/session-manager.ts`, `src/restart.ts`, `src/permission-poller.ts`, `src/permission-click-handler.ts`, `src/persona-notifier.ts`, `src/notice-correction.ts`, `src/persona-destination*.ts`, `src/health-check.ts`, `src/cli.ts`, `src/cli-teardown.ts`, `src/agent-director-template.ts`, `src/ad-error-class.ts`, `src/ad-settings.ts`, `src/unavailable-retry.ts`, `src/persona-episodes.ts`, `src/outage-state.ts`, `src/conflict-latch.ts`, `src/checked-kill.ts`, `src/kill-retry.ts`, `src/kill-failure-alert.ts`, `src/live-row-sequence.ts`, `src/old-life-wait.ts`, `src/pane-read.ts`, `src/invalid-flags-hold.ts`, `src/pending-row.ts`, `src/persona-routing.ts`, `src/clear-latch.ts`, `src/state-dir-migration.ts`, `src/channel-delivery-attempt.ts`, `src/channel-delivery.ts`, `src/thread-memory.ts`, `src/own-post-lookup.ts`, `src/thread-memory-reports.ts`, `src/own-post.ts`, `src/file-upload-observation.ts`. Imports of the named exports in `HELPER_SURFACES`, or a Slack stub `leakMarker`, also require coverage; that map includes shared authority/recovery, Thread Memory, own-post, population/configuration and upgrade fixture builders. Keep the audit’s map as the authority for individual helper exports.
- **What a covered suite must do.** Import `assertNoLeak` from `tests/test-helpers/credentials.ts` and call it over its captured logs, errors, written files and tool results, or the audit fails naming the suite and why it counts as touching. A suite that builds `makeReloadHarness` must pass a run's `captured()` to it.
- **Exemptions.** A suite that matches but has no secret-bearing surface (nothing it logs, throws, returns or writes can hold a token) goes in the audit's `EXEMPT` map with a one-line reason. An exemption with no reason, for a missing file, for a suite that no longer touches, or for one that now calls `assertNoLeak` fails as stale; remove it. The named legs (`config`, `persona-connections`, `reload`, `reload-apply`) can't be exempted.
- **Literals.** No file under `tests/`, helpers, fixtures and scripts included, may hold a token-like value, and `LEAK_SENTINEL`'s value may appear only in the credentials helper. Build near-miss strings from the prefix constants (for example `BOT_TOKEN_PREFIX.slice(0, 3)`) as `tests/persona-identity.test.ts` does.
- **A new source module** that reads config or credentials, builds Slack clients or runs reload, or whose lines or kept state carry agent-director or Slack failure text, belongs in `SOURCE_SURFACES`, with a reason; an entry with no reason, or one matching no module under `src/`, fails as stale. To pin which imports of a module count, feed import snippets to the audit's own `touchReasonsOf(file, code)`, as the conflict latch's cases do; a new helper that builds tokens, credentials or config files belongs in `HELPER_SURFACES`. `src/live-row-sequence.ts` is one such surface (its step lines carry described agent-director failure text, and its kill results keep kill-failure descriptions raw): its functions touch, its constants and types alone do not, and every suite that touches it, `tests/live-row-sequence.test.ts` among them, calls `assertNoLeak` with no exemption. The shared-choice adapter is another: a suite touches through it when it has a value import from `src/channel-delivery.ts` that is not a SCREAMING_CASE constant (a function, renamed or not, a value namespace or a dynamic `import()`), or imports `writeChannelDeliveryRecord`, the choice-seeding helper export in `HELPER_SURFACES` (the helper's `readChannelDeliveryRecord`, `declarationOf` and `SAMPLE_SET_AT` do not touch). Every such suite, `tests/channel-delivery.test.ts` among them, calls `assertNoLeak` with no exemption. `tests/server-startup-wiring.test.ts` imports the module only as a type (`import type * as …`), so it does not touch.
- **Named legs.** `config` must reject a persona entry holding a fake token under `bot_token` and under `app_token` and one with a computed, token-named key; `persona-connections` must assert `attachOriginalToWebAPIRequestError` false on a socket client's `clientOptions` and on a Web API client's own options, drive `createUnhandledRejectionHandler` and keep its `rejected Web API calls` block; `reload` and `reload-apply` must leak-check a run's `captured()`. Renaming those rows or blocks fails the audit.
- **Source audit.** Every log call under `src/` (a console method, or `log`, `logFailure`, `logViaDeps`, `logDeps` (the click handler's log sink), `safeLog` (the persona episodes' guarded log), `recordStartupError` or `fatal`, bare or on an object) is checked for raw error text: a caught error passed as an argument, interpolated, read for its `message` or `stack`, or handed to a function that is not a safe describer (`String(err)`), an `errDescription` not through `redactSlackLogText`, or an `errName` not checked by `isSafeIdentifier`. A message is allowed only inside a safe describer call: every describer call, its arguments included, is replaced by an empty string literal before the rules run (a placeholder no name can match, so a local that shares a placeholder's name cannot taint the described calls), so `redactSlackLogText(err.message)` or `describeLogMessage(err.message)` passes while a bare `err.message` beside it is flagged. A caught error is a `catch` or `.catch(…)` binding, a name like `e`, `err`, `error` or `<word>Err`, or a name set from a raw use of one. The safe describers are listed in `SAFE_DESCRIBERS` (`describeThrownValue`, `describeThrownValueWithoutStack`, `describeLogMessage`, `describeSlackCallFailure`, `describeAgentDirectorFailure`, `describeReportedAdFailure`, `describeAdFailureForLog`, `describeCliFailure`, `describeRefreshFailure`, `redactSlackLogText`, `isSafeIdentifier`, `slackPlatformReason`, `errnoSuffix`, and `launchTimeoutFormOf`, which returns only one of CSCB's fixed launch-timeout form constants or `undefined`, never error text), each of which must still be declared under `src/`; a local sink that passes its error only through one is a describing wrapper and not itself a sink. The rule table is pinned by snippet checks, positive and negative.
- **The allow-list.** A deliberate exception (a path that is not a Slack or agent-director one, or text CSCB wrote; see the engineering guide's Error Handling) goes in `RAW_ERROR_ALLOWED` as a file, an anchor (a stable fragment of the call's text, never a line number) and a reason. An entry with no reason, for a missing file or matching no flagged call fails as stale. Fix a new finding by describing the error, not by adding an entry, unless the path really is one of those exceptions.

### Operator review fixtures and diagnostics

`tests/test-helpers/shared-channels.ts` exports `applicationState(input)` for a parsed state or authority bytes: it removes only envelope revision and operator-review metadata, retaining applied/source/identity/intent facts. `activationRecord(bytes, path)` validates the exact consumed outcome at the current revision, selecting activation among metadata writes.

`sharedRecoveryRequest` uses production format/hash/base64/parser for restore/replace fixtures; no supplied snapshot can authorize restoration. `initialSharedState(stateDir, input?, threadHybridSince?)`, `makeSharedAuthority(stateDir, input?, deps?)`, `sharedChannelPath`, `readSharedState` and `writeSharedState` build, validate and persist the sole envelope.

`FIXTURE_THREAD_HYBRID_SINCE_PREFIX` names the fixture prefix; `fixtureThreadHybridSince(after?)` mints deterministic fresh values beyond a reopened state; `withThreadMemoryCreated(state, keys, path?)` and `malformedThreadMemoryMarkers(state)` build validated markers and invalid variants. Shared recovery, membership, reload and Thread Memory suites use them.

`SHARED_CHANNEL_IDS` names primary/secondary/private, numbered additional channels and future/foreign/forged inputs; select the intended population rather than treating every named negative input as an upgrade channel. `channelPopulation(count, offset = 0)` builds deterministic IDs with the shared delivery cycle.

`withIndependentDestination(persona: PersonaInput): PersonaInput` derives a repeatable destination from persona name, credentials_file and working_directory, replacing channels and permission_prompts together. Reload tests use this shared helper so distinct identity replacements stay independent.

`scanMembershipEventId(scan, channel, member = true)` names positive/absent scan records; `applyMembershipPage(authority, key, channels, scan, identity = 'app')` seeds a page through production membership application and durable transactions. `retainedScanHistory(authority, key = 'alpha')` performs five two-channel reconciliations, with secondary absent in the last two, then reads through the production parser.

`RETAINED_SCAN_EVENTS` independently names the expected beginning, leave and latest records. Channel-delivery tests mutate this valid output for malformed-history checks; never handwrite a parallel envelope.

See [Membership fixtures and evidence](#membership-fixtures-and-evidence) for live discovery and chronology.

For review-history retention, `withPreRuleReviewOutcomes(state, earlier, path?)` returns `state` with every outcome the `earlier` production states recorded appended after its own, each at its last saved status: a history saved before outcomes were pruned, validated through the production serializer and parser (`path`, default `'fixture-authority'`, names it in parser errors). `botAttemptAtReviewOutcome(state, fingerprint)` moves a production state's first real bot application's start onto that saved outcome's revision; it bypasses the validating writer, so that shared position is the one broken relation for a readability check.

For recovery retention, `stagedRecoveryOf(state)` returns a staged record and `activationOf(state)` an active record's activation, each throwing on the other phase or none. `activatedIdentity(stage, { fingerprint, order })` builds the exact record an activation leaves, independently of production's `recoveryIdentity`.

`foreignRecoveryRequests(request, evidence, input)` returns three valid requests differing from `request` only in request ID, action or evidence hash; a restoration turned replacement chooses `input`. `changedReplacementRequest(request)` keeps a replacement request's identity and adds a final newline to its chosen input, so only whole-request equality tells the two apart. `repairOriginals()` returns two distinct accepted originals in FIFO order (different keys, text, channels and thread context) as `slackInput` overrides, since importing `slackInput` into the helper module would make an import cycle.

`seriesRecoveryId(n)` and `seriesDamage(n)` give fixed-width IDs and damaged bytes for a repair series, and `numericWidth(bytes)` sums the decimal width of every number in saved JSON, the allowance for a series' size bound. `stagedRecoveryMissingBytes(stage)` and `malformedActiveRecoveries(active, stage)` return labelled unreadable states derived from production states, bypassing the validating writer: a stage missing each byte field it needs, or an activation with a dropped field put back or emptied, a surplus field, broken identity grammar or a broken link to its consumed outcome.

Use `reload-request.ts` exports `REVIEW_REQUEST_FORMAT`, `REVIEW_REQUEST_SUFFIX`, `REVIEW_REQUEST_INVALID`, `REVIEW_REQUEST_RECORDED`, `REVIEW_REQUEST_STORAGE`, `reviewRequestDiagnostic` and `reviewIntentLine`. `reload-review.ts` exports `RELOAD_REVIEW_RECOVERY`, `RELOAD_REVIEW_OUTCOME`, `reviewRecoveryLine`, `reviewOutcomeLine`, `reviewRecoveredBringUpFailedLine` and `reviewRecoveredLifecycleFailedLine`. Render channel effects through `reviewedChannelLine` and the import-free `REVIEW_OMISSION_CLAUSE`, `REVIEW_FUTURE_CLAUSE`, `REVIEW_RESET_CLAUSE`, `REVIEW_RETENTION_CLAUSE`; never copy diagnostics into consumers. Confirmation revalidation observes revocation without metadata writes; failed persistence must retain revocation through input reversion.

### Fixture assignments

`_assignFixture` in `tests/test-helpers/shared-channels.ts` constructs fixture state through the supplied live authority's real `transact`. The caller owns that authority and its scratch directory; this helper opens no second authority and supplies no bot authorization, membership/attempt evidence or reviewed operator application.

```typescript
_assignFixture(
  authority: SharedChannelAuthority,
  key: string,
  incarnation: string,
  channel: string,
  delivery: DeliveryMode,
  expectedRevision: number,
  threadHybridSince: () => string,
): SharedMutationResult
```

All seven inputs are required, with no defaults: supply the persona key/current incarnation, a valid channel and delivery, the expected authority revision and the fixture's retained mint. It returns synchronously as `{ kind: 'applied' | 'stale' | 'failed' | 'unresolved', revision }`: obsolete incarnations, revision mismatch and reentrancy are stale; unreadable/review-held authority is unresolved; invalid input or a definite write failure fails. An uncertain write leaves the authority unreadable and returns unresolved without publishing.

A successful call takes exactly one application position, including a same-value assignment, and updates the matching applied channels without altering operator source bytes. Production validation, serialization, repeat pruning, durable writing and publication remain in force; publication follows durability.

Retain one `fixtureThreadHybridSince(authority.snapshot())` mint across writes, initializing it from reopened state on reopen, or reuse the fixture's explicitly controlled mint. Continuing `thread_hybrid` preserves its marker, entering it mints one and leaving it removes it. `makeMembershipHarness` exposes its shared mint as `f.threadHybridSince`; see [Membership fixtures and evidence](#membership-fixtures-and-evidence) for production assignment drivers.

### Membership fixtures and evidence

`membershipPage(channels, cursor?)` accepts channel IDs or explicit page objects; ID inputs derive public/private kind and internal-sharing facts. `membershipJoin(channel, event?, overrides?)` supplies foundation observations, defaulting to a channel-derived event, app identity, positive membership and boundary zero.

`membershipObservation(authority, key, channel, member, event, observedThrough?)` takes the current lifetime boundary; a supplied observation time also supplies internal channel facts. These constructors do not establish authenticated discovery: use the real router/scanner below for that evidence.

`membershipTimestamp(offsetMs = 0)` uses `MEMBERSHIP_FIXTURE_TIME`; `membershipEventTimestamp(now = MEMBERSHIP_FIXTURE_TIME, offsetMs = 1)` places an event after the supplied fake-clock observation.

`CHANNEL_DELIVERY_TIMES` names distinct root, other-root, ordinary and mention timestamps, and `channelDeliveryEventTimestamp(sequence)` supplies distinct next-second event times. `CHANNEL_DELIVERY_EVENT_IDS` names the held, bot and failed leave events.

`channelDeliveryOriginals(channel = SHARED_CHANNEL_IDS.primary)` returns two independently keyed FIFO `slackInput` overrides, retaining byte-distinct whitespace/CRLF/emoji content and hourglass acknowledgement.

Use these with `THREAD_ROOTS` from `thread-memory.ts` for delivery/leave/rejoin chronology, as `tests/set-channel-delivery.test.ts` does; membership scan assertions select their actual channel from the named IDs or `channelPopulation`.

Use [Fixture assignments](#fixture-assignments) only for setup; a membership harness exposes its authority and retained `threadHybridSince` mint for that purpose. Real held-scan assignment evidence uses `makeReloadHarness` as described under [Reload Tests](#reload-tests), keeping the bot store, membership and scanner on `run.controller.sharedChannels()!`.

Use `makeMembershipHarness`, `membershipPage` and `MEMBERSHIP_FIXTURE_TIME` from
`tests/test-helpers/shared-channels.ts`; optional `startTime` controls reopen
chronology, `threadHybridSince` controls the mint and `failWrites(predicate)` injects persistence refusal. `unsyncWrites(predicate)` installs the exact production bytes and then reports an uncertain directory sync; reset either fault with a predicate that returns false. `onScanStatus` observes the scanner independently of connection status. Script explicit Slack
pages: configuration is never discovery evidence. `readSharedState` and
`writeSharedState` use the production parser/writer. `captured()` includes
`authorityFile: writtenFile(authority.path)` alongside parsed state, logs and
statuses; leak-check it before deleting or corrupting the file. Close managers,
scanners, engines and fake clocks, settle callbacks, and reset acknowledgement
tracking and registry state.

In `tests/channel-membership.test.ts`, each bot/operator origin writes while the production scanner is held on that same authority. Capture the original membership `boundary` and scan-start `observedRevision`, then take `assignmentOrder` from the actual applied choice; assert those exact conflict anchors, preserved unresolved choice, dropped superseded repeats and retained beginning/conflict/replacement/leave records through later reconciliations. Fixture construction does not establish this production-path coverage.

The membership suite pins two distinct optional historical records in
`SharedPersona`. `membershipInventory` has exactly `incarnation`, canonical
`identity`, `observedThrough`, `observedRevision`, `recordedOrder`; timestamp and
revision are captured at scan start, with safe integers
`1 <= observedRevision < recordedOrder <= state.revision`. Absence of the whole
field is valid for a foundation baseline; a present four-field record is not. Negative
history recovery, inferred absences and cutoff commit are one transaction;
failed/held/invalid batches cannot publish absence, while valid positives progress.

`membershipAbsenceConflicts[channel]` has exactly `identity`, `boundary`,
`observedThrough`, `observedRevision`, `assignmentOrder`, `recordedOrder`.
Identity and original positive boundary match retained membership, with safe
integers `1 <= boundary <= observedRevision < assignmentOrder < recordedOrder
<= state.revision`; the current explicit assignment order is at least the
retained order, and a join default cannot substitute for it. Missing/extra
fields, invalid channel/timestamp/identity and broken relations are rejected;
absence of the whole optional field is valid. Held first/final-page scans with
same-value or changed choices preserve the original uncertainty across absent
and present retries, live recovery and reopen. No leave/default/current authority,
unrelated negative mutation or complete cutoff is invented. Failed persistence
keeps in-run protection for idle retry; persona reset drops old-life evidence.
This record is historical uncertainty, never an operator clear action.

Complete event payload identity excludes local connection and receipt/application
order. Optional `MembershipEvidence.originalEvent` links a different valid Slack
event in the same persona to retained evidence or `membershipEvents`, only with
`state=conflict` and `conflict=contradictory-id`; older records without the link
remain valid. Foundation effects without payload cannot prove exact live retry.
